REBEL_PULSAR_TEXT: A Rebel captain appears on the screen. "I thought we had been doomed to backwater assignments. This is my chance to get back in Command's good graces! Charge the weapons!"
A small rebel research station overlooks a pulsating star. Before you can react a Rebel ship spots you and moves in to attack.
You arrive at an infrequently used beacon close to a pulsar. Before long a Rebel ship happens to jump nearby. Looks like you'll have to fight.
PIRATE_PULSAR_TEXT: Sensors go wild as a nearby pulsar is detected. While you are attempting to recalibrate the FTL drive, a pirate sneaks up on your ship, weapons charging. Prepare for a fight!

You arrive to find a pulsar dominating the view screen. You see a small silhouette pass in front of the star. Before you can ponder what it is, warning signals go off. It appears to be a ship in a firing trajectory!

A small research station orbits a nearby pulsar. It appears largely abandoned, but you detect power signatures flaring up as soon as you're in scanning distance. A small combat ship launches from the station. Pirates!
REBEL_PDS_TEXT: You're shocked to discover a Rebel forward base on this planet. A patrol ship moves in to intercept and sensors indicate an Anti-Ship Battery is about to fire. We've got to get out of here!
REBEL_AUTO_PDS_TEXT: As soon as you arrive multiple warnings go off. A hostile automated ship is detected and an Anti-Ship Battery begins firing. This doesn't look good!
GENERIC_SURRENDER_TEXT: "Alright, you win! Here's some equipment from our stores, leave us alone!"
The ship repeatedly hails you. It looks like they want to surrender.
"You are considerably more well-armed than I would have thought. We surrender."
They send you a message: "Your ship is surprisingly well equipped! Please take this and let us live."
"Please don't kill us. We will give you everything we have!"
They offer you some of their cargo if you let them live.
They offer to give you some of their goods if you don't destroy their ship.
You get a frantic message, "Take everything we have! Just don't kill us."
"You have clearly bested us. We merely request our lives."
"You have made your point, we are beaten. Take these and leave us to our shame."
"Take everything we have and let's both forget this happened."
ABANDONED_PIRATE_CIVILIAN_TEXT: You discover an abandoned mining facility in the process of being 'acquired' by pirate scavengers. However, you immediately receive a call from a civilian transport vessel, "Help! We were trying to escape only to be caught by pirates!" You see a lone pirate ship boarding the civilian craft.

A pirate ship emerges from hiding after you and another ship jump into the area. Sensors show the pirates ran a quick scan of your ship's weapon system before flying off to pursue the unarmed civilian ship.

A pirate ship is firing on the small ships docked at a refueling station. They are broadcasting on a wide band channel. You catch the captain's rant mid-speed, "...saw you trading with those damned scavengers. I'll show you what happens when you try and undercut the Red Giant gang!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LANIUS_ABANDONED: A Lanius vessel stops repurposing an abandoned satellite as soon as you jump in. It blocks all hails and powers its weapons.
You arrive to see a well-armed Lanius craft preparing to salvage a badly damaged Rebel patrol ship. Noticing your arrival, the Lanius greedily moves in to intercept its second target of the day.

The Lanius don't pick and choose when it comes to their targets. If you've got scrap, they'll gladly take it from you. Unfortunately, you've been detected by a nearby Lanius ship that swoops in to attack.
Lanius aren't exactly known for friendliness, but an unusually aggressive military vessel has locked onto your ship and is readying its weapons.

You stumble across a Lanius vessel melting down the last few remains of a heavily armed Zoltan peace-keeping fighter. Wanting to defend their latest score, they don't give you any opportunities and attack immediately.
A Lanius ship looking for easy salvage spots you and moves in to intercept.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_GHOST_ABANDONED: Ghosts love getting their hands on new ships, and usually they go for easier pickings. Despite this, the Vagabond ship here seems ready to migrate and they've chosen your ship as their target.
It's beyond you why most Ghosts choose to populate barely functional wreckage, but it seems the hostile ship here has slightly higher standards and have chosen to take yours next.

You receive a hail from a dysfunctional and heavily damaged ship, but the only audible noise is static. You attempt to respond but somehow seem to have angered the populates of the ship, a clan of Ghosts.
The range of ships you see here keeps growing, and it seems 'wreck full of mad gas beings' can be added to the list.
Ghosts aren't known for being super confrontational, but when they find a ship that piques their interest, they aren't shy to try and take it. Clearly, you've made quite the impression out here.
You nearly make the mistake of attempting to salvage the wreckage at this beacon before realizing it's populated by Ghosts, but it's already too late. They've noticed you now and move in to attack.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_ABANDONED: If there's one thing pirates like more than anything, it's scrap. Though most come here to salvage empty ships, the one here has chosen to attack you instead.
A nearby pirate ship notices you. It abandons the wreck it's currently salvaging, hoping you'll be carrying a greater bounty.
This sector has proven to be a magnet for pirates, an unfortunate fact that has led to the confrontation awaiting you at this beacon.
Few pirates can resist the temptation of a large bounty regardless of the risk, and it seems the pirate barreling towards you has given in.
It seems a pirate has found their way to this beacon already, and is eager for a fight.
Surprisingly, a pirate ship scavenging an old Militia Transport abandons its latest prey in favor of fighting you instead.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_ABANDONED: Though the fighting in this sector has long since ended, it seems a Rebel ship still lingers, and is ready to fight you.
A Rebel captain hails you: "Do you see now the cost of your war? Give up and let the Rebellion take over, it is best for everyone this way."
The Rebel ship that rests here is not willing to let you go without a fight. Prepare for battle!
You thought most of the Rebel forces had left this sector after the evacuations, but it seems a few ships remain and are just as ready for battle as ever.
"Haha! You were expecting another empty colony, but it was me all along!" The nearby Rebel ship locks onto your hull and attacks.
It seems a Rebel ship here was lying in wait, ready to ambush any Federation ships that may be passing through. A fight is inevitable.
TEXT_AUGMENTED_CHOICE: The Augmented might not always be the friendliest, but the ship here makes no move to fight you. Will you do the same?
"Am warning you avoid. My ship dangerous, you wanting not to mess with." The Lanius on the other ship sticks out his chest in pride and waves his sharp blades boastfully.
A Lanius trying to avoid conflict with a military ship isn't all too uncommon, but you've seen some particularly savage Augmented ships. Still, the vessel here makes no aggressive moves.
At first you aren't certain if the Lanius ship in front of you is still active, but scans turn back faint life signs. Not injured, just asleep. Do you wish to take advantage of this situation?
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUGMENTED: The Augmented are fearsome fighters and scavengers, even if you've met a few friendly ones too. It appears you've met one that is far less friendly, and they're looking to attack you!
It appears the drive for life-sustaining scrap has driven the nearby Augmented Lanius to madness, and they're desperate enough to attack a military vessel like yours!
You didn't think the Lanius could get any more scrap-hungry than the ones in the Swarmlands, but the Augmented have proven otherwise. Prepare for battle!
"Needing scrap. You have ship made of scrap. I eat you ship. Do not worrying, am fair. Will give you shuttle." This won't fly for as long as you are captain of this ship!
You knew the Augmented come here to feed on ancient wreckage, but you didn't know they'd go so far as to attack a ship like yours!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUGMENTED_LANIUS: This sector might be primarily run by the Augmented Lanius, but that doesn't mean it isn't possible to find regular Lanius lying in wait to prey on passing ships, such as the one here that's firing in your direction.
You might have been surprised by seeing a hostile Lanius ship here, but the Augmented have to come from somewhere, you suppose.
This ship here might be no Augmented vessel, but it is a regular Lanius, and they're as hungry for your ship as anywhere else!
You briefly hope you might be able to reason with the approaching Lanius ship, but alas it appears it's too late for words, only violence.
AUTO_FREE_ITEMS: You arrive in a system and immediately discover a pirate ship nearby. Strangely, scans indicate there are no lifeforms aboard. You salvage anything useful, but find no clue as to the whereabouts of the former crew.
Not much remains in this abandoned system; however, scans reveal a nearby mining platform with some salvageable materials.
You happen upon the remains of an automated space station. It has been mostly picked clean but there appears to be a few materials that will aid you in your mission.
TEXT_AUTO_YARD_CHOICE: You have discovered a dormant Auto-ship at this beacon. It makes no attempt to attack you, but the low power signatures from it suggest it is still functional.
An Auto-ship patrolling the sector has not yet spotted you at this beacon.
A prerecorded message plays over the intercomm. "It is advised that you do not attack this ship."
It appears it is not within the programming of the Auto-ship at this beacon to instigate combat. That doesn't mean however that it won't fight back should you choose to attack.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUTO: You discover one of the Rebel's autonomous scouts. The ship's AI wastes no time in engaging your ship.
Your ship is hailed: "This is an automated message. Resisting our takeover is pointless. Prepare to die." It appears this Rebel ship is run by an AI.
A Rebel autonomous vessel is exploring this beacon. You attempt to hide behind a nearby moon, but the ship finds you and begins its assault.
The AI of a nearby small Rebel auto-ship immediately identifies you as a threat and engages.
A Rebel ship moves in to engage. You attempt to open communications, but realize the futility of that action when you see the ship is run by an AI.
This must be one of the Rebels' unmanned scout ships. Looks like there's no way around a fight.
Another unmanned ship patrols this area. You prepare the ship for combat.
This beacon is being patrolled by an unmanned scout. A fight is unavoidable.
A small shuttle appears on the local radar. Turns out it is a Rebel automated scout!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ENGINEER: Though the primary Rebel fleet mostly avoids this sector, their Engineer vessels can still be found somewhat frequently. One of these ships has already arrived at this beacon and wastes no time to attack your ship.
You're hailed by a gruff looking Rebel engineer. "Frankly, I'm not paid enough for this job. Though at the same time, if I kill you maybe I'll get a raise!"
Only the Rebels could see the opportunity to make their engineer ships just as deadly as their primary fleet. One such ship spots you and attacks!
A Rebel Engineer ship is exploring this beacon. "Damn it, you should know very well that this sector is off limits!"

The Rebel Engineers are tasked with repairing damaged Auto-ships in this sector. That doesn't mean they aren't willing to get into a brawl with passing Federation ships. The ship here is evidence of this.
NEBULA_CLAN_FIGHT: The Exotic Hunter's Guild has many scouts patrolling this sector, alongside its usual hunters. When they spot you here, and recognize you as a Federation ship, they quickly arm themselves for battle. Their reasoning? Either they think you're a threat, or they want to make a coat out of your skin. Or both.
The silence of the nebula around you is starting to get to you. Fortunately, this beacon appears to be empt- oh wait, it appears you're mistaken. Clansmen inbound!
You catch a nearby Clansman watching you from a distance. "Well I'll be, that'ssss one fine ssset of teeth, mate! I'm gonna make a lovely necklace out of thossse!"

"An MV ssship? Didn't you get the memo? Thissss isss Guild territory! We didn't buy thisss land from the Kleptocracy jussst to have sssome freakin' interdimenssssional assshole pop in and sssteal all of our prey!"
A nearby Guild ship approaches, its weapons already charging. You have to admire the courage of these Clansmen, even if it usually ends with them dead.
"Hey, isss that a sssship over there? Oh crap, it issss!" A Clansman scrambles for his rifle then swerves his ship around to fight you!
The Clansmen are prestigious hunters who aren't known to pass up the chance for a quality hunt. While you might be a military vessel armed for combat, that doesn't seem to deter the nearby vessel.
NEBULA_SLUG_CLAN_FIGHT: Usually the Slug ships you expect to see here are property of the Guild, but sometimes standard Kleptocracy citizens make their way to this sector for a bit of hunting. And as usual, looks like you're the one being hunted!
"Federation! Thisss isss Kleptocracy ssspacce. Don't think jussst becaussse the Guild letssss in outsssidersss that you'll be welcomed by ussss!"
A Slug vessel is inbound! They might not be EHG, but they're still a hostile you need to eliminate or run from!
"You're the lasssst kill I need to passsss my memberssship exam and become a member of the Guild! Now sssstand ssstill, I'm tired of having to put effort into thisss!"
There's many Slugs in EHG space, but you didn't expect to see a standard Kleptocracy citizen. Not that you're surprised, but you are mildly displeased that they've already turned hostile!
NEBULA_SHELL_CLAN_FIGHT: You wouldn't be one to expect Shells to be so hostile, but apparently the ongoings of the Guild have really agitated the nearby ship, because they're already attacking!

Shells are normally very appreciative of science, but the ship here appears to have abandoned all reason and is attacking straight on. The Guild probably has something to do with this rash behavior, but it's too late to diagnose it now!

"You must run! My crew, thhhey have caught a rare case of space rabies from an Equinoid we recovered during a raid on a Guild stati-" The Shell is cut off as he is murdered by one of his friends, who moves to take control of the ship and attack.
INFORMATION_BROKER_RANDOM: "Apparently, the Crysssstalssss have devissssed a Mine Launcher who'sss ussse isss not considered bothersssome by the authoritiesss due to the nature of itsss projectilesss. You can find it in their capital worldssss. It doesssn't ussse ammunition either!"
"The Brood ssssometimessss holdssss sssspider racing contessstsss. While they don't allow performance enhancerssss, you might be able to gain an unfair advantage if you did ssssome genetic meddling."
"If you find it, try usssing the Panic Button. It will definitely end the fight right away!"
"That powerful merchant ssssayssss no-no wordssss ssssometimesss. It might be hard to pisssss him off enough to get him to ssssay it, though."

"My sssson issss a technical wizard, you know. Likessss to travel the universssse jusssst like hissss old man. Came up with a unique auto-pilot sssscrambler... Lassst I checked, he wassss doing bussssinessss in a Dynassssty ssssector."

"Ever been to Tony'ssss? If you take out a loan, they'll sssend a certain LaRoache who'll lurk around ssssector exitssss looking for you, to collect on your debt. Loan ssssharking is a frighteningly lucrative bussssinessss, which meansss they can afford to command a vessssel unrivaled by all but one other entrepreneur."

"Did you know that Argeonn sssssmugglessss fugitivessss out of ssssensssitive areassss? I heard one ssssuch ssssmuggler went to the heart of the Harmony. Probably hassss ssssomething to do with the Engi Brigade."

"The Harmony Linkssss are guarded for a reasssson. Ssssuppossssedly, they contain the ssssecret of a realm of unimaginable treassssure. If you don't get killed by the mysterioussss technology that protectssss them, that issss."
"The Rebelssss devote a ssssurprissssing amount of ressssources protecting a ssssector with sssseemingly no tactical value. It musssst mean a lot to ssssomeone important."

"The Black Market guard hassss ssssome valuable information aboard their sssship. If you can get onboard, you could find directionssss to valuable technology. Jusssst err on the sssside of caution if you meet any piratessss."
"The Minisssstry issss asssshamed of itssss hissstory. If you venture into their sssspace, I recommend you keep your eyessss open for their attemptssss to bury their passsst."

"One of the mosssst massssive objectssss in the galaxy issss ssssaid to be at the heart of a particularly dangeroussss nebula. It'ssss sssso dangeroussss, not even sssslugssss dare to live there! But it holdssss ssssignificance to the Zoltan Extremisssstssss for ssssome reasssson."
TEXT_COALITION_CIVILIAN: You are repeatedly hailed by a nearby civilian ship. You approach it carefully when a Coalition ship flies past, firing at the civilians!
You notice a Coalition ship assaulting a civilian transport. You receive simultaneous hails from both ships, a plea for help and a warning to stay away.
Coalition space is a dangerous place for any ship, so you are not surprised to see the unarmed civilian ship at this beacon under attack from a Coalition ship.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_COALITION: Two Coalition ships appear to be exchanging slaves at this beacon. One of them quickly jumps away after seeing you, but the other attacks!
The Coalition is made of the 4 most hostile races in the galaxy. They aren't known for ignoring a potential fight, and this ship is no exception.
You find a Coalition ship salvaging the wreck of a Federation scout. Upon seeing your ship, it immediately abandons the wreck and attacks!
You are hailed by the captain of a nearby Coalition ship shortly after arriving. "You have a lot of nerve showing up in our sector. Now you will die!"
You see a Coalition ship docked outside a nearby outpost. You order your crew to engage the ship.
The war has brought out the worst in the 4 races that make up the Coalition. The ship at this beacon clearly has no intentions of letting you go unharmed.

"Hehehe, are you lossst? Ssseemsss you wandered too far into Coalition ssspace, buddy! Heheheheheheh, gonna cry about it? Hehehehehehh..." You take this chance to arm the guns while the Slug captain continues to laugh.

The Leech captain on the nearby Coalition ship waves to you. "Sup, man. How's it goin?" He is promptly shoved to the side and replaced by the true captain, a Slug. "You ssstupid tapeworm, we're sssupposssed to fight thessse idiotsss!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_COALITION: "You're stuck in this hell too? I'm almost sympathetic, but the Federation is responsible for creating the Coalition!"
A Rebel ship, trying its best to escape from Coalition territory, has decided to take a detour and attack your ship.
The Rebels tend to avoid the Coalition as much as the Federation, but this ship appears to be an exception.
"At last, a ship not filled with alien filth. I'd much prefer to fight Federation scum!"
TEXT_NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_COALITION: The Coalition's alliance with the Slugs means many times their ships can be found crawling around nebulas. This is one such occasion.
It appears a Coalition ship is hiding in this nebula beacon. Upon spotting you they arm their weapons!
A Coalition ship exploring this nebula has found you and attacks!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_VAMPWEED: "The Federation clings to the past, but you shall find it will be your own undoing for pushing us away! When Ivar sees the truth and joins the Coalition, your hypocritical leaders will be annihilated! And until then, we'll have to make do with picking off you intrusive Universe 0 Renegades!"

Following the Federation-Mantis war, it was agreed during the Kadahellian'ek Treaty that the Gathering and Confederacy would never enter war against each other. Despite this, tensions remain high, and it seems many Vampweeds still hold history against the Federation. One particularly radical vessel nearby locks onto you!

Vampweeds might not be your friends, but it's not too typical for them to act in such aggressive manners. However, scans show the crew of the nearby ship have succumbed to some kind of parasite that creates irrational behavior. Prepare to fight!

"And so it's true, the Federation has finally sent Renegades to renew the old war! Well, we won't take this insult without a fight, scum!" Unfortunately, the ship refuses to listen to you, meaning a fight is inevitable.

A drunk Vampweed factory worker's vessel lurches towards you. "Ehhh... dumbass... Feds in my sector? You'll regret this, hear me!" Despite barely being able to form a coherent sentence, the captain is able to order his crew to attack!

Vampweeds are known to drink a fair bit as a culture, and intoxicated Orchids aren't an uncommon sight here. Unfortunately, the side effects of heavy drinking tend to cause irrational decisions, such as engaging Renegades in combat!
"I didn't side with the Hive during the old war, but now? Now I think I should have! The Federation has done nothing but push us away when we needed it most, and you're going to regret that!"

"Ivar has grown weak in trying to defend you Federation filth! It is time for insurrection, time to plant the seeds of rebellion so that it may flower into a galaxy where your lies no longer corrupt our youth!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_COALITION_VAMPWEED: "The Federation had its chance over a century ago, but still you cling to this galaxy as if you really represent anything but a dying age! Your stake at the Confederacy is long past nullified, so you might as well roll over dead and allow the inevitable to happen!" Seemingly hoping to make rolling over dead more than a metaphor, the Coalition vessel attacks!

Unfortunately, in light of the Federation's reluctance to welcome the Vampweeds, a large number of Confederate nationalists have taken it personally and are pushing to join the Coalition instead. This has resulted in an influx of Coalition vessels in their territory - not a good thing for you!

"You claim to represent peace and prosperity, yet where were you when the Confederacy came knocking? When your so called 'mission of unification' really came to the test, the whole galaxy got to see exactly why the Federation must fall. Your claim to this reality, U0 scum, is nullified in the wake of the Coalition! You will be eradicated!"

The Slug captain of the nearby Coalition vessel hails you, barely holding onto consciousness. "Thessse... Vampweedssss know their way around alcohol, hah! Oh I'm going to... *hiccup* regret thissss in the morning..." A morning he may never see, because as soon as he registers you're a Renegade he decides to open fire!

"In old war, I fight on behalf of Hive and gain brotherhood with Confederacy. While those days over, the brotherhood never dies! Whether it is the alliance of past or Coalition of future, we will strike Federation scum down!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LEECH_VAMPWEED: "The Republic will rise again! And the Coalition will be the one to do it! Yeah... probably! I actually don't have much confidence in this, but I was told yelling would make you sound sure of yourself! Now I'm embarrassed and I'm going to fight you anyways! I will regret this!"

The Confederacy has for a while now been playing a part in aiding the revolutionaries against Tyrdeo in the Eargen Republic. All of this, confusingly, has been going on meanwhile as a significant percentage of the Confederacy has been pushing to join the Coalition - of which the Republic is a founding member. This confusing jumble of politics has left many to wonder who is on who's side - such as the lost Leech vessel nearby who's weapons lock onto you out of instinct as soon as you approach!

"You should have taken the chance to welcome the Confederacy while you could, Federation scum! Now you stand even weaker in the face of the Coalition! We'll pave over you and build a new galaxy free of your tyranny!"

It seems everyone universally enjoys the sweet mixtures of Vampweed alcohol - or at least particularly violent drunks do. A Republic captain, having just finished raiding a Confederate bar, orders an attack on your vessel admist a drunken stupor.

A vessel from the Eargen Republic is making back and forth patrols of the area, weapons still charged from some prior encounter, likely with the Confederate military. When they spot you, they lock on and attack!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MANTIS_VAMPWEED: "I mark your vessel rightfully property of mine, for entering Krakiiil hunting ground! I will chop out bloated liver and sell to plant as scientific curiosity!"

The Hive and the Confederacy aided each other back in the days of the Federation-Mantis war. Though that alliance has since fallen apart, the Confederacy has retained some archaic open border laws allowing Mantis hunters into their territory - as long as it's ships like yours they're hunting, and not their own.
"Do you smell that? It is the scent of murder on horizon. Your corpse will making fine decoration for my vessel, as reminder for how old war should have ended!"

"Renegade, I slaughter you like I slaughter Federation back in days of old war! It is nothing personal, really. I am just missing those days of red blood running in trenches. And also, I don't like you."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_VAMPWEED: "The Confederacy has put countless millions of honest Unionists out of business, outcompeting them with their unsanitary and inhumane working conditions in their sweatshop factories! Yet you, Federation scum, you would rather 'keep the peace' and allow this kind of conduct to continue! It's despicable!"

The Confederacy has drawn the ire of quite a few humans, who see the raw industrial power of the Vampweeds as a threat to the Union's dominance on galactic manufacturing. Of course, the Rebels have taken this to the extreme and are now making unprovoked attacks on Confederate space!

"If I had a penny for every time I've run into a Renegade in some random backwater alien sector, I'd have... well, I'd have one penny because this is the first time it's happened. But it keeps happening to my friends too, so it's still kind of a weird coincidence."

"The Union opened its arms to the galaxy, and offered an honest chance to any xeno willing to take it! And how were we repaid? The Confederacy spat in our hand and built its own industrial empire with half the moral fiber! They call themselves capitalists, but they're nothing more than a money farming parasite!" The Rebel spits on the ground and decides to take out his frustration on you.
TEXT_FINISH_BEACON_DROPPOINT_ENCOUNTER: "Blegh, you're the ship we traveled all the way from Universe 1 to meet? I thought they said you were a THREAT." Looks like you'll have to show these guys not to underestimate you.
"Looks like you've stumbled into my.... AMBUSH! Nyeh heh heh! Heh. Heh... Die." The Rebel ship moves in to attack.
"Your mistake for coming here, bucko. End of the line!" It's the end of the line for someone, but let's hope it's not you!
The Rebel captain says nothing, but imitates a pair of guns with his fingers and draws a line across his throat. When did the Rebels get so childish?
The Rebel captain breaks into laughter upon seeing your ship. You won't take this insult lightly. Not like you have a choice, since their weapons are already firing!
QUEST_ESCORT_TEXT: After a short time you receive a message, "Hello. I hope it's not a bother, but I'm looking for an escort to a nearby system. This region is quite dangerous and our ship is not well-armed."
There is a single ship at this beacon. They hail you, "We could really use some help. Our FTL navigation system is shot. Can you help us get to a nearby station where they can patch us up?"
"Hello," your communicator opens a hail from a nearby ship. "Our weapon systems are malfunctioning and we're too afraid of pirates to travel home unassisted. Can you escort us?"
After a short time you receive a message, "Hello. I hope it's not a bother, but I'm looking for an escort to a nearby system. This region is quite dangerous and our ship is not well-armed."
There is a single ship at this beacon. They hail you, "We could really use some help. Our FTL navigation system is shot. Can you help us get to a nearby station where they can patch us up?"
"Hello," your communicator opens a hail from a nearby ship. "Our weapon systems are malfunctioning and we're too afraid of pirates to travel home unassisted. Can you escort us?"
TRAP_BEACON_TEXT: You arrive at the beacon and immediately detect a pirate ship. It seems this distress beacon was a trap!
"Haha! I knew someone would fall into our dastardly trap!" It appears this distress beacon was nothing but a decoy for a pirate ambush.
Your cockpit lights up with warning signals. You are being targeted by a nearby ship. The distress call was a lure to attract unwitting ships into weapons range. You prepare for a fight.
As soon as you arrive at the distress signal, shots are fired toward your ship. A trap!
You arrive at the beacon and immediately detect a pirate ship. It seems this distress beacon was a trap!
"Haha! I knew someone would fall into our dastardly trap!" It appears this distress beacon was nothing but a decoy for a pirate ambush.
Your cockpit lights up with warning signals. You are being targeted by a nearby ship. The distress call was a lure to attract unwitting ships into weapons range. You prepare for a fight.
As soon as you arrive at the distress signal, shots are fired toward your ship. A trap!
TEXT_DROPPOINT_SUPPLY_DEPOT: You have arrived at a Federation supply depot for Multiverse Renegades. These were established across various realities deemed prominent for protection.
This beacon serves as a temporary outpost for Multiverse-drive equipped vessels, established and maintained by the Federation.
You're not surprised to see this beacon has been outfitted with a Multiverse supply depot. Many such beacons were constructed by prior Multiverse Renegades to help prepare ships such as yours.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_DUSKBRINGER: The Duskbringers are more extreme than the regular Zoltans, if that was even possible. Usually, they prefer to kill on sight, and the ship here attempts to do the same.
Duskbringers blame the Federation in particular for the Rebellion's uprising. There is already a Duskbringer ship here, and they intend to repay the favor.
There are many ways to describe the Duskbringers. One such way might be overly agressive space nazis, but you don't have time to fathom more before a ship is attacking!
A Duskbringer ship is approaching at high speeds. Arm the weapons!
Duskbringer patrols often scout out the sector to ward off unwanted visitors. One of these patrols has spotted you and moves in to attack.

"Greedy, corrupt Renegade pig! Your presence here violates code protocol-R78-T! Prepare to be erased!" You suspect their fury is due to more than a simple protocol violation, but you have no choice but to fight.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_DUSKBRINGER_STATION: "Unidentified ship, this system is off-limits for- ah crap, Feds!" The nearby Duskbringer station activates their arsenal, ready to attack.
The Duskbringers are surprisingly even more cautious of protecting their borders than the Zoltans. A station built here to ward off ships like yours spots you, and a fight is inevitable.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_DUSKBRINGER: A smug Rebel captain hails you. "Do you need further proof that your Federation is corrupt, when your existence doesn't fuel just one, but two Rebellions?"

The Rebels and Duskbringers have a strange relationship. Though it would be a lie to say they like each other, the two have a weak bond over their hatred of the Federation. The Rebel ship at this beacon wastes no time proving that this hatred has yet to die down.
Though this is not their territory, Rebel forces are not all too uncommon in Duskbringer sectors. It appears you have encountered one of their ships.
"Blegh, can't say I'm a fan of these Zoltan idiots either. Buncha' mini space-nazis or something. Anyways, time to die!"

You're hailed by the Rebel ship at this beacon. "Well, aren't you just so brave, coming here? I wondered if I would see you here, considering how much you love killing your enemies. Funny, because I just happen to love doing the exact same thing!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_DUSKBRINGER: A pirate hiding from the Duskbringers already occupies this beacon. They seem confident in taking on your ship, and attack!

You pick up a frequency between two pirate ships. "Yeah, these damn Zoltan bastards -- no, everything is still going as planned -- ah crap, Federation!" It appears they've noticed you. One of the ships escapes, but the other attacks!

Despite trying desperately to keep pirate forces at bay, there's a considerable amount of underground black markets and slave trades held in Duskbringer sectors. Why the pirates do this, whether to rub their superiority in the Zoltans' faces or some other ulterior motive doesn't matter, because one such ship is barreling down on you!
"A Fed? In this sector? How curious. You should have stayed away, amigo. You might think the Dusks are the biggest threat here, but you're wrong. We pirates own this sector!"
"Damn it, Federation too? Why can't we just catch a break!" The pirates at this beacon don't seem pleased at your presence. Prepare for battle.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_DUSKBRINGER_CAPITOL: The Rebel invasion of this sector is bad news for not just the Duskbringers, but you as well. A Rebel forward scout locks onto your location and attacks.
"Well, ain't this a nice turn of events. I expected to be stuck fighting Zoltans this entire invasion, but now a Fed shows up? My lucky day!"
A Rebel thirsting for blood is a threat you'd like to avoid, but unfortunately this encounter hasn't given you an option. A hostile Rebel ship approaches!
A smug Rebel captain hails you. "Do you need further proof that your Federation is corrupt, when your existence doesn't fuel just one, but two Rebellions?"
"Blegh, can't say I'm a fan of these Zoltan idiots either. Buncha' mini space-nazis or something. Anyways, time to die!"

You're hailed by the Rebel ship at this beacon. "Well, aren't you just so brave, coming here? I wondered if I would see you here, considering how much you love killing your enemies. Funny, because I just happen to love doing the exact same thing!"
NEBULA_DYNASTY_FIGHT: It's strange how aggressive the Dynasty is, especially when the breakaway Vagabond Ghosts are much more reclusive. Though, perhaps that may be why they broke away in the first place. You'll have to think about this later, as a Dynasty vessel is inbound!
Make no mistake, the ship coming at you isn't friendly. A Dynasty vessel lurches forward, eyeing your weapons before attacking!
A garbled message comes across your radio. "Weapons. They belong to me. GIVE!" A Dynasty ship uncloaks nearby, weapons drawn!
For such an elegant name as the Spectral Dynasty, their ships are uncharacteristically hostile and violent. There's no better example than the vessel here, as it approaches menacingly.
A shot flies right past your ship, and seconds later a purple vessel comes drifting out of the clouds. Looks like it's Ghosts... and they don't look friendly!

A bloodchilling scream fills your speakers, followed by unsettling static. Any captain with lesser nerves might have fainted on the spot, but you know better. This isn't some demon, this is a much more real threat. A Dynasty vessel approaches!

Looks like you're receiving a short range broadcast. "Your flesh shall appease the demon's heart one more day. Your weapons shall be its destruction! For the good of the Dynasty!" A Ghost vessel appears nearby, weapons drawn and already firing!

An unsettling chant echoes through the nebula as a ship approaches. "The demon's heart shall cease! The demon's heart shall cease!", followed by the flashing of gunfire as a Dynasty vessel draws near. Are you the demon? You aren't sure, but you won't have time to ask!

In light of the seemingly empty nebula, you make conversation with the crew on enemies you could have found here instead. As soon as one of them mentions the Dynasty, a ship comes barreling out of the nebula, as if it were summoned. Speak of the devil...

At first you assume the static over the radio to be nonsense, but suddenly your translator starts to pick up words! "A breather! In Dynasty space, how putrid. It turns my insides into coils of anger. I will unleash hell on you scum!"
NEBULA_VAGABOND_DYNASTY_FIGHT: The Vagabonds usually just avoid Dynasty space, not worth the risk. This ship must be desperate - desperate enough to attack you!
Looks like you aren't safe from the scrap hungry Vagabonds, even in Dynasty space where they try to so hard to repel them. Prepare for combat.
You notice a Vagabond ship nearby watching you hungrily. "In my heart I feel the desire of a new vessel... this one is depreciated and has failed its function..." The Ghosts attack!

A Vagabond, likely fleeing from Dynasty patrols, has stumbled right into you. "You side with the Dynasty, nay? Oh, for what am I asking. The risk is not worth it, I shall simply remove you from my path."
NEBULA_ENGINEER_DYNASTY_FIGHT: Usually the Rebel ships you'd expect to see here are Autos, but it's not surprising to see an Engineer here either. Unfortunately, they're no less friendly either!
"You've just come here to make my damn job harder, haven't you? Piss off!" A particularly agitated Engineer vessel swerves to attack you!
After a long day working on the always damaged Auto-ships they construct, it's no wonder the Engineers feel the need to let off some steam. Alas, it looks like you're their next target!
"Oh come on! I haven't even finished my lunch break! You picked the wrong time to ruin my day, asshole!" Hostiles inbound!
Could it be? A Rebel ship? Your eyes aren't lying to you - and this is no ordinary Rebel. It's an Engineer, but they're no less deadly!
NEBULA_AUTO_DYNASTY_FIGHT: The Dynasty has been waging 'war' against the Auto-ships for a long time now. How the Rebels are able to afford such a massive stream of ships - or why Vance approved it - is a mystery to you, but it's only a hopefully minor inconvenience to you.
"You are not father. Father is not as ugly as you. Entering combat mode." The nearby Rebel Auto-ship suddenly activates and attacks!

You assume this to be an empty beacon... until you notice the dozens of dormant Auto-ships floating through the nebulas. You try to avoid them, but unfortunately it looks like one of them has noticed you and attacks!
You practically bump hulls with a Rebel Auto-ship, but it's too late to slip away before it's already noticed you and started to attack!
Curse the Rebels and their massive fleet of Auto-ships at constant disposal. Looks like you have another ship to take care of before you can carry on.
The Dynasty will probably be pleased to hear of your path of destruction through all of the Auto-ships you see. But before you can brag, you have another ship to add to your kill count.
NEBULA_DYNASTY_HOSTAGE: "OooooOoOh, so you've come to interfere? A royally immense pain in the end the Federation is proving to be!" An agitated Dynasty vessel attacks as soon as you enter. Behind them is an unidentified ship they must have been interrogating before this!

The Dynasty normally doesn't take prisoners, but it seems they haven't gotten the desired reaction from the unidentified ship behind them, as you can hear the agitation in the shouting Ghost captain's voice. As soon as you enter the system however, his concentration focuses on you!
Looks like two ships are here - one of unidentified origin, and the other Dynasty. The Dynasty ship doesn't seem to want you around, because they attack almost immediately!
TEXT_DYNASTY_OUTPOST: The Dynasty seems to appreciate keeping a very close watch over potential threats... so close in fact, that they've set up a forward station all the way out here. Maybe it contains data worth something to you?
You've seen few factions as overly paranoid as the Dynasty. A full blown outpost has been established here, and scans show it has data. Valuable data.

For what reason is this beacon marked as important? As soon as you jump in, it's clear. A Dynasty outpost has been established here, and the beacon marker was a warning for ships to stay away. Somehow they haven't spotted you, yet...

Looks like a broadcast in many different languages is being sent out from a nearby Dynasty outpost. It's right to the point: "This observation location is not to be tampered with. Attempts to raid or damage Dynasty property will be met with lethal force."
At first you assume your eyes are deceiving you, but nay. This is a Dynasty outpost, quite bravely posted so far out from Dynasty space.
TEXT_FREE_CRYSTAL: You notice the barebones wreckage of a nearby Crystalline vessel; though little scrap matter remains, it appears the scavengers overlooked a single Crystal weapon!
A small Crystalline trader with a squeaky high-pitched voice hails you. "Foreigners! It is important we make peace with barbaric aliens, perhaps this free weapon of war will soothe you?"

A Crystalline trading outpost hails you, requesting a trade. You look through your supply count until you realise their offer is a sample of foreign rocks in return for a military grade weapon... an offer you take in a heartbeat.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_CRYSTAL: You arrive near a fleet of Crystal ships, civilian or mercantile from the looks of them. You pause to scan one but they react immediately and send an escort to fight you off. Prepare to engage!

You arrive at the Beacon and are immediately greeted by an automatic message or warning of some kind. The translator can't seem to discern its purpose but after a few short moments an alarm goes off and a hostile ship jumps in!
You receive a message, "Hah. It looks like another worthless alien-filled craft. Prepare to meet your maker!" Weapon locks detected.
A Crystalline ship messages you, "I have not yet seen an Alien ship of such caliber as yours! As a warrior I demand to test my skills against you!" Before you can respond they move in to attack.

You arrive in a busy sector. At first no one pays any mind to your foreign ship but soon you're registering a number of scan signatures. You get the feeling you're not wanted here just seconds before registering enemy weapon locks!

You jump next to a node busy with traffic, but before long all nearby ships notice you and keep their distance, uncertain of your allegiance. After an awkward standoff, a military ship breaks away from the rest and charges you.

A barrage of rasps and clicks is broadcast over the comm; the universal translator understands little, but the words 'aliens', 'allowed' and 'no' come through quite clearly. You'll have to prove your right to be here in combat!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_CRYSTAL: You see a Rebel ship approaching. "Ack, I can't tell if this sector is any worse than the time we were stationed in that Slug hellhole. Maybe if we kill you, we can finally be stationed somewhere nice!"
The Rebels haven't been pleased with the return of yet another alien race. A particularly agitated Rebel ship wastes no time locking onto you and attacking!
A Rebel ship, hot on your tail, approaches. Its weapons are armed and there's no doubt a fight is about to ensue.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROCK_CRYSTAL: A Rock fanatic, here to watch and study the Crystals, notices you. Thinking you've come to harm its idols, it attacks.
"You are not welcome here! This sector has been chosen by the gods, and you are intruding! We are their divine prophets, and we will remove you!"
A group of egotistical Rockmen hail you, claiming they have been chosen by the Crystals to destroy your ship.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_COALITION_CRYSTAL: It appears you've had the misfortune of running into a Coalition ship travelling through this territory. They spot you almost immediately and attack!
A Coalition vessel is salvaging the remains of a nearby Crystal station. However, upon spotting you they quickly undock and attack!
TEXT_NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_CRYSTAL: It seems the Crystalline people have adjusted well to the nebulas found throughout the galaxy. A hunter hiding in the depths of the clouds here descends, weapons ready!
It makes sense for the Crystals, lovers of solitude, to take refuge deep in the nebulous clouds. A ship here, unhappy that you've disturbed them, attacks!
You spot a Crystalline vessel sneaking through the nebula. "Gah, I came here to escape you aliens! Now you chase us down?" It seems conflict is inevitable.
You aren't alone in this nebula. A Crystalline vessel approaches, ready to attack.
TEXT_FED_REBEL_CHOICE: A Rebel ship is making minor repairs at this beacon, likely repairing the damage they took charging past the Federation's borders. They will probably leave you alone if you do not engage them.
A nearby Rebel gives you a wide berth. They're looking to damage Federation supply lines, not pick a fight with a Renegade.
Some Rebels break through the outer defenses of the sector. This one is avoiding you, likely not wanting to endanger its mission.
The Rebel fleet that is chasing you through this sector might not be focusing all their attention on you. This ship seems preoccupied.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MANTIS_FREEMANTIS: Two Mantis ships, one belonging to the Hive and the other to the Free Mantis duel nearby, and the Hive Mantis emerges victorious. Driven by bloodlust, they target you next.

The Mantis Hive does not appreciate the Free Mantis attempts at separating themselves, and rogue Mantis hunters often go out to hunt them down. The one at this beacon seems to be willing to settle with you as their target.
The views of the Mantis Hive and Free Mantis are polar opposites, and so are their opinions of the Federation. The Hive Mantis here are eager to take you down.
This beacon is abandoned by the Free Mantis, and for good reason. A Mantis hunter, waiting for its next prey, catches you and moves in to attack.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_FREEMANTIS: The Zoltans have recently begun a much more concentrated attack on Free Mantis territory, and unfortunately sometimes ships get caught in the crossfire. This time, it appears you're one of them!
It's not usual for Zoltan ships to go out of their way to attack Federation ships they should be allied with, but an irate Zoltan captain nearby seems to think you're a threat and attacks!

"The Federation knows the Free Mantis have been a constant issue for the Ministry, and yet you chose to do nothing about it! I might not have direct orders, but no one will mind if you go missing after this conflict!"

The Zoltans seem to blame the Federation to some extent for the Free Mantis that have been "stealing" their territory. The ship at this beacon seems to have taken that to the next degree, because now they're attacking!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_FREEMANTIS: Amongst the many wrecks of what was once a Free Mantis clan are three Rebel ships, their guns blazing. One of them spots you and attacks!
You receive a hail not long after jumping. "At last! I thought our detour into this forsaken sector would be the death of us, but now that you're here, things are starting to look up!"
Blaster fire batters your defenses, and a Rebel ship moves in to attack!

The captain of the Rebel ship approaching you hails, "Do you know what trouble you've caused, creating these murderous psychopaths? Worse than the Hive Mantis, I can tell you that. Consider your deaths my revenge for the crew I've lost to your fanatics."
The Free Mantis have actively been searching out and killing Rebels in their territory, but the one here appears to have escaped from their grasp. They're quite eager to engage you!
ORCHID_FREE_ITEMS: A friendly Gathering station at the beacon is offering scrap metal for free. Using sign language, they message you. "Military vessel? You can have our excess scrap. We're in the transition to using titanwood instead."
MAYEB_CHILDREN_1: "Sit down and listen to me. Those are our children you're threatening. I'm not just going to stand by and do nothing. Surely you didn't think that I - a flower defined by her desire to protect the helpless - would just let you get away with bringing harm to helpless sprouts, even if they weren't sapient."

"I am not going to back down here, so you'd better listen good, Captain. These children deserve to have a long and healthy healthy life, as any child does in this multiverse. Sapient children often have a long period of time in which they are vulnerable in order to properly form their mental faculties, and Orchids are no exception. That you would prey upon something which is so helpless speaks to your callous disregard for life."

"Who do you think you are, that you can waltz in and order the deaths of children? Not only have they done nothing to hurt you, they wouldn't even be capable of trying. They're children, for Rt'Lak's sake. There's nothing that their deaths could possibly serve - haven't we got more important things to be doing anyway?"
MAYEB_CHILDREN_2: "Shut up. I'm not done yet. Were you not a child, Captain? Do you not understand the fragility and volatility of youth? Do you not witness the long term scars that people bear from childhood? It's not simply a matter of prioritization of the needs of the youth over the needs of the elder, those wounds of childhood are so much more potent. Is that something you want on your conscience?"

"SHUSH! I'm still talking. Is it that you don't respect us, or that you don't respect people who are younger than you in general? Is this perhaps a species thing, or are you incapable of empathy for those who are less developed than you? I'm genuinely curious - if these looked like little human sprouts, would that stay your heartless amusement?"

"Zip it, chowderhead! You purport to be a savior of the Federation. Well, start acting like one! No monster who commands the deaths of children could ever be worthy of saving anyone. Commit whatever garden variety war atrocities you want, but I insist that you leave the children out of it!"
MAYEB_CHILDREN_3: "You must be a very sick person to even consider something so vile, so cruel, so heartless. No, I'm not saying you are irredeemably so, but you must take proper stock of yourself if you are ever to settle down after your adventures through the multiverse. Or... have your forsaken your humanity in this vocation, that you plan to die in the stars, never giving a damn about any who do not serve to benefit you?"

"You still have the opportunity to do the right thing here. The vile act has not been committed yet. These children can still live a long and fruitful life free of the cruel machinations of a multiversal vagabond. Turn off your weapons and we can all move along and... well, I won't forget this, but I'll let it slide."

"You might be an accomplished Captain. You might be capable of facing off with the most dangerous threats in all of reality. Or you might not. It doesn't matter to me. I will advocate for these children until my dying breath, so you turn this ship around and get back to doing your job."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_ORCHID: The Gathering has been ramping up internal security heavily in recent history, but still pirates always manage to slip through the cracks. Get ready for battle!
Gathering sectors are known hotspots for wealthy Zoltan and Rock traders. Of course, such abundant wealth serves as a honeypot for the flocks of pirates looking to scavenge a pretty penny.

"Honestly captain, I'm no pirate. I'm a warrior for the free market!" A pirate captain smiles smugly at you. "Just... a very, very free market. These flower communards though? They don't know a single thing about how money works! I'm doing you all a favor by cleaning them out. Unfortunately, you're in my way. Gotta get you out of it."

"I'm sick of these plants! They're boring! I go to a tavern looking for a good time and instead I just find a bunch of monks throwing me hand signals! God, it's driving me mad! Mad enough to kill someone!" The pirate blinks when he notices you nearby. "Hey... speaking of someone to kill!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROCK_ORCHID: The Theocracy will make allies with any nation willing to accept the Chrysolic faith within their borders. The Gathering has been very receptive to this faith, and unfortunately a heavy flow of Theocracy ships that aren't quite so friendly to you keep finding their way here!

"You know nothing of faith, Renegade! Look around you and witness the holy alliance of sillicon and leaves! When the Federation crumbles, the Gathering will not mourn your death, instead they will join us in holy matrimony! Tremble before my crusading might as I vanquish your evil from this place!"

The first contact between the Florals and the Theocracy happened many centuries ago, but it was the beginning of the Gathering's interstellar colonization projects. Ever since, relations between them and the Theocracy have been very solid. As solid, perhaps, as the hull of the irate Rock vessel barreling towards you.
A babbling Rock captain, drunk on Floral-made beer and perhaps some narcotics too, starts shouting insults at you and raises his weapons to attack!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_ORCHID: A Rebel vessel approaches cautiously, trying to figure out your purpose here. "This sector belongs to the Rebellion, and always has! The Federation will respect our claim to the lands of all inferior species or we will annihilate you like we should have during the Civil War!"

"You know the thing I like about the Orchids, captain?" A Rebel captain takes a whiff of his cigar and frowns at you. "They don't scream when I kill them. Makes it easy to give the orders to shoot, 'cause I know my men don't have it in them to mow down pleading civilian families when they can hear them. You on the other hand... no matter how much you plead, nothing's going to stop us from painting the walls red with your blood."

"Glory to the Rebellion! Your choice in defending these communist flowers betrays your claims of representing a prosperous galaxy! There is nothing prosperous to be found here!" The Rebel ship's weapons lock onto your hull and conflict becomes unavoidable.
A Rebel vessel, likely sent here to take advantage of the usually non-violent Florals, has identified you as a Federation-hired Renegade and is firing! You have no choice but to defend yourself.
CLAN_FIGHT: You've discovered a Guild ship resting outside of the nebula. However, as soon as they spot you they abandon their rest and attack immediately.
You notice several Slug Clansmen planning out their attack on a Shell colony when they notice you eavesdropping, prompting them to retaliate!
NEBULA_SHELL_MILITARY_FIGHT: The Shell Military district is in shambles, and their workforce on strike. Still, those most loyal to the Geniocracy remain behind to protect their people. Protect them from who? You, apparently.

"Military vessels are not allowed thhhis close to civilian districts! Federation or not, you will leave at once!" You try to explain your FTL drive isn't charged yet, but the Shells won't listen and get agitated, then attack!

"Unauthhhorized non-Shell personnel have been identified on your vessel. Under orders of Director and Standing-President Nerva, Federation officials are not allowed in Geniocracy territory. You will be removed."
A Shell militant vessel has locked onto your vessel. You wonder if they're going to stop and scan you, but they instantly open fire! So much for Shell space being friendly!
NEBULA_CLAN_SHELL_FIGHT: It appears you've run into one of the dangerous members of the Exotic Hunter's Guild. These Slug hunters tend to hunt Shells for their armor, but they aren't above hunting other ships as well!
"Hope you undersssstand it's nothin' persssonal kid, but your head would look mighty fine on my trophy wall!" A Slug clansman and his ship approach, weapons ready.
From out of the nebula comes a Slug hunter, baring their weapons straight at you!
You start to get the sinking feeling that you're being followed. You spin the ship around to face your pursuer, to see a Slug Clansman heading straight for you!
"Ah, look at that one. Sssssurely he'sss got sssomething worth bringing back to the Guild!" A nearby Slug vessel moves in to attack.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_HACKER_DISTRESS: Despite the distress beacon being encoded as a Civilian signal, the source of the signal was a Hacker ship, lying in wait for someone to fall into their trap!
The original source of this distress beacon is gone, now replaced by a hostile Hacker vessel!
"Ahhh, you would not believe how eassssy it isss to trick people like you. We didn't even have to hack anything, we jusssst turned on our dissstresssss beacon and waited!"
The hacker ship at this beacon makes it clear that the distress beacon was merely a trap!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_HACKER: "You made your lassst missstake coming here, Federation sssship. Thisss isss our sssssector now!"
A hacker ship tails you far from behind as you explore this beacon. As they slowly inch closer, it's apparent that they're looking for a fight.
"Oh goodnesssss, we are blesssed to be in the pressence of a Federation vesssel!" Before you can respond back, the hackers interject, "Jussssst kidding! Prepare to die."
You detect a foreign signal on your computer. While in the process of discerning its origin, a hacker ship jumps out and attacks!
The Hackers have taken control of this sector, and they aren't keen on letting others in. The ship here prepares to defend its claim over this territory.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_HACKER_PIRATE: This sector may be under the control of the Hacker clan, but that doesn't mean it doesn't have pirates swarming around as well. A pirate ship at this beacon spots you and attacks.
A pirate ship, idly exploring this sector, spots you and wastes no time in attacking.
Hackers aren't the only pirates who can be found in this sector. The hostile ship at this beacon is evidence of this.
ENGI_GIFT: An Engi vessel hails you. "Identity: Federation? Outlier probability. Implies... revival. Implies... hope. Assistance suggested." They offer some supplies.
You cross paths with an Engi cargo vessel hurrying home before the Mantis fleets attempt to take over this sector. They're happy to offload some of their cargo to get home faster.
You make contact with an isolated Engi science station who are staying put despite the likelihood of Mantis invasion. They suggest you trial some experimental technology.
This was the site of a recent battle. Either a show of Mantis force, or the Engi here weren't disposed to go peacefully. You pick through the pieces.
HARMONY_SEARCH_INTRO: "This = Harmony Investigation Unit. Task requirements: means to conduct necessary sector safety measures. These means: 100% access to your ship."
"Stand down. You = suspected of harboring fugitives. We offer: the opportunity to dismiss claims. You must: allow [complete] access to your ship."
"Your vessel != cleared. Sudo: allow Harmony Engi aboard." The Engi ship waits, expectantly.
"You = in danger. Likelihood that dangerous fugitives = using your ship: 70%. Grant this ship access or risk destruction."
HARMONY_SEARCH_ATTACK: "Fugitive detected. Violent action = justified." The Engi ship attacks yours without hesitation.
"Your destruction will increase the Harmony prosperity index by 0.03%. Do not resist." The Harmony has sent a patrol after you!
"Optimal Harmony safety requires your destruction." The Engi are intent on destroying you, likely due to your reputation.
"Your survival is an obstacle to Harmony efficiency. This is unacceptable." Perhaps the Harmony has taken issue with your recent actions.
ENGI_IMPLANT_UNION_SAVED: "I can't tell you how thankful I am that you intervened. Maybe the Federation isn't so bad after all." The civilian offers an augment for your trouble.

"I swear I wasn't going to join the Rebellion. I just want the freedom to express that I don't think the Federation is doing right by the human race, okay? Anyway, thanks for saving us." You're presented with an augment as the civilians hastily clarify their stance.
"The Harmony can't take any criticism, I swear. We're getting out of this sector as fast as possible. Thanks for the assist." The civilian sends you an augment for your time.
ENGI_MANTIS_FIGHT_MV: A mixed radar signal turns out to be a Mantis attack ship scavenging the remains of an Engi carrier. They turn and fight.
You come across a Mantis raider taking pot shots at a defenseless Engi supply station. Discovering its weapons aren't much of a match for the station's armour, it turns on your ship. Battle stations!
The area looks clear, and you prepare to jump off, but a Mantis scout jumps in behind you! They're as surprised as you are, but their weapons are already online.
You find a Mantis ship harrying a small squad of Engi. They make it to the node and jump off, leaving you toe to toe with their pursuer!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ENGI_HARMONY: You're hailed by an Engi ship, their crew as close to mad as they can be. "This sector is restricted. Access to beacon denied."
Ever since the rise of the Rebellion and the increase in Mantis invasions, the Engi have placed this sector under quarantine. An Engi ship, intent on protecting this beacon, spots you and attacks.
As you learnt from the guard, this sector is restricted from public access. Unfortunately, there appears to be an Engi ship here set on enforcing this rule.
TEXT_TURZIL_REINFORCEMENTS: An Elite Engi ship moves in to attack. If you had to guess, you'd assume these were the reinforcements sent by the Harmony to hunt down the fugitive!
"Cease movement. You are wanted by Harmony for transporting and protecting fugitive." An elite Engi ship attacks!
The Elite Engi ship at this beacon looks out of place. You receive a short message about the fugitive you're protecting and the ship moves in to attack.
"You are wanted by the Harmony for: harboring fugitive. Deactivate your weapons and surrender." An Engi Elite approaches, but you have no intentions of giving up.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_HEKTAR: As you're starting to notice, the most prominent trait of all Hektar employees is their extreme greed. One particularly greedy Slug nearby looks to be wanting a piece of your ship and attacks!
A Hektar ship approaches, weighing their odds of success against you. Apparently they rank them high, because the ship attacks!
"Let'sss both be real. You're never going to pay off that debt of yoursss. Sssso, why not jussst let usss kill you and sssteal your ssstuff, and then your sssuffering can be over!"
A Hektar ship is nearby. Their captain hails you, waving cheerfully. Suddenly, a timer goes off. "Ah crap, my break issss over. Sssorry man, now I gotta do my job and rob you."
"Did you know I get a bonussss for every sssship I rob? Not from Hektar, but from money I get ssselling your garbage. Now, give me your cargo!"
MANTIS_FIGHT_CHOICE: You're greeted by a rare sight: a Mantis ship that appears not to have noticed you.
For once, you see the Mantis before they see you.
When they see the Mantis warship waiting in ambush at your intended coordinates, your crew is relieved to note you've jumped someway off the mark.
You overhear Mantis comm chatter: "Negative, I kill more humans!" You gulp noticeably, but luckily they don't see you yet.
You overhear Mantis comm chatter: "One on the right starting to rot. Take him down. Take off fingers. Put out of airlock." They certainly don't seem to be friendly...
You overhear Mantis comm chatter: "Agreed. Next ship your turn. Good hunting." They don't see you yet.
MANTIS_CIVILIAN: A Mantis vessel flashes past your view-screen, weapons and engines at full. A tiny blip on the sensor readout marks its quarry.
You spot a Mantis ship hunting in the distance.
A Mantis ship engaging a civilian hails you. Sparks fly about his cockpit as he yells, "Stay out this human! Else you next!"
Local sensors pick up two ships engaged in a heated battle. It seems the Mantis military ship will surely defeat its prey.
You pick up a distress call from a civilian ship. It's being chased by a Mantis ship!
MANTIS_CIVILIAN_AVOID: Smoking, the civilian ship limps on. You set your sights on the future.
The noise of the FTL spinning up almost drowns out the explosions. Almost.
You let them pass and try not to think about it.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MANTIS: A Mantis military ship appears on local radar alongside the remains of a human freighter. Prepare for a hostile encounter!
A Mantis military scout hails your ship. "Foolish alien! You has stifled greatness for too long! You rue the day you back the Federation!"
A small Mantis cruiser is broadcasting a repeating message on a wide-band frequency, "Non-Mantis ship that enter territory are forfeit. Lower shields and surrender if value your lives."

You detect a small military outpost and a few freighters nearby. This mineral rich planet in an isolated location would be perfect for an illegal Mantis mining operation. As you consider your options, a ship launches from the outpost. Prepare for a fight.
You discover yet another unlicensed and uncharted Mantis colony. They certainly waste no time expanding their claims. A Mantis ship moves to intercept you before you can jump away.
A Mantis military scout seems to have just finished a salvage op on a nearby wreck. They have no time to waste with warnings and appear to wish to fight.
A small military craft hails you and a Mantis captain appears on your receiver. "All local colonies punished for Federation's transgressions. Submit to processing."
A nearby Mantis ship begins aggressive maneuvers. You prepare for the worst.
A stream of clicks and gurgling comes on the comm from a hostile Mantis scout. The universal translator might be on the blink, but his intent is obvious.
The Mantis ship is pleased to see you, and fires up its weapon systems.
You recognize the outline of a Mantis ship against the blackness. Engage!
Something red looms. It's the Mantis.
A Mantis vessel hails you. "Hail is merely distraction!" You notice their shields and weapons have come online.
You notice a flurry of laser fire glance by the port window. The Mantis are upon you.
The Mantis hail you. Their captain says, "I claim vessel for my clan. Good hunting!"
A Mantis female comes on the vidscreen. The females don't make it to authority unless they're particularly vicious. You power the weapons.
A Mantis ship with the markings of a warrior tribe breaks position and attacks!
A Mantis ship hails: "Ah! Fine prey. Fine prey! We honor with most eviscerating arsenal!" You sense a cloud to this silver lining and power the weapons.
Children on Earth are told terrible tales of the blood red Mantis invasion ships - much like the one bearing down on you now - which once threatened the planet. You order weapons free!
A youthful-looking Mantis captain hails. "You, prey, must know. Your death, Kaaazthwak's final kill before maturity. Kaaazthwak pay respects." Seems respects in Mantis culture are paid with lasers.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MANTIS_HIVE: If you thought Mantis were deadly in other sectors, nothing can match the rage of a Mantis when you've entered their territory.
Hive Mantis aren't very friendly, but now that you've invaded their hive they'll stop at nothing to destroy your ship. A furious Mantis ship spots you and attacks.
You're hailed by a Mantis ship. "Federation fleshsack? Here in Hive? You have death wish. Let me grant it!"
You're greeted by the sight of a Mantis ship scavenging the remains of the last poor ship to have intruded on the Hive. Their attacker moves in to make you the next example.
You receive a hail from the Mantis ship at this beacon. "You come to Hive, so you must understand that you shall not leave Hive!"
A Mantis ship moves in to attack, set on the defending the Hive from your ship.
It doesn't take long for the Mantis ship here to notice you. They hail you. "Federation not welcome in Hive! You know this, yet you come here. Prepare die."
Something red looms. It's the Mantis.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_SUZERAIN: Suzerains are no force to be reckoned with. Unfortunately this beacon currently hosts a Suzerain, and they seem eager to reckon with you.
A Suzerain ship approaches, ready to attack! You hurry to arm the guns.

Suzerains are chosen and trained by the Mantis Bishops to be the strongest warriors in the galaxy. Unfortunately for you, at this beacon you find yourself squared off against one of the Suzerain's ships.
At the first sight of the cyan hull, you know the ship at this beacon is a Suzerain. You prepare yourself for a fight.
Suzerains utilize both drone and boarding tech to kill their enemies. You find yourself face to face with a Suzerain ship and have no choice but to fight.
You're hailed by a Suzerain warrior aboard the nearby ship. "Ah, Federation ship. You are first kill I make since I become Suzerain! I thank you, and welcome you to death."
A Mantis ship hails you, and you go pale when you see it is led by a Suzerain. "You are no coward, yes? Good, I look for challenge. I welcome challenge! Prepare for bloodbath."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ESTATE: A crimson Auto-ship appears from around a nearby moon, weapons already hot. Say what you want about W.I., but they sure keep tight security!

"Renegade Warning! Renegade! Renegade Warning! Renegade!" The ear-splitting bleeps from the nearby Auto-ship remind you how much you hate that everyone calls you by that name. While murdering everyone who does in cold blood might not be the best option, you doubt anyone will complain if you blow up this Auto.

"You thought you could hide. You cannot hide. I am programmed to be perfect at hide and seek. I have found every ship to ever hide in this system. My programming insists that I should be insulted at the thought that you could hide. I think I will kill you. Yes. The programming never lies."
Just when you thought standard Auto-ships were enough of a plague, these Innovation Autos are even worse. At least for every one you fight, it's one less the fleet can use against you later.
It seems there's no end to W.I.'s supply of crimson Autos to throw at you. You suppose this journey would be awfully boring without some fodder to plow through with your cannons though.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_TECHNICIAN: "I wanted to join the Rebellion as a soldier, but they told me my talents lay elsewhere. Well, it seems now I get a chance to redeem myself! Sorry, Renegade, but I'm just doing my job!"

Engineers aren't a common sight, but Technicians are even rarer. All of these synonyms are getting confusing, but enemies are enemies, and once you've put enough lead in them, the difference hardly matters.

"I bet you think this red uniform is cool, huh? I bet you think it's sooo great to be working for this company, huh? Real swell, huh?! HUH?! I bet you think that, idiot! It's not! It sucks! I'm stuck in the call center all day helping old people, and then during break I have to fight people like you! Do me a favor and die quickly so I can maybe scarf down my lunch before my next shift."

"I am legally required to read you the following disclaimer before I fight you: Wentworth Innovations is not liable for any and all damages that occur on, surrounding, or spiritually within grounds owned, contested, desired, or potentially future occupied by Wentworth Innovations. Damages are to be paid at the expense of the aggressor. By definition, the aggressor in any situation involve Wentworth Innovations technology, faculty, or staff in the party uninvolved with the corporation. Thank you for understanding."

A nearby Auto-ship swerves to attack you, but almost immediately malfunctions and shuts down. An irate technician appears shortly after. "Ugh, these damn things keep breaking down. Guess I'll have to fight you myself."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_ESTATE: "Oh thank god. I thought I'd never see any action after being stationed here, but now I finally have a chance to prove myself to command! No more talking to tech nerds! Woohoo!"

A Rebel Elite approaches. W.I. likely called in some extra protection from U1 since this sector is so vital to the Rebellion. Unfortunately, that means you have some Rebels on your hands that you'll have to grind through!

"Seriously? A Renegade? Here?! I was just about to head home, and suddenly you show up? You have horrible timing, you know that?" Though the Rebel could easily just leave, he seems to be preparing to fight. Some things never change.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MV_JERRY: "Bah, we didn't come to this reality to visit Jerry just to find Federation filth here instead! Out of our way!"
The Rebel ship at this beacon is no standard vessel - it's a Multiverse traveler like you, and it appears they're hungry for some Federation blood!
It makes sense for there to be heavy Rebel influence in this sector, but you didn't expect to be finding a Multiverse vessel!

"Finally we've found you!... wait, is this Jerry's sector? God damn it, now you've done it! If you've done anything to Jerry I swear to god that'll be the end of you! Well, I'm going to kill you either way, but you get the idea."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_JERRY: You are traveling in a Rebel sector with security measures akin to their Stronghold, so it should be no surprise that you've run into a ship that actually wants you dead!
A Rebel ship approaches: you already know what to expect with these kind of encounters. Get ready for combat!
It seems this sector is not without threat after all - a Rebel ship approaches!
"Hey, you're not one of Jerry's friends! Who let you in here?" A Rebel ship attacks out of nowhere.
It seems your travel through this elusive sector will have to take a pause - a Rebel ship is inbound!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_JERRY_HELLO: "Jerry?! Hey man, how's it hanging!" The Rebels are no longer trying to fight.
The Rebels are delighted to see their friend, and power off their weapons.
As soon as they see Jerry on your ship, the Rebels no longer seem to want to fight.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUTO_JERRY: "Prime Directive: protect Jerome from intruding Federation vessel. Do not resist destruction."
It's no surprise to find an Auto-ship in Rebel space, but for some reason you weren't expecting one here. Prepare for battle!

"Warning: Unwelcome Federation ship has entered the Jerome Protectorate. Please evacuate the system." The Auto-ship nearby scans your ship. "Oh. Warning: unwelcome Federation ship identified. Entering combat mode."
"Critical problem, Federation ship detected, threat to Jerome at least 2%. This risk has been deemed unsatisfactorily high. Preparing to exterminate."
TEXT_SLUG_PIRATE_CLEARING: There appears to be a pirate ship nearby. Be on your guard; anyone trying to hunt in Slug territory is either formidable or deeply stupid, and in space, either can be dangerous.
"We knew anyone foolish enough to try and sneak through a Slug nebula would stick to open space. Yield your goods and we may let you live." You cut the transmission in lieu of a response.
Before you can take a moment's rest from the ever present nebulas in this sector, a pirate ship appears behind you and opens fire.
TEXT_SLUG_REBEL_CLEARING: As you arrive at the beacon, a hostile ship immediately registers on your scanners. You didn't expect to see Rebels extending their reach into Slug territory. Charge the weapons!
You jump into empty space and are relieved to see your sensors blink back to life. However, you are less pleased to see them immediately register a Rebel ship on an approach vector!
You receive a message from a nearby ship, "Looks like our intelligence was correct! Sneaking through the clouds with the Slugs... No one can hide from the Rebellion!"
NEBULA_SLUG_FIGHT: Your sensors are no match for the Slug's telepathic abilities - a ship you never even saw opens fire from astern!
The Slug vessel you encounter here has obviously made a big score and is looking to test its new armaments. They picked the wrong ship to attack.
A Slug passenger ship hails: "Please, your worthy alien highnessesss, we are unarmed and sseeking asssylum." You approach cautiously, and weapons immediately spring from their hull!
A Slug ship approaches, but when he sees you're Federation he thinks better of the sneak attack and fires everything he has.
Direct attacks are not preferred by the Slugs, but of the three you see at this beacon, one has the brass to make a move on your position!
STORM_SLUG_FIGHT: The ion storm here threatens to deactivate your core systems, a fact made all the worse for the largely unaffected Slug ships circling like space-vultures.
The Slug ship that descends into view as you enter the ion storm must have sensed your distress - defensive action!
You arrive in the middle of an ion storm. Slugs generally avoid these storms but you find one waiting in ambush. Prepare for a fight!

You find yourself stuck in the middle of an ion storm with a Slug ship just a short distance away, refusing all hails. You cautiously try to slip further into the clouds, but they turn suddenly to attack!
NEBULA_KNIGHT_FIGHT: "Thessse nebulasss aren't for the Federation to be sssnooping around in! Get lossssst."

The Knights of Nights sure are determined not to let anyone interfere with the festival. Despite you not even being able to participate, the mere suggestion you might be working with Slocknog is enough to drive the ship nearby to murder.

A Knight ship jumps in, weapons blazing. It's not usual for Slugs to attack in such a blunt manner, but judging from the strange flight patterns of the ship, they're likely drunk. Let's hope that plays in your favor.
It appears a Knight vessel is waiting for you here. "I made a bet that I would be the one to kill you! Now ssssit ssstill and let me blow you up."
A Knight vessel appears to just have finished salvaging the remains of a small Slug interceptor, but as soon as you enter they decide to pick you off next!
The Knights of Nights have proven to be far more aggressive than regular Slug vessels, and aren't afraid to attack you straight on!
NEBULA_KNIGHT_CLAIRVOYANT_FIGHT: The Clairvoyants are primarily in favor of Slocknog, but despite this it seems the ship here has chosen protecting their homeland over letting a foreign Federation ship rumored to be supporting their king running about.
Though you haven't encountered as many Clairvoyant ships as you might have expected in a dense Slug nebula like this, it appears your luck has run out.
A Clairvoyant ship has chosen to do their job and protect their sector, and is moving in to attack.
"Renegade, you aren't ssssuppossssed to be here! Thissss isss a private sssector!" A Clairvoyant ship moves in to attack.
LANIUS_TRADER_MV_TEXT: A small Lanius craft approaches. You prepare for a fight but they do not seem to be carrying any weapons. After a brief moment they message you, although your translator struggles with the unfamiliar dialect. It appears they wish to trade.
You arrive to find a large Lanius vessel laden with recently collected metal. They are apparently offering to trade for supplies they are lacking.
LANIUS_CIVILIAN_MV_TEXT: You immediately receive a message upon arrival, "Help! These metal bastards have gone crazy!" The communication originates from the hull of a partially dismantled ship which lies among a number of other destroyed ships.
