The violent Lanius ship responsible for this carnage is advancing on the survivors.
You scan the area after arriving at this system. A Lanius ship is in fast pursuit of an unarmed civilian ship. It's hard to say if it's truly a threat since its weapons are not charging.

You arrive at the location of a recent battle. Judging from the debris, some settlers attempted to fight off a number of small Lanius ships, although it's impossible to say who instigated the aggression. A few skirmishes can be seen in the distance, but more notably a lone Lanius ship is firing on a heavily damaged civilian vessel.
LANIUS_SOLO_SALVAGE_MV_TEXT: You come across a single Lanius ship salvaging a small civilian craft. You cannot tell if they attacked the craft or just happened upon it.

There are remnants of a fierce battle here. Scattered among the hulks are small Lanius craft, slowly breaking apart the wrecks. One of the ships is close enough that you could probably attack it without immediately alerting the others.

When you arrive at the beacon you discover what must have been remnants of a large battle. However the vast majority of metal has been stripped from the ships, only various plastic and other materials float in a ring around a planet. A lone Lanius ship moves between the wreckage looking for more salvage.

A small asteroid belt is near this jump beacon. It must be mineral-rich since a Lanius ship is docked on a large rock, slowly absorbing parts of it. You could probably get their attention pretty easily.
A Lanius ship is slowly salvaging what remains of a small research station. It's hard to say if it was abandoned or attacked by the Lanius.
TEXT_DISTRESS_LANIUS_EMPTY: Whatever was the original source of the distress beacon, it has since been removed. Likely a gruesome fate at the hands of the Lanius, if you had to guess.

When you get to the beacon you quickly try to locate the source of the distress call. As you are looking, the signal blinks out. It is then that you notice the small fleet of scavenger ships absorbing debris from a large battle nearby. You can't help but wonder where the distress signal came from, but you decide not to risk pressuring the fleet.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LANIUS: Sensors indicate a small Lanius cruiser in the process of salvaging another small Lanius ship. Before you have a chance to wonder what caused them to turn on each other, the survivor notices you and moves in to attack.

Shortly after your arrival, a Lanius ship jumps near the beacon. It begins to move slowly toward you. You open wide band communication channels, attempting to make contact. However, it either ignores you or is unable to receive the messages. As they get closer you issue the order to charge weapons and find they do the same.

You receive a message on a wide band frequency, originating from an approaching Lanius ship. It appears not to be directed at you, but your translator does its best all the same: "... metallic opportunity... acquisition... by force..." Looks like you're in for a fight.

The beacon is surrounded by many tiny Lanius craft, surely only capable of holding one occupant. Perhaps they are some kind of forward scout searching for 'metallic opportunities'? As you consider this, a much larger Lanius vessel moves in to engage you, and the scout ships scatter in all directions.
As you arrive in the system, your proximity alarm begins screaming: there is a Lanius ship right on top of you! Before you have a chance to hail, they open fire!
As you are getting your bearings, another ship suddenly arrives at the beacon - it's the Lanius, and they've marked your ship for salvage!
At first everything seems quiet, then your scanners pick up a ship approaching at high speed - the Lanius have detected your arrival and are powering up their weapons!
You have stumbled across a mining expedition - unfortunately, the miners are the Lanius, and they've chosen your ship as their target!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_LANIUS: You arrive to see a number of Rebel ships attempting to dissuade Lanius scavenger ships from "acquiring" their forward station. A passing Rebel patrol ship spots you and moves in to intercept.

A Rebel scout patrols near the beacon. "Hah! I know you would try and sneak through this sector! You thought the Rebels wouldn't come here, did you? Well I've been waiting here for months, and now it has all paid off!"
The Rebels will spare no race any mercy, not even one as menacing as the Lanius. Though they came here to hunt the deadly metal men, the Rebels are just as keen to fight you as well.

You arrive at the beacon and notice a small Rebel ship chasing Lanius scavengers away from a wrecked Rebel battleship. As soon as the Rebel notices you and moves in to attack, the Lanius ships return to their prey like flies on garbage.

"It's awfully convenient that you've come here! I was given the horrible job of cleaning this sector of the Lanius, but perhaps killing you is the chance I need to be put somewhere else where our targets don't try to choke us to death!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_LANIUS: "Funny, how these Lanius still think they own this sector. They signed away their rights to be here the moment they fell asleep! This is our territory now, and we don't appreciate Federation ships coming in here and getting involved in our business!"
It's a strange day when you can bet just as much on a hostile Pirate encounter as a Lanius one in the Lanius' Homeworlds. Had you gambled on the pirate, you could have made some nice money just now.

Debris from a number of battleships are scattered around the beacon. As you approach the area a pirate ship thrusts itself through the hulks to attack. It must be using the metal to lure the Lanius into a trap.

The pirate ship patrolling this sector has been busy. The debris of several Lanius scouts and at least one civilian ship litter the area. "Welcome, welcome, there's room for one more!" The over-confident pirate hails you as he charges his weapons and moves in to attack.
A pirate vessel is hunkered down at this beacon in wait of a victim to appear. Satisfied with your ship over some giant Lanius militarized convoy, they attack.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUTO_LANIUS: An automated Rebel Auto-scout has been deployed to this beacon. Considering plenty of Lanius would love to eat it for breakfast, you consider the death you're about to bring to the ship a mercy kill. Do Auto-ships even feel pain?
It seems the Auto-ship here has just barely avoided being melted down by a now-destroyed Lanius destroyer. Still in combat mode, the ship registers you as its next target.
Auto-ships are sometimes used as bait by the Rebels to lure away Lanius ships. They also double as scouts for taking out passing Federation ships, a job that the ship here is intent on fulfilling.
An automated message registers on your screen. "This is Unit-964205-A. I will now begin combat with you."
A hostile Auto-ship comes swerving by, guns blazing. Behind it is the wrecks of several Lanius and pirate ships, and it appears a fight is unavoidable.
TEXT_NODE17_RESCUE: Shots fly by your port windows followed by a Rebel scout in pursuit of a damaged cruiser. Should we move in to engage?
There seems to be a small Federation colony under attack by a Rebel forward scout. Will you protect them?

A number of large transports are being pursued by a Rebel bombing squadron. One bomber has managed to slip through the defensive fire, and is poised to wreak havoc among the enormous yet vulnerable transports. There's time for you to advance and take it out!
A battle rages nearby between small fighters; apparently fighting over a space station. The Federation appears to be losing ships fast. Shall we assist them?
A civilian ship is broadcasting a request for assistance on a secure Federation channel. They are being harassed by Rebel scouts. Will you respond?

A number of large transports are being pursued by a Rebel bombing squadron. One bomber has managed to slip through the defensive fire, and is poised to wreak havoc among the enormous yet vulnerable transports. There's time for you to advance and take it out!
A battle rages nearby between small fighters; apparently fighting over a space station. The Federation appears to be losing ships fast. Shall we assist them?
A civilian ship is broadcasting a request for assistance on a secure Federation channel. They are being harassed by Rebel scouts. Will you respond?
TEXT_NODE17_ENCOUNTER_REBEL: A Rebel ship jumps after you, warming up its weapons as soon as it arrives. "Renegade! You've evaded the fleet for too long! You die, here and now!"
"So, the fleet let a Renegade through? How annoying. You'll never make it to the Flagship as long as I'm alive!" The Rebel turns to fight.
A Rebel ship moves to intercept you as you arrive at this beacon. There's no hesitating now, a fight is inevitable.
A Rebel breaks away from the fighting to face you. "Another Fed ship...? Will this war ever end?" Even through all this musing, they're intent upon fighting you.
A Rebel hails you, a crazed expression on his face. "Why do you persist? Can't you see the Rebellion is destined to succeed?" He confidently readies his weapon systems.
The warfare is unending in this sector. A Rebel is waiting for you at this beacon, and they're intent upon destroying you!
"Give up! Your insipid Federation is about to fall! You may as well surrender now and throw yourself at our mercy!"
TEXT_NODE17_ENCOUNTER_MV: A MV Rebel is finishing off a Federation ship at this beacon. The moment you arrive, they shift their attention to your ship instead!
"All that time and effort traveling to this 'verse... What a waste! It ends here!" The Rebel attacks you after closing communications.
A Rebel arrives at the same time as you. "This universe will achieve a Rebel victory! I won't let you interfere!" They're preparing for a fight!
You're not the only multiversal belligerent here - a Rebel from another universe is defending this beacon from Federation ships!
Even in this sector, the Multiversal Rebels follow you. They wordlessly prepare to attack you!
"Another universe will fall to the Rebels! Our hour of triumph is at hand!" They're readying their opening attack!
TEXT_NODE17_ENCOUNTER_AUTO: It seems the Rebellion is pulling no punches now - a brand new Auto model from Wentworth Innovations is deployed from the Engineer fleet to handle you while the bulk of the engagement goes on in the distance.
You aren't sure at first, but your eyes aren't deceiving you. A highly advanced Auto-ship has locked onto your vessel and is firing its full arsenal!
It seems Wentworth Innovations has given everything it's got towards the Rebellion's efforts here. An Innovation vessel is deployed from the fleet in the distance as soon as you're detected.

"Activating quality assurance mode. Running bootup protocols. Combat testing engaged. Please do not interrupt combat assessment or proceeding diagnostics." It seems this Auto-ship is brand new - so new its first test is against you!
A Rebel Auto-ship hurtles past you, nearly colliding with your hull, then stops and returns to engage you. You're visibly a higher priority than its prior target!
NODE17_REPAIR_STATION: There is a mobile ship construction platform stationed at this beacon. After a brief exchange they give you clearance to receive emergency repairs and military supplies.
An Engi civilian ship-yard has been converted into a military refueling station. They offer you the chance to patch up your ship and refresh some supplies.
Chatter on the comm suggests the nearby Federation base is outfitted with a repair station. When you forward your mission priority they quickly help repair your ship and give you some supplies.
A forward construction station is in the process of repairing damaged warships. Your command codes convince them to do a quick patch job on your ship.
A trade station was abandoned nearby. Some Federation engineers repurposed their shipyard to perform military repairs. They offer to help fix your ship.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LOSTSUN: "This is our territory, Renegade. Not all of us welcome your pity. Get out of our sector, or we will send you to the fiery pits of the underworld."
You find yourself in an argument with another Lost Sun ship over restricted beacons and such, and soon their weapons are drawn!
Not all Lost Suns are appreciative of the Federation's help, and some are even angered by it. The one at this beacon most certainly does not appreciate your presence.
Your presence appears to have offended the Lost Sun ship at this beacon in some way, because their weapons are ready and aimed straight at you!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROCK_LOSTSUN: "Your alliance with the radical terrorist group that is the Lost Suns will not be tolerated anymore, Federation Renegade."
The Rock government frequently sends ships to attack this sector. One such ship has noticed you, and doesn't risk you revealing their position.
Shots scatter across your defenses, but none do any severe damage. An unseen Rock ship scouting out the sector is attacking!
"Brave, coming here. The Rockmen do not appreciate your support of these arsonists, and we intend to do right by our true leaders!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_COALITION_LOSTSUN: As the Rockmen are a powerful ally of the Coalition, they have requested that some force be dispatched to take care of the Lost Sun threat. The ship here appears to group you in with that threat and attacks!
A Coalition ship hunting down Lost Sun ships spots you. They waste no time to power up their weapons and attack.
An angered Slug captain aboard the Coalition ship at this beacon hails you. "I came here to hunt ssome fire-obsssesssed freaksss, not more Federation asssssholesss! Prepare to be erasssed."
TEXT_LOSTSUN_ROCK_CHOICE: A Rock and Lost Sun ship are dueling at this beacon. Both notice you, and surprisingly both also call for your aid.
Taking sides in a duel can be a dangerous way to prove loyalty. At this beacon, a Rock and Lost Sun ship are fighting. Both have clearly noticed you, so you're going to have to save one of them.
Both the Rock and Lost Sun ship at this beacon are aware of your presence, but are too busy fighting to deal with you. Whose side will you take?

You find yourself faced with a dilemma as a Rock and Lost Sun ship are locked in a dogfight at this beacon. Either way, you can't leave without angering both, so you're going to have to make a choice.
MILITIA_FREE_AMMO: Nearby drifts the burnt husk of what surely was once a Militia transport. Little remains other than a single crate of ammunition.

You notice a mine drifting nearby, followed by several more. Most, if not all, are inactive, probably left over from some sort of training exercise. Fortunately, this means you can salvage them with relative ease.
A small resupply drone flies past, stops, then returns to scan your ship. It identifies you as friendly and restocks your ammo supply free of charge before speeding off again.
TEXT_MILITIA_CHOICE: A Militia vessel is making small repairs to their hull after a fight. No other ships are nearby.
You notice another ship, belonging to the Militia, drifting some distance away. The ship is fully functional but politely declines any hails.
A decently armed Militia vessel is patrolling the beacon. Because of your Federation status, they don't mind you.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MILITIA_MISTAKE: The wreckage of a civilian ship drift nearby, but before you can even think to salvage some of it, a Militia ship mistakes you as the attacker and prepares to avenge the civilians.
You get into some trouble over your identification with the Militia ship at this beacon, and not long after things get heated to the point of conflict!
The Militiamen at this beacon seem to mistake one of your crew as an infamous pirate with a heavy bounty. Not about to hand over your crew, you prepare to fight.
You try not to get into fights with civilians, but sometimes the civilians get into fights with you. Somehow you've angered the Militia ship here, and it's already moving in to attack.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_MILITIA: It takes a bold pirate captain - or a stupid one - to try and invade Militia space. When you notice the hostile ship approaching, you hope they're the latter as you prepare for combat.
A pirate vessel approaches, weapons already charging. They must be on quite the killing spree in this territory, and they're ready to take a break from Militia ships and fight yours!
It's ironic what a pirate problem Militia territory suffers from despite the heavy militarization here. No one will miss the ship here once you've killed them.
"Hah, I bet you expected a Militia vessel! Now you surely cower in your boots at the sight of my ship, yes?" You mute his comms mid-monologue and prepare to fight.
You catch the glimpse of purple fly past. Not long after, a pirate ship comes into view. "Haha! I have claimed the lives of many Militiamen, and now I shall claim yours! Prepare to fight!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_MILITIA_ONLY: The Militia fleet boasts a large amount of ships, but this also makes them a prime target for pirates in need of a new ride. A pirate controlled Militia ship approaches, weapons blazing.
A pirate ship, looking to test out the new gear they just stole from the Militia, locks onto your ship and attacks!
At first you assume the ship here is just another ordinary Militia ship, until you see the pirate paint decorating its hull. Pirates inbound!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_MILITIA: "The Rebellion shall never cease! All who ally with the Federation will be killed!" You doubt the moral superiority of murdering civilians only trying to protect their sectors, but if the Rebels want a fight, a fight they will get.

The Rebellion seem to hold a grudge against the Militia, though you can't imagine why. The Rebel ship here seems hell-bent on a fight, and since you're the only ship here they decide you will be a satisfactory opponent.
A Rebel ship has picked clean the remains of a Militia station. Nearly seconds after you jump in they spot you and decide to make you their next target.

The Militia tries hard to keep this sector clear of Rebel forces, but their defenses are incapable of keeping all of them out. A Rebel forward scout that has found their way into the sector spots you and attacks.
TEXT_SHERLOCK_TALK: "Ah, quite the interesting case, is it not? I do wish we knew how severe the victim's information was. Hard to judge how important this case might be. I've worked many a murder case, but none with such hypothetical stakes!"
"Unlucky they're all human, yes? Had one been alien we could have ruled them out surely. Or maybe not, and it would have made the case only more interesting!"
"Oh, I never grow tired of this job. Just wish I stopped landing cases involving murderous Rebels. I've lost quite a few partners to a stray bullet while chasing a suspect down."

Sherlock is busy polishing his revolver. "I'm a fan of Old Earth tech, the craftsmanship of their weaponry is quite astonishingly beautiful. If things here go awry, I hope I can trust my aim to put a bullet in the suspect's head before he puts one in mine."
"Do remember, you can never be sure if anyone is telling the truth! Put more faith into the physical evidence than a tale spun by a man."

TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN: A Zoltan ship makes contact. "The nature of the day is rotational. The fever is emaciated. The reason is-" They've caught some nasty deep space dementia. Before you can consider finding help for them, they open fire.
You're surprised when a stationary Zoltan ship opens fire. It appears there are aggressive pugilists even among the 'enlightened'.
You receive a message, "This area is off limits. Submit your ship to processing." It's only one guard ship in a lonely beacon. You decide to fight your way out.

You discover a number of Zoltan civilian ships fighting off pirates. Unfortunately one ship mistakes your purpose and moves in to attack! They are refusing all communication; you have no choice but to fight.
Like many areas in Zoltan space, the residents of this sector prepared well for Galactic war. The military here seem to have given up reasoning with foreigners, preferring instead to attack on sight!

A Zoltan ship is waiting at this beacon. They request your identification, but radiation from the sun in this system is disrupting your communications. They take your silence for aggression and move in to attack.
The Zoltan ship patrolling this area hails you: "This area is off limits. Secrecy is vital." They power their weapons.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_PULSAR: "The end is upon us. The eye casts its madness upon the sector - electromagnetism!" A stream of incoherent babble floods your speakers as a Zoltan ship attacks!
A Ministry research station has been constructed near the pulsar here to study it. Your presence, for some reason, is recognized as a violation of boundaries and they send a ship to ward you off!

Most species would tend to avoid locations such as these, but the Zoltans don't seem to particularly mind the hazards. They do mind, however, military vessels like yours wandering through their territory!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_AUTO: The Zoltans are one of the few races who've invested in automated drone tech. Unfortunately, these ships are unpredictable at best and often attack random passers-by, such as yourself.
"Combat mode engaged... looking for targets... target found!" An automated Zoltan vessel moves in to attack.
It appears the automated Zoltan vessel here is malfunctioning... and has falsely decided that you are a threat!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_ZOLTAN: "Emergency, all ships in range, we are under attack!" The frequency matches a nearby Zoltan ship; you move in on their pursuer. They take your intervention as a cue to jump away. Cowards.
You jump just in time to witness a Zoltan ship's FTL drive overload. In his final moments their captain implores you not to get involved, but it's too late - their attacker is already upon you!
Despite their precautions, pirates have begun to harass the local Zoltan settlements across this sector. One such pirate spots your ship and moves in to attack.
A ship with pirate markings demands your surrender. These are sad times when even Zoltan space is beset by pirates. You doubt these fools will be missed.
You spot a pirate ship looting a small Zoltan cruiser. They spot you and move in to attack before your FTL drive has a chance to recharge.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MONK_ZOLTAN: Monks aren't the only Zoltan ships to be found here. A Zoltan vessel admiring the scenery spots you, and somehow feels threatened by your presence enough to retaliate violently!
"What are you? Pirates? Mercenaries? You have come here to harm the Monks, have you not? Prepare to meet your end!" A confused Zoltan ship moves in to attack.

A Zoltan ship slips out of the nebula, its weapons drawn. It must have already been in the middle of a fight, and now that it has stumbled across you, it mistakes you for its previous attacker and locks on to attack.

A Zoltan ship comes lumbering drunkenly out of the nebula. It scrapes against your ship, though luckily it only does superficial damage. Still, in their strange stupor, the Zoltans blame you for the collision, and activate their weapons!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_AUTO_MONK: "This is a holy place. You are surely not welcome here." The mysterious voice is followed by gunfire as an Auto-ship approaches!
"Possible threat detected. Risk evaluation suggests immediate termination." Your radars show a hostile ship approaching fast!
The Zoltans value the security of this sector highly, so it's not surprising their Auto-ships are on high alert to attack any ships they don't recognize!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MONK_PIRATE: A pirate ship lingers at this beacon, attacking you on sight. It's no surprise however, this sector is a pirate magnet as the Monks rarely defend themselves.
It appears a pirate ship was waiting for you in the nebula!
"What are you, one of them Monk's protectors or somethin? Hah!" An arrogant pirate ship slips out from the nebula and attacks you.
Despite the disapproval from the Monks, pirates still visit and plague this sector. It appears you have encountered a rather nasty ship here looking for a fight.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MORPH: "KALPU! KALPU! RETER LIP LOO TIKA TIKA BOO!" An irate Morph begins to fling insults you can only imagine are incredibly vulgar in their language. You have literally no idea what you did to anger them though. Maybe just existing is enough to offend them?
As yet another hostile Morph vessel approaches, you can't help but wonder if the Shells never actually finished "designing" their temperament. What else could explain how erratic they are?
You receive a video with a gibberish title which shows several cartoon alien warriors fighting each other in gladiatorial combat. Minutes later, a Morph ship approaches, weapons on the ready.
Something tells you the nearby Morph ship isn't friendly. It might be the aggressive shouting, or their charging weapons. Just a hunch, though.
These aggressive Morphs really set a bad image for the rest of their kind. At least they don't yell "Hey, you're that Federation ship!" every time they see you.
You wonder if the Morphs are even aware who you are, or what your mission is. Unfortunately, "booj kabooj" is not an indicative answer as their vessel opens fire.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_MORPH: The Rebellion's sudden interest in these small, grey, unassuming blobs is concerning. It seems to have drawn a lot of their ships here too, such as the one here currently moving into fighting you!
"Hey, you're that Federation ship! Stop right there-" You mute the Rebel vessel. All of these lackeys are the same, they might as well be Morphs themselves.
Something isn't right about this nebula. A sliver of orange slips through the clouds, and your body goes into alert. Rebel vessel inbound!
There's never a dull moment in this sector. This time it appears your foe will be a Rebel. Is it better than a Shell or Morph? Time will tell...

Rebels aren't all too common nowadays outside of sectors of interest or the fleet trailing you, which means if anything the ship here is a sign of something bigger. Beyond that, it's also a sign there's a fight in your very near future!
You gave up your past self to become the brave Multiverse Renegade who'd save the Federation. Now, a Rebel ship moves into your path to stop you. Show them how you get things done.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUTO_MORPH: "Detecting for samples of substance M4-RH. Error. Reprocessing vessel. Federation ship detected. Activating 'sweet jesus that's an enemy' protocol." An Auto-ship quickly transitions from recon to combat mode. Prepare for battle!

You've seen several Rebel vessels prowling about here already, but this time it appears your foe is an automated vessel! Good thing this nebula is keeping you on your toes, because you've already started charging the weapons.
The Atlas entry said the Rebel threat here was high, and these Auto-ships are a clear sign of it. How much property damage will you cause the Rebels today?
"This beacon is under Rebellion control. Federation vessels will not be tolerated." An Auto-vessel moves in. If the Shells haven't taken care of this scrapbucket yet, then you will.
Thankfully, though it's sometimes hard to spot the grey wings of an Auto-ship slipping through the dark nebula, their distinct orange glow gives them away. Get ready for a fight!
TEXT_ANCIENT_CHOICE: The Obelisk ship at this beacon has not yet noticed your presence. If you wanted, you could fly away safely, or attack now and take them by surprise.
"You have made a mistake coming here. Clearly, you are not sane. I will give you one shot at mercy. Leave this beacon or die."
For once it appears you're the one with a decision to make. An unaware Obelisk ship appears to be making minor repairs to its hull and is oblivious to your presence.
It's rare to see a peaceful Obelisk ship. The ship nearby makes no move to fight nor contact you.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ANCIENT: "You are the ones sent by the traitor Aenwithe to bring our end! We shall not stand for this. Prepare for eradication!"

An Obelisk ship appears to be guarding this beacon, which seems strange considering you must have been the first unwelcome foreign ship to have come here. Still, you have no chance to escape this fight.
You're hailed by an Obelisk ship, which is already descending to fight you. "You've made a terrible mistake coming here, mortal. We shall make an example of you!"

"Welcome, welcome! I hope you understand the importance of what is about to happen. You shall be the first alien to die! We haven't even begun our invasion yet, and I get to enact such an honor. Goodbye, flesh-being."
Most Obelisks do not welcome a foreigner such as you to their sector, including the one at this beacon, barreling towards you.
You're hailed by an Obelisk ship. "Oh, so you're approaching me?" You nod, and tell them you can't blast the crap out of them without getting closer. Enraged, they power up their weapons and attack!

"So you are the ship I've heard about. The filthy trespasser who comes into our sector and dares challenge the master Obelisk race! Prepare to be annihilated!" The Obelisk ship speaking to you activates its entire arsenal and advances.
Shots scatter around you as an Obelisk ship moves in to attack!
"Oh, what a small little ship you have there. Shame I must destroy it, it would make a good decoration on my wall!"
The Obelisk ship looks at yours, first with disinterest, then with contempt. "Your ship displeases me. I do not wish to see it any more."
"Want to know an interesting fact? The divine creator who wrote this line was running out of things to write! Doesn't matter anyways, you'll be dead soon!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ANCIENT_AUTO: "This is an automated message left by master Xithe. Please die." An Obelisk Auto-ship attacks!
Despite also having made the Cognitives, the Obelisk's Auto-ships don't appear to be sentient themselves. More mindless robots for you to trash.
It seems, no matter where you run, there will never be an end to the onslaught of automated vessels attacking you!
Just when you thought the Rebellion's Auto fleet was a nuisance, now you have to deal with the Obelisks' too! Another hunk of scrap you need to kill to finish your mission.
In your mind, there is no difference between these ancient automatons and the Rebel's kill-machines. Just another brainless machine to be killed.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROYAL: "Blood bearing varmint! Get out of our sector you scum!" An aggressive Royal ship shouting expletives at you raises its weapons, clearly intending to attack.
"Ugh, how truly repulsive. Have you no dignity, wandering around like that, without your chassis? You should be ashamed, mortal being. I will put you out of your suffering."
You can understand why the Royals wouldn't be happy with you invading their sector, but you don't have time to think things through further, there's a mad ship on its way with murderous intent!
The Obelisks might be aggressive, but the Royals are even more so, and deadlier too. Unfortunately, a Royal ship nearby has chosen you as its prey!
An Obelisk Royal appears on your vid-screen and briefly glances at you. "Yuck", and with that their weapons go online.
You're even deeper in foreign territory now, and the native Royals aren't terribly happy to have you here. Looks like you'll have to fight for your right to be at this beacon!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROYAL_MFK: You've never seen such a large concentration of MFK Aces in a single sector, but it appears Vance sent his entire fleet to stop you. Prepare for combat!
"Hah, there he is! Let's show this little Multiverse ship how the Rebellion treats our enemies when they start playing dirty!"
"YOU! Do you know what you've done? This sector is living hell, and it's all your fault Vance sent our squadron here. I'm going to kill you for bringing this upon us!"
As you prepare to fight the nearby MFK Ace, you contemplate on the vast number of their ships in this sector. The Obelisks might be deadly, but even they are no match for the Rebellion's numbers...
The bright white hull of an MFK Ace ship approaches. There's no negotiating with Rebels, time to fight!
In front of you, an Obelisk vessel is blown into pieces as an MFK Ace ship flies past, stopping briefly to re-target and lock onto your ship next!
TEXT_ORIGINS_ATTACKERS: A Crystalline vessel is the source of this distress beacon. It appears they're under attack!
A Crystal ship hails you, requesting that you protect them from a hostile ship that has been following them.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_CULTIST: Not that you expected a warm welcome from the cultists, but the ships here seem particularly aggressive. Perhaps their religion requires them to be rude...
"You are not true believers, your presence here insults the Ember spirits! Die die die!"
A hostile Cultist ship is here, their insane captain drooling at the prospect of killing you. These guys really are freaks.
An Ember vessel is drifting nearby the skeletons of some poor tourist vessels. At the very moment they notice you it seems they're set on destroying you next!
It appears a fight is inevitable as a Cultist vessel moves in to attack.
You never could have guessed at how many ships these cultists would have in reserve. Oh well, at least it means there's no shortage of scrap for the taking either.
"The Grand Priest has not sanctioned your presence here! You are not worthy of being in the presence of the Ember spirits!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ORIGINS_CRYSTAL: A Crystalline ship is moving about this beacon. You know there's an issue when you're seeing more cultists than Crystals in what should have been Crystalline territory, but you don't have time to ponder that though any longer until the Crystal ship turns aggressive.

It seems the original population of Crystalline people of this sector have been on edge since the invasion of cultists. So much so that the ship here attacks you on sight without so much as a second thought!
"You are intruding in our sector, Federation! We have enough cultists to deal with, you cannot be here!" You try to reason with the Crystal ship, but they're beyond listening.
A Crystalline ship approaches, weapons drawn. You don't know what you did to anger them, but looks like you'll have to fight.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_OUTCAST: When Rockmen go against the Elders, there is not much left for them to become other than outcast pirates or refugees without a future. One such ship patrols the nearby system, and upon spotting you decide your ship would make an excellent target for them!
A ship full of Rock outcasts sees you first. Apparently they are no longer satisfied with the condition of their vessel, because now they're looking to take yours instead.
Outcasts are refugees from the Rock Government. Now forced to live the life of a pirate, they have no choice but to prey on ships such as yours to survive.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_SSLG: The SSLG's agents have little beef with the Federation, but they've always been suspicious that it might try to intervene with their movement. One overly cautious ship nearby spots you and isn't taking any chances!

You catch radio chatter on a nearby SSLG ship and an unseen outpost some distance away. "By the glory of Dianesh, it's so damn boring here. We're supposed to be overthrowing brutal dictators, not sitting on our asses singing kumbaya with a bunch of hippies! Er, hold on. Someone's watching me... oh what the hell, I'll just go kill them and say they were a spy. Finally something to do!"

"Hey, you! You aren't meant to be here! This sector is under occupation of the SSLG!" Last time you checked, the SSLG has as little authority here as you do, but looks like these guys are intent on beating you up. Get ready for combat!
PIRATE_CIVILIAN: Scanners indicate that a battle is taking place nearby. It seems that someone is under attack by space pirates.
You detect two ships, one chasing the other... Scanners show the pursuer is a pirate!
There are only two ships within range and they seem to be engaged in battle. One of them has the markings of a space pirate.
You arrive at the next beacon only to be immediately hailed by a small shuttle. "Help us! We are being attacked by pirates!"
You come out of the jump to see laser blasts coming from the other side of the beacon. It looks like someone is under attack from pirates.
PIRATE_BRIBER: You come across a pirate in hot pursuit of an unidentified ship. You quickly receive a transmission from the pirate: "Stay out of this fight and we'll make it worth your while."
An unidentified ship is badly damaged and still being assaulted by a space pirate. The victim begins a distress message until the pirate cuts in and offers to split the bounty if you sit tight.

A missile shoots across your bow when the jump completes. Your scans quickly reveal a ship with pirate markings pursuing an unknown vessel. The pirate hails you: "Damn it, we weren't expecting company. Stay out of this and you could profit."
TUCO_DRINK: The Rockman slides you a shot of some suspicious looking alien goop. It's surprisingly tasty. Two drunken pirates get into a brawl behind you and are escorted out.

The bartender polishes a glass and hands you another shot. This time it's a relatively normal looking glass of liquid, but it makes your insides burn like fire. You cough and spit it out. You catch some Rebels behind you laughing.
You're handed a glass of a putrid smelling substance, which you're told is freshly bottled Slug slime. When the bartender isn't looking, you pour it down the sink.

The Rock gives you a glass of clear liquid. It doesn't taste like anything. The chattering in the background quiets down for a second when a drunken Slug falls off the stage, then goes back to its usual volume.
The drink tastes an awful lot like urine, and your suspicions are confirmed when the Rockman informs you it's Human waste, considered a delicacy in some areas.
While you down the latest shot, you watch a Mantis juggle flaming skulls. The crowd breaks into applause until the Mantis catches on fire and runs screaming out of the inn.

As you drink the green substance in your bottle you observe the crowd further. It's an interesting bunch. You can see enemies staring at each other across the room, and glancing away when their gaze meets.
You choke down the horrid substance given to you by the bartender, a strange chunky white substance. The Rockman tells you it's expired milk from a space whale.
TEXT_CARPENTER_BENIGN: Your human finds a field of chairs. They look to be both comfortable and sturdy. Great value, but maybe not what you need on a starship.
Your human finds a lovely dining table. Your human isn't an expert on wood, but the artisanal value is exquisite.
Your human finds a series of wooden figurines of animals of all sorts. Your crew seems to want one.
Your human finds a lovely cabinet, with a delightfully rustic feel. Should improve the comfiness of any dining room by 300%.
Your human wanders into the massive garage, which contains canoes, kayaks, and other small boats. Given the abundance of water on this world, they're likely to be useful.
Your human finds an array of empty barrels. Your crew takes entirely too long to realize they're empty because they're for sale.
DISTRESS_REBEL_HOSTILE: The distress signal at this beacon is coming from a Rebel ship. "Warning to all ships! We barely escaped from a silver Duskbringer cruiser fully decked for war!" They stop abruptly upon detecting your ship. "Oh come on! Another one?!" Full of exasperation, they attack your ship.

The distress signal at this beacon is coming from a Rebel ship. "Evacuate this region! We spotted a horrifying Mantis Renegade armed with a full array of bombs!" They stop abruptly upon detecting your ship. "We might be able to take this one. Battle stations!"

The distress signal at this beacon is coming from a Rebel ship. "General alert: We've encountered a pitch black, nearly indestructible Renegade! Recommend-" They stop abruptly upon detecting your ship. "Are we being invaded by Renegades or something?"

The distress signal at this beacon is coming from a Rebel ship. "I don't mean to alarm anybody but there's a Kestrel class ship with an absolutely absurd rate of fire. We barely escaped with-" They stop abruptly upon detecting your ship. "I'm so tired of Renegades." Reluctantly, they attack you.

The distress signal at this beacon is coming from a Rebel ship. "Stay clear! Some Renegades have jury-rigged a Federation cruiser to lob gigantic mines! We were a hair's breath from blowing up!" They stop abruptly upon detecting your ship. "How are there so many of you guys?"

The distress signal at this beacon is coming from a Rebel ship. "Be warned! An amber-colored Renegade has been spotted lighting Rebels on fire and freestyle rapping insults about our demise." They stop abruptly upon detecting your ship. "...At least this one's not flooding our comms with obnoxious garbage."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL: A Rebel appears on the screen, and unfolds a long sheet of paper. He dons a pair of spectacles, and begins to read; "A poem, for you. Ahem; Die."
Your ship is hailed. "We've found you at last. Prepare to die!"
A small Rebel ship is docked at a small station. You try to lay low but it spots you. Power up the weapons!
A Rebel ship has been patrolling this region. As soon as you arrive it begins its assault.
A Rebel ship hails you: "Federation scum! We've waited a long time for this!"
You receive a transmission: "Sorry sir, this is nothing personal but we're under orders." The Rebel ship's weapons go hot.
By the time you notice the Rebel ship behind the beacon, it's too late to avoid a fight.
A Rebel ship hails. "We did not fight a war to let a single Federation ship shatter our dreams of a better galaxy!" He locks weapons.
A Rebel ship approaches cautiously. "Personally," says the captain, "I'd have stuck with the Federation. But I'm a soldier, sir, and I'm no use without a war to fight. Raise your shields!"
You're hailed by a Rebel ship: "When the rebellion is complete you'll see the safer world we provide. Well, you won't, but you get the point." They arm weapons.
You receive a hail from a Rebel fighter: "I'll have you know I graduated top of my class in the-" you cut off the Rebel ship and prepare to fight.
Your arrival coincides almost exactly with that of a Rebel ship. It's hard to know who is more surprised, but there is no option but to fight.
"GLORY TO THE REBELLION!" A Rebel ship speeds past, firing its entire salvo at you. Defensive positions!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_PULSAR: A Rebel captain appears on the screen. "I thought we had been doomed to backwater assignments. This is my chance to get back in Command's good graces! Charge the weapons!"
A small Rebel research station overlooks a pulsating star. Before you can react a Rebel ship spots you and moves in to attack.
You arrive at an infrequently used beacon close to a pulsar. Before long a Rebel ship happens to jump nearby. Looks like you'll have to fight.
BOARDERS_REBEL_SHIP: You receive a message from a nearby Rebel station, "You have a lot of guts passing through our space, I'll give you that." He turns giving an order, "Kill their crew, I want that ship intact."

Your sensors warn of an incoming Rebel ship at the same time as you hear the telltale signs of a teleporter. You hear someone taunt from within the ship, "Ready to die? I sure am ready to get a promotion!"
Incoming message, "Hello Captain," says a Rebel in an officer's garb. "How very generous of you to turn yourself in. Prepare to be boarded. Come quietly and we may be lenient."
You receive a message on a low-band channel. "You're surrounded, just like the last of your Federation friends. Just die already." The enemy has teleported onto your ship!
TEXT_LEECH_SPACE_TRASH: It's only here in Leech space that you could expect to find immense volumes of garbage littering the cosmos. This beacon is abandoned save for all of the trash, so perhaps you could take advantage of it?

Several large chunks of debris almost collide with your ship, but fortunately you're able to swerve out of the way. Looks like the nearby region is littered with space trash left behind by the Leeches.
A black bag filled with toiletries and used food wrappers splatters on your windshield. Disgusting, but it looks like the rings of garbage all around this system might contain some hidden treasures.
TEXT_FAKE_SOLD_OUT: "Oh, awful luck, just awful! Somebody just scooped the last one up right before you got here. Literally, they jumped away and you appeared right after they left."
"Sorry, we sold out of those a while ago. They really just fly off the shelves!"
"Ah, see, we used to stock those but then nobody in this sector ever buys them. Eventually I just threw them all out. Guess I should have kept at least one, huh?"

"Yes! We should have one of those... Let me see..." He rummages around in the backroom for a bit before coming back. "You know what? It's orange. Sorry. Do you want something else?" You try to tell the salesman that you'll still buy it if it's orange. "No no, listen to me. It would be just a bit too orange for your taste. You'd better get something better." You tell him that it's okay, you still want to buy it. "I'm afraid you don't understand. It's far too orange for the likes of you." You insist that you don't care about how orange it is. "Well... You have to realize. It's... STAGGERINGLY orange. Like, more orange than you could even believe. If I sold you this, you would punch my lights out." You insist that color doesn't matter and you just want to buy it. "Well, if you insist... Oh shoot. I just checked, and it's broken. Sorry. You'll have to buy something else."
"What's that? Sorry, I don't think I'm familiar with that one." You try describing the weapon, but you only get a blank stare in return.
"You know what? We actually do have one of those, but it's been reserved by one of our other loyal customers. You understand, right?"
"Ah, bad luck! Out of stock. The next batch is supposed to show up in like, four hours. Sorry about that."
"Oh, oops. We have a full shipment of it, but I left them in my garage back home. Clumsy me!"
"I don't order those anymore. You know, they use unsafe labor practices to make those... or at least, that's what my customers tell me. And the customer is always right!"
"Oh, you know what? I used to have a manufacturer for those, but they went out of business. I never managed to find someone else to buy those from. Maybe you'll take something else?"
"Yeah, we have that. Let me go find it." The leech leaves to go back into the store room. Several minutes later he comes back empty handed. "It seems like I might have misplaced it. My bad!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LEECH: Leeches might be depressive and unmotivated, but not even that can get in the way of their arrogance. Some high and mighty Leech soldier apparently thinks he can take you on and attacks!

The unpredictable strategies employed by the incompetent and usually only half-willing modern Eargen military can make Leech ships frightening adversaries. Let's hope you can make it out of this one without too many scratches!

A Leech captain of the nearby ship hails you and clears his throat. "Ah crap, I had something I was gonna say. Awkward... uh, I'm just going to kill you. But it was going to sound WAY cooler if I had remembered my original speech."

Judging alone from the drunken movements of the nearby Leech ship, you suspect their captain isn't all there at the moment. In his stupor, he mistakes you for an enemy and attacks! Looks like you won't be able to reason with this one.
Hard to say why the nearby Leech ship has chosen to attack you. A death wish perhaps? You wouldn't be surprised, but you would have preferred if they had just asked instead of forcing it upon you!
A Leech ship eyes you passing by, and orders you to stop. Apparently, he's one of the last few soldiers left with the motivation to actually uphold his post. It's a shame his effort is wasted on you!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REVOLUTIONARY: It sure seems as if nearly every government nowadays is in the midst of rebellion, including the Leeches. A revolutionary vessel, dangerously low on fuel, decides to attack you for all that you've got!
A nearby revolutionary ship accuses you of supporting President Tyrdeo and attacks before you can defend yourself!
As with many insurrections, it appears the Leech revolutionaries are violent and aggressive nationalists who'll attack anyone, even passing Federation ships like you with no word in the matter!

The Leech revolutionaries themselves probably wouldn't mind the Federation so much if it weren't for the Vampweeds assisting them. The Vampweeds technically aren't your enemies - but with their nation being so inclined towards militarization, and the fact they fought on the side of the Hive in the Federation-Mantis war means they aren't so hesitant to taking on Federation ships in their space!

"The future is now! First the Eargen Republic, then the galaxy, then the Multiverse! The Leeches shall taste glory once again!" These revolutionaries seem to be setting their sights a bit too high, but you won't waste time talking it through.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LEECH_ROCK: The Inquisition made a deal with Tyrdeo to protect Eargen space from the revolutionaries, but so far they've mostly just established immense numbers of troops here that do little to actually help the government, and more to just bother travelers like you. Whoopee!
A Rock captain stares down your ship. "I am tired of working with these repulsive tapeworms. I will escape, using your ship."
It's a miracle the Rockmen can tolerate being around the Leeches when they're normally so prudish. It's clearly putting them on edge, enough so that with little reason the Rock ship here attacks!

"These Leeches know nothing of the holy words! I am tired, and frustrated. The Theocracy will not let us leave until the war is over. I will now pretend you are my coworkers, and I will smash you into bits."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_LEECH_COALITION: The introduction of the Leeches into the Coalition seems to have been only a half-hearted gesture on both sides. The Republic doesn't seem all too keen on acting in the interest of the Coalition, and it's highly probable the Coalition is only helping fight the revolutionaries because of the number of soldiers the Leeches can provide. Now, enough politics. A threat approaches!

For all the Coalition's build up as some grand galactic threat, they really haven't seemed to do much besides the Aquarian Invasions. Sure, it's a nuisance you have to deal with ships like the one barreling towards you right now, but at least they aren't directly attacking the Federation anymore.
"Geh, you know what's worse than a stupid smelly Leech? A stupider, smellier Federation captain!" The Coalition captain receives several high-fives from his crew, then attacks!
A Coalition ship looms, unsure whether it will attack you. That's a joke of course - they already made up in their minds to attack before you'd even had the time to read the first sentence.
TEXT_VISION_ENCOUNTER: A vessel as black as night approaches, and without words begins its assault on your vessel. You have no choice but to fight!
"And so the Renegade seeks to undo the eternal reign of chaos they set in motion? How cute, but there is no hope for you now. Simply accept the inevitable and surrender."
An alien vessel, another of Her minions, opens fire on you. There is seemingly no end to these legions of darkness.
You think you might be hallucinating at first, but a black vessel begins to take form in front of you and eventually opens fire! Get ready to fight!
It's unfortunate that the C.E.L. is still preoccupied, because you could really use their fire support right now. Hostile vessel approaching! No choice but to fight!

The waves of enemies in this sector seems to be unending. It's weird She is willing to sacrifice so many minions on you, but perhaps She's afraid? Or more realistically, She just has a lot of cannon fodder to feed you.
TEXT_DISTRESS_SEPARATIST_TRAP_BEACON: The Engi ship emitting the distress beacon here has already been destroyed. The responsible Separatist ship engages you next, assuming that you are the reinforcements they were calling for.

"Captain, you should have [known] this was a fake distress beacon. The differing micro-oscillations and gamma node frequencies are a -dead- giveaway. Given that you failed to observe them, it follows that you must be an individual of low IQ - therefore leaving me no choice but to [eradicate] you. Do not worry, the universe will not miss your -underwhelming- intellect."
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_SEPARATIST: A short screech plays over the comms followed by a looping message of binary. You don't have time to translate before a Separatist ship fires a warning shot that ricochets off your defenses.

A strangely verbose Engi hails you. "Unfortunate time of encounter, -Federation- ship. I appear to have [damaged] the part of my system that encodes for reason and logic, and now have the burning desire to kill."
An enraged Separatist hails you. "Problem: You have -accidentally- stepped on lifelong friend of [mine] in microscopic state. Solution: die."
Though Separatists usually avoid other ships, the one at this beacon appears to be in critical condition, and in desperate need of scrap.
A Separatist ship moves in to attack. You aren't sure how you angered them, but it no longer matters.
You're hailed by a Separatist ship, who begins to speak a great deal about the works of some dead guy named Shakespeare. He suddenly stops his speech abruptly and attacks!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MANTIS_SEPARATIST: Separatist or not, the Mantis don't care about the source of their Engi slaves. A Mantis scouting out this sector decides to attack your ship!

A Mantis ship, most likely coming here under the assumption it would be a regular Engi sector, has grown aggravated from the lack of populated ships to fight. Finally greeted by a challenging battle in the form of your ship, they waste no time to move in and attack.
You're hailed by a Separatist ship, which briefly shouts "Watch out for killer bugs!" before jumping away. The pursuing Mantis ship decides to make you its prey instead.

A frustrated Mantis captain appears on the call screen. "Oh great, another ship. What wondrous horrors you greet us with? Perhaps flesh eating cloud? Maybe knife hand monster with long tentacles?" He quickly realizes you are in fact a Federation ship, and all of his doubts are cleared. He orders his crew to prepare for combat!
In this sector it can be hard to tell whether the flash of a red hull will bring an Engi or some other vessel. Unfortunately, this time it turns out to be a Mantis, longing for a fight.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_INFESTED: You attempt to hail the neighbouring ship, but all you get in return is a series of clicks and chittering. The ship is infested, man the weapons!

One can never be too careful in this sector full of unusually-intelligent spiders. Quick scans reveal the ship here has been infested, and when the ship moves in on the attack your suspicions are confirmed.
An infested vessel moves in. Looks like you have another ship full of spiders to deal with!
The Militia wasn't joking when they said this sector was infested to the brim with spiders. A full functional vessel now controlled by spiders approaches, on the offense!
You attempt to hail the neighbouring ship, but all you get in return is a series of clicks and chittering. The ship is infested, man the weapons!

One can never be too careful in this sector full of unusually-intelligent spiders. Quick scans reveal the ship here has been infested, and when the ship moves in on the attack your suspicions are confirmed.
An infested vessel moves in. Looks like you have another ship full of spiders to deal with!
The Militia wasn't joking when they said this sector was infested to the brim with spiders. A full functional vessel now controlled by spiders approaches, on the offense!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_BROOD: You remember the guard's warning about Brood ships here, and you can see why. A deadly Brood vessel with their weaponized spiders approaches.

A civilian ship jumps away after sending you a very brief message. "Crazy spider people, stay away!" You don't have time to process what the ship means before a hostile Brood ship comes out of nowhere and attacks!

Few threats are more menacing than a ship full of eternally burning Rockmen with giant laser cannons. Fortunately, such a ship is not what you're greeted with at this beacon, but it's still no good sight. A crazed Brood vessel attacks, and it appears conflict is inevitable.
"Fear me! Fear the spiders!" You aren't given a chance to respond before a spider-obsessed pirate vessel barrels down on you with murder on their minds.
You remember the guard's warning about Brood ships here, and you can see why. A deadly Brood vessel with their weaponized spiders approaches.

A civilian ship jumps away after sending you a very brief message. "Crazy spider people, stay away!" You don't have time to process what the ship means before a hostile Brood ship comes out of nowhere and attacks!

Few threats are more menacing than a ship full of eternally burning Rockmen with giant laser cannons. Fortunately, such a ship is not what you're greeted with at this beacon, but it's still no good sight. A crazed Brood vessel attacks, and it appears conflict is inevitable.
"Fear me! Fear the spiders!" You aren't given a chance to respond before a spider-obsessed pirate vessel barrels down on you with murder on their minds.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_CLANSMEN_INFESTATION: "I grow tired of thessse ssspiderss. I came for a challenge, but thessse arachnidsss are too easssy to kill. I long for a challenge... ssssuch asss you!"
The Clansmen enjoy a good exotic hunt, and the spiders are just that. However, that doesn't mean they won't also go out of the way to hunt ships like yours!
"Pissss off, Feds! Thisss sssector is my hunting ground, not yoursss!" An offended Slug arms their weapons, and it's about time for you to do the same!

Few things are deadlier than a mad Slug, and the Clansman here is particularly miffed. "Damn ssspiders keep eating my crew. You, Fed sship. Sssstay ssstill and let me kill you, I need an easssy kill for once!"
"I grow tired of thessse ssspiderss. I came for a challenge, but thessse arachnidsss are too easssy to kill. I long for a challenge... ssssuch asss you!"
The Clansmen enjoy a good exotic hunt, and the spiders are just that. However, that doesn't mean they won't also go out of the way to hunt ships like yours!
