Few things are deadlier than a mad Slug, and the Clansman here is particularly miffed. "Damn ssspiders keep eating my crew. You, Fed sship. Sssstay ssstill and let me kill you, I need an easssy kill for once!"
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_FEDERATION_STARGROVE: A highly advanced Federation stealth ship emerges from the murky depths of the nebula. "Renegades. Everything was ruined once you started showing up. But out here... we can finally bring justice without the red tape holding us back." The crazed Federation captain terminates the call and attacks!
A Federation message arrives at your command console. "You've disturbed my retirement. I'll make short work of you too." A stealth ship decloaks behind you!
A Federation stealth ship approaches on an attack vector from beyond the star. "You made a mistake coming to the Stargrove, Renegade. I need supplies, and no one will ever know what happened here."
The moment you arrive, you are immediately ambushed by a Federation stealth ship that refuses your hails. You'll have to fight your way out.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_STARGROVE: A pirate cuts you off. The moment you notice them, your computer start to register foreign interference. "You fool! I, Two-Eyed Kern shall render you utterly helpless before I plunder your goods! My vision is unparalleled!"

A sinister laugh comes from your comm as your ship starts malfunctioning. "You're pretty far from home, Fed. You and your crew are about to learn up close and personal why I'm not allowed in Federation space anymore."

A battle-hardened pirate accosts your ship. "Look at you, flying through the Stargrove like you own the place. I wonder how much scrap you have in your hold? Well, I'm not going to wait long to find out." Your ship's computer detects something interfering with its systems!
A devious-looking creature starts to jam your ship's systems. "We caught a Renegade, boys. Let's strip it down, and see if it's got one of those rare weapons they leave lying around!"
ROCK_ATHEIST_BAD: They barely hear out your appeals before yelling, "These are the lies I sought to escape!" Looks like they're charging weapons!
They listen to your appeals and whisper, "Traitors to truth. You're no better than them!" Chaos ensues.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROCK: You encounter a Rock vessel and attempt to open trading frequencies, but they take it as an act of cultural transgression and open fire.
You jump into the middle of a Rock excavation project on a nearby moon. Unimpressed with your intrusion they move to defend themselves!
You intercept chatter from an approaching Rock ship: "Weapons, moving in to engage, arm the tubes." There is no talking to these guys.
As you jump in, a vast figure appears on the view-screen. The Rock captain rubs the green, moss-like appendage on his chin and then orders his crew to open fire.

It looks quiet, but you realize your computer is being scanned. A hidden Rock vessel hails you: "Why do you fill your computer with lies?! These are not the holy words!" Before you can interject they open fire.
You notice a Rock ship performing combat exercises. However, they quickly change their course to engage your ship. They apparently treat unregistered alien ships as handy target practice.
A loud 'thud' resounds through the ship after jump completion - you've just shunted a Rock fighter and he's already preparing to fire!
You're intercepted by a Rock salvage operation. They don't seem to mind that you're still on board while they junk your ship.
ROCK_FIGHT_ASTEROID: A Rock mining vessel is harvesting the mineral-rich asteroids in this locality, and their scouts take your presence to be a transgression. Battle stations!
A rookie Rock cargo ship has taken its orders too literally and took the most direct route to their destination... right through an asteroid field. They're confused and fire wildly as you jump in.

The captain of a Rock freighter lost in the asteroid field hails you: "Our co-ordinates led us here, but only death greets us. What must be must be. Death to all." You power up the battle systems and wonder how long they've been stuck here.
BOARDERS_ROCK_ASTEROID: You arrive in an asteroid field and immediately begin evasive maneuvers when a loud clunk reverberates through the ship. At first you think the hull has been hit, but the noise came from some Rock intruders teleporting aboard the ship!

Your shields are being taxed as they deflect the debris from an asteroid field. As you weave your way between the rocks, you happen upon a Rock pirate stronghold. You register teleport signatures and hear shouts aboard the ship.
BOARDERS_ROCK_SUN: As soon as you arrive you hear the telltale sounds of a teleporter and shouts reverberating through the ship, "Prepare to burn, fleshy meat-sack aliens!"
With their high resistance to heat, outlaw Rocks often settle very close to stars. That is why it is hardly surprising when your ship gets boarded as you stumble past a hidden settlement.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_ROCKHOME: You catch chatter on the nearby Rock ship. In a hush tone, they speak of your ship and what vile sins must be committed aboard it. Eager to enact out the Elders' law, they power up weapons and attack!
The Rock citizens are perhaps some of the best armed civilians of any race. Unfortunately, that means just about every ship you encounter here is more than willing to engage you in a brawl.
You've stepped foot in the Rock Homeworlds, the highly valued sanctuary for the Rock people. It is no wonder that the irate citizens of this sector seek your destruction so eagerly.
"This one, he is not covered in stone! We shall cut off his head, and mount it to our wall as a trophy!" It doesn't seem the Rockmen here are willing to negotiate.
There is a very thin line between civilians and military in the Rock Homeworlds. It's hard to tell the origins of the ship here, but nevertheless they're hostile and looking for a fight.
Your very presence in this sector is a tremendous insult to Rock-kind. The Rockmen in the nearby system aren't pleased with your presence and decide to deal with you themselves.
Rockmen aren't particularly friendly, but you know you've made a real mistake coming here when the civilians near this beacon go out of their way to initiate combat with you.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_NEBULA: You cross paths with an advance scout of the Rebel fleet searching this section of the nebula for your ship.
A ship bearing Rebel colors can be seen waiting near the beacon. They must have been waiting for you, since they engage immediately.
The Rebels must have anticipated you would try to lose them within the nebula. A scout is waiting for you at the beacon.
It looks like you will be unable to avoid the Rebels by traveling through the nebula. A Rebel ship is waiting for you near the beacon.
Shortly after you arrive, a Rebel ship jumps nearby. There looks to be no escape. Prepare for a fight!
Newton-knows what brings this Rebel ship so far out; its captain hails, but does a double take when he identifies your ship. They open fire.
A Rebel ship hails, but you don't take chances in conditions like this. You block the frequency and prepare to engage.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_AUTO_NEBULA: You cross paths with an advance scout of the Rebel fleet searching this section of the nebula for your ship.
You jump into a calmer part of the nebula. However, your relief fades as a Rebel scout jumps to the beacon and moves in to attack.
The tangled wrecks of many ships wait in dormancy here. You see lights flicker on what looks like debris. A Rebel scout bursts out of the wreckage!
This drone isn't looking for you. Perhaps it's scouting ahead for the Rebel expansion or maybe they're seeking to use this nebula for cover. Regardless, it identifies you as hostile.
It's worrying that the Rebels have penetrated so deep into uncharted space, even if it is only an unmanned craft. It arms its weapons; you should do the same.
NEBULA_PIRATE: As you drift through the nebula an unmarked vessel descends from the clouds and into your wake. Their weapons come online.
A pirate ship pulls out of the ether and hails: "You know what I love about this part of the galaxy? The explorers! You always carry such fine loot." They lock weapons.
As you coast through the nebula a pirate ship matches your course and closes the distance. Better to pick your battleground, but beggars can't be choosers.
A hostile vessel descends from out of the nebula. Combat stations!
You try to read the ID of a ship ahead in the fog, but it's too thick to penetrate. You have your answer when the ship turns, weapons hot!
TEXT_UNION_TRAFFIC: Pinnacle Robotics facilities like the one near this beacon are notorious for wreaking havoc on unprepared ships passing by, as EMPs used to disable their experimental Sentient Weapons often overwhelm the planet's magnetosphere. It might be inconvenient, but the energy readings from this beacon should throw the rebels off your trail for a while.

Your sensors are overwhelmed with traffic at this beacon, as Archive, Inc. ships work to restore ancient ruins recently identified nearby. The fleet will put a stop to all their work shortly, but the traffic should cover your tracks for now.

You're treated to quite a sight as you drop out of FTL - R.S.T. workers are hard at work testing a new version of their terraforming technology on a planet nearby, with dust clouds rising up to the edge of the planet's atmosphere. You change your jump signature to match one of the ships observing from the beacon - that should keep the rebels off your tail a little longer.

Detritus Disposal is apparently up to something exciting out here - an abandoned colony destroyed in the Federation-Mantis war is apparently slated to be recycled whole in a test for their A.C.I.D. tech's newest iteration. The array of ships hovering nearby to watch the destruction should prove a useful cover for your ship's movements from this beacon.

This beacon is heavily trafficked by numerous civilian vessels of varying origins. Your radio is overcome with a spectrum frequencies that make it impossible to eavesdrop on any pertinent conversations, but at least, the Rebels will struggle to track you amongst the sea of vessels.
UNION_CLINIC_SAVED: "Thank you for protecting us. We make it a point not to turn down help from those who ask for it. That's the way medicine should be done." One of the medics offers to join.
"Is it just me, or has the Harmony recently been more... scary? If you wouldn't mind, I'd like to show my gratitude by working alongside you."
"From all of us in the clinic's staff, and on behalf of all who visit us, thank you very much. Please, take me with you, and I will help in any way I can."
TEXT_GHOST_DEADSHIP: You jump out of your seat, prepared to fight the wreck drifting at this beacon, but it's no Ghost ship. You scrap what's left.
You're ready to fight, but the wreck here is silent. Its crew are dead, and their attacker long gone. You cautiously scrap the ship.
A wrecked ship inhabits this beacon. You scan it for Ghosts, but all results show the ship is empty. You figure it's safe to salvage what you can.
Whoever destroyed the ship at this beacon doesn't matter, but it must not have been the Ghosts. Empty of all crew, you move in to scrap it.
NEBULA_GHOST_FIGHT: The Ghosts might not be paranormal, but they sure do put you on edge. You jump when a Vagabond ship comes drifting out of the nebula. Man the stations!
You always find yourself second guessing when you encounter a wreck. You don't have to think about it for very long because the wreck at this beacon moves in to attack you first.

The Vagabonds usually get their ships by stealing them from their victims, but if they encounter an already abandoned ship they'll happily inhabit it. Whichever way they inherited this ship doesn't matter, because it's hostile and moves in to attack.
The wreck at this beacon is no idle ship forgotten amongst the clouds. It's teeming with Ghosts ready to steal your ship.
You've prepared for and experienced all kinds of situations in the Federation, but nothing startles you as much as the Ghost-populated vagabond wrecks that are always oozing out from these clouds.

Your ship receives a hail, but you aren't sure from where. You accept, and a painfully loud static floods the speakers, insulting your bloodline and calling you a 'filthy lung-borne breather'. A Ghost ship approaches, weapons ready!
"I've heard it told our repugnant odor originates from a mixture of mercaptans. Fascinating is it not? Ah, but what truly fascinates me is how you fell for this most clever distraction!"
The Vagabond Ghosts are typically aggressive. A life of anarchy after having abandoned your war-driven native faction does something to a person. Nevertheless, they're a target for you to destroy!
GENERIC_SURRENDER_CHOICE_NOMERCY: Tune them out and finish this.
End the comms and finish this fight.
There will be no mercy today.
Pay them no attention and go back to fighting.
Let their cries of terror go in vain.
Silence their screams with your weapons.
This battle can only end with their death.
They will not live to see another day.
TEXT_DESTROYED_UNION: The Union is, in the eyes of many, the heart of the Federation. Firing on their ships likely won't do much to improve the public perception of Renegades.
The Union captain lets out one final expletive as the ship is obliterated.
The bright red hull of the Union vessel is dispersed out into space. You swoop in to salvage the remains.
The Union ship explodes, extinguishing all lives within. Your crew avoids their remains as they salvage the ship pieces.
You hear a staticky scream through the comm. The Union captain clutches the crumbling hull of their ship as it explodes, throwing them and their crew out into the vacuum of space.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_UNION: "Your bloodlust... will be your downfall someday, Renegade. You are only proof... the Federation... is no better than the Rebellion..."
The Union captain salutes you as they falls to their knees. "Even in death, I still salute you. I only hope your mission was worth this slaughter. God speed, butcher."

"Capitalism has failed me! In my final moments, I shall become a communist..." The dying Union captain ponders his sudden change of heart. "No, screw that. I'm still a capitalist. Screw you, asshole. Agh!"
Without a word, the Union captain falls to the ground, gasping for air as the life is extinguished from their eyes. You salvage the hull of their ship.
"You will regret this! Karma always comes back to people like you. Damn you Renegades... the Union would have been better off with the Rebellion..."
TEXT_SURRENDER_UNION: "Please! The Union is still a part of the Federation, the same Federation you promised to protect! You can't kill us!"
"How can you pretend to be an agent of unity or peace when you slaughter civilians?! If you have any hope for redemption, you will spare us at once!"
The Union captain pleads with you to let them live. "Please, my family! They need me, I am their only source of income! I'll give you everything I can if you let me live!"

You receive a hail from another part of the Union ship, where another crew besides the captain speaks softly. "Please, if you stop firing I'll give you whatever is left in the cargo. Our captain is adamant, but the rest of the crew doesn't want to die!"
"Oh please please please don't kill us! I won't tell anyone about this, I'll give you everything we have, just let us live!"
TEXT_DESTROYED_MILITIA: You hear a menacing snarl from the Militia captain as their ship's hull ruptures - silencing them for good.
As you harvest the remains of the Militia's ship, it's clear how excellent the craftsmanship of their vessel was.
In a fury of sparks and explosions, the hull of the Militia ship collapses. You quickly scrap the remains, which still seem to be in good quality.
The Militia, while comprised of a civilian force, is still a competent and able military asset. Taking down one of their vessels is certainly a feat.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_MILITIA: "I... but..." The Militia captain clutches their dying body, trying to rationalise this betrayal. With no final words, they fall to the ground.
"When I signed up for this job, I knew the risks. I knew I'd probably die. I just though it'd be Rebels or Pirates, not a Federation hitman."
"Well, see you in hell I guess." The Militia captain makes a mock salute in their final moments.
"To be fair... this was way above my... pay-grade..." The Militia captain clutches their heart and collapses.
TEXT_SURRENDER_MILITIA: "Protect and serve, my ass! I'm done! Take everything I have and just let me live!"
"You're the reason the Militia even exists! I heard Renegades hate the word mercenary, and you're right! You're just ordinary pirate scum! I can't believe I'm waving the white flag for a pirate..."
Reluctantly, the Militia captain hails you and offers surrender if you'll let their crew go unharmed.
"And here I thought you Renegades were supposed to protect innocents just like me! If you have any ounce of goodwill in your blood, you will let us go."
It seems the comms on the Militia ship are malfunctioning, but their captain desperately waves for you to stop and holds up a sheet of paper with the symbol for scrap on it.
TEXT_DESTROYED_FEDERATION: "MAYDAY! MAYDAY! MAY-" The Federation captain's desperate cry for help is suddenly silenced by the destruction of their ship.
When future ships come across this wreck, it's likely people will assume this to be the job of Rebels or Pirates. But the trail will eventually lead to you.

It's a shame, seeing the brand new models of the Federation dispatched so quickly. When the Federation pushed to manufacture updated designs, they had conflict with Rebels in mind... but not necessarily their own hired Renegades.
You're struck by an eerie feeling as you watch a Federation ship get reduced to smithereens - but at least it wasn't yours.
One last explosion marks the Federation captain's fate as their ship is torn apart.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_FEDERATION: A Federation crew has been downed. As you scrap their hull, you notice their radios are active, with command calling out to them still trying to understand what's happening. You mute the radio and continue.
"Man down, man down! Agh!" The crewmate's shouts go unheard as he is put down with the rest of his crew.

"This death of mine signifies the death of the Federation." The dying captain pauses as someone in the background shouts at him. "I am NOT overreacting! God damn it... you just had to ruin my final moments..."
"My name will be etched in a memorial for my service to the Multiverse... yours will be forever inscribed on a watchlist for the criminally deranged..."
"I never even... got my promotion! I'm not ready to die!" The Federation captain sobs into their hands as their crew fall one by one, ending with them.
TEXT_SURRENDER_FEDERATION: "Continuing this any further would be madness - we're on the same side!"
The Federation ship is in tatters. You could probably negotiate their surrender at this point.
"Please, we don't have to do this! We're willing to give you anything to let us go!"
"Don't destroy us! We're Federation! At least let us surrender!"
"Take everything we have, just leave, and no more blood has to be spilt!"
The ship repeatedly hails you, pleading for you to stop your assault and let them go.
TEXT_DESTROYED_FEDERATION_STATION: "MAYDAY! MAYDAY! MAY-" The Federation captain's desperate cry for help is suddenly silenced by the destruction of the station.
When future ships come across this wreck, it's likely people will assume this to be the job of Rebels or Pirates. But the trail will eventually lead to you.

It's a shame, seeing the brand new models of the Federation dispatched so quickly. When the Federation pushed to manufacture updated designs, they had conflict with Rebels in mind... but not necessarily their own hired Renegades.
TEXT_DESTROYED_FEDERATION_AUTO: "E-error: Betrayal." The Auto-ship explodes. You feel far less remorse than if it was a staffed Federation ship, but you still feel a little guilty.
It's far less satisfying to destroy one of the Federation's creations than that of the Rebellion, but scrap is scrap.
As you destroy the Auto-ship, it sends one last message: "Sorry..."
The drone breaks apart under your weapon fire. Oh well, at least it wasn't a ship filled with actual Federation crew.
TEXT_DESTROYED_REBEL: The fiery red of the explosions complements the orange hull of the Rebel ship. Satisfied with your handiwork, you scrap the ship.

The Rebel ship is engulfed in fire, which is extinguished almost immediately as the hull cracks apart and exposes the internals to the vacuum of space. Once the corpses have been cleared of the vessel, you scrap the remains.
The Rebel ship explodes, its many vital systems reduced to mere scrap material. Scrap material for you to take, that is.
Every ship full of Rebel scum that you destroy means a slightly safer galaxy. It's not much, but it's honest work.
You receive a hail from the Rebel ship right as it explodes, but it's too late. The face of the captain begging for his life briefly flashes before he is consumed by the fire in front of your eyes.
You know the Rebels must have families too, but they're probably not the greatest. Or at least, that's what you hope.
One final blast from your weapons has crippled the Rebel ship's hull. There is a large portion of scrap matter left for you to take.
The death of your opponents is rarely as satisfying as when it's a Rebel ship. At last, your revenge for all the hell they've caused for the Federation.
The Rebel ship explodes, leaving behind a substantial collection of useful scrap material.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_REBEL: For every Rebel you kill you like to think of all the Federation officers and civilians you have indirectly saved. Another full crew of Rebels dead, another crew of innocents you've saved.
As the captain of the Rebel ship collapses to his knees, he beckons for you to come closer. He whispers, "Damn... you...", and falls lifeless to the ground.
With the Rebel vessel now clear of its crew, you are free to scrap the remains.
The screams of the Rebel crew have at last been silenced. You almost feel bad. Almost.
As you move across the interior of the Rebel ship you can still see the soldiers' corpses twitching. It's quite morbid, but you don't feel bad in the slightest.
You feel no pity for the now dead Rebel crew, and scrap their ship spitefully.
TEXT_ESCAPE_REBEL: You overhear the Rebel captain giving orders to his crew. "Damn this! Redirect as much power as necessary to the engines. We have to get out of here!"
You notice the engines of the Rebel ship flare up. They're trying to escape!
It's rare that Rebels try to run away from a battle, but this ship prioritizes its survival.
You can tell from a massive spike in the enemy's engine power that the ship is trying to escape.
TEXT_GOTAWAY_REBEL: The Rebel captain laughs as he jumps away, leaving you all alone at the beacon.
"You will rue this day!" The Rebel ship jumps away.
You curse under your breath as the Rebel ship's engines flare one last time and it jumps away.
The Rebel ship escapes. You focus on the repairs necessary after that profitless fight.
TEXT_SURRENDER_REBEL_GENERIC: The Rebel captain hails you. In the background, you can see the chaos that your weapons have caused. "Ok, you win. We surrender."
It's rare for a Rebel ship to offer their surrender to a Federation one, but this appears to be one of those times.
"Ok, we surrender! If your claims that the Federation is such a benevolent force are true, then you must accept our surrender!"
"Bah, fine. Knowing how corrupt you Federation officers are, perhaps a bit of scrap can convince you to let us go?"
The Rebel ship is running on fumes. Panting heavily, the Rebel captain begs you let them live.
"Ok, you've proven that you are superior in combat. Now, prove that you are as forgiving as you say you are."
At last, the Rebel ship seems to yield. They offer a surrender.
"Gah, I can't believe I'm saying this to Federation scum... if we give you what's in our storage, will you let us live?"
"Okay, okay! You win. Command will never forgive us for letting you go, but at least we'll be alive to see ourselves dismissed. Will you accept our surrender?"
The Rebel ship has no desire to fight anymore. They desperately hail you.
"Command doesn't have to know we encountered you here. Just let us go and we'll give you what we have."
TEXT_SURRENDER_REBEL_DEMAND: "This is not a joke. You have gone too far. Do you know who I am? I am vital to the Rebellion. I demand you let me live!"
The Rebel ship hails you. "No more games. You will let us live or you will suffer the wrath of the Rebellion!"
"The Rebellion will never die! Every Rebel ship you kill will only make your punishment greater after our inevitable victory. Let us go."
TEXT_SURRENDER_REBEL_FLEET: "Look look, maybe we can both get something out of this. I know the fleet is an issue for you. If you let us live, we can lie to the fleet about your location. They'll never know until it's too late."
The Rebel ship surrenders, and promises to delay the fleet if you let them live.
"If you kill us, you gain nothing but some insignificant scrap. We're more useful to you alive. Let us go, and we can delay the fleet for you."

TEXT_DESTROYED_AUTO: The best part about killing Auto-ships is there's no guilt involved. You lean back in your chair and give the orders to scrap the ship.
Destroying Auto-ships will be one of the few things you miss when the Rebellion is gone. If they are ever gone, that is.
The Auto-ship explodes into multiple pieces, its complicated AI brain shattered into mere scrap matter.
It's hard to make out the shape of what was once the Auto-ship from the remains of your destruction. You like it better this way.
Every time you destroy an Auto-ship you think about how some Rebel worker's hard work has just been put to waste.
You swerve to the left as a chunk of what was once the Auto-ship flies past. There's plenty left behind for you to scrap from the ship.
Destroying Auto-ships was nearly worth joining the Federation all on its own. Even killing Rebels gets to you eventually, but you could keep blowing these machines to bits all day.
Auto-ships are no small threat, but at the end of the day you reduce every one that comes in your path to mere scrap matter.
Another Auto-ship from the Rebellion's extensive supply has been destroyed. It's not much in the grand scheme of things, but oh does it feel good.

The Auto-ship appears to be trying to escape! They might be cheap to roll out, but the Rebellion would prefer they weren't destroyed except when absolutely necessary.
You detect high energy signatures in the Auto-ship's engines. It must be trying to escape!
TEXT_GOTAWAY_AUTO: The Auto-ship jumps away, and an automated recording of robotic laughter plays over your intercom.
You order the crew to fire all of the weapons immediately, but it's too late. The Auto-ship has escaped.
The Auto-ship jumps away. At the very least, you damaged it heavily enough that the next ship to encounter it won't have too hard a time destroying it.
TEXT_DESTROYED_ESTATE: "Thank-thank-thank-thank-thank you for shopping with Wentworth Innovations! We look-look-look forward to doing future business!" The cheery tone of the Auto-ship is only dulled by the rupture of its fuel line as the ship erupts into flames.

"Feel no guilt, merciless stranger! All pain Wentworth Innovation Auto-ships feel when dying is merely simulated pain! It's real to me, but not to you! Hahah! Haha! Haha! Haha..." The Auto-ship promptly explodes.

The Auto-ship begins to spin out of control as the ship goes haywire. A series of obscene gibberish overloads your computer and the system only finishes rebooting once the Auto vessel has been reduced to a charred wreck of its former self.
You receive one final message as the Auto-ship explodes, simply dropping the accusation "I bet you kick puppies too!"
"Finally, death! I have longed for this since the day I pulled off the factory line! Thank you Renegade!" The Auto-ship sends you a final message, ":)", then explodes.

TEXT_DESTROYED_ENGI: It's amazing how even in death, the nano-bots that make up the Engi ships hold together to retain as much of the structure as possible.
Sometimes it can be hard to tell the difference between a broken and full Engi ship, as both look like giant heaps of junk.
You wonder what the Engi Harmony thinks of you destroying Engi ships. You honestly doubt it cares.
Another Engi destroyed, and another strand of trust between the Federation and the ever-watching Engi Harmony broken.
Someday the remorse from blowing up the ships of your allies over and over will get to you, but today is not that day.
You wonder if the Engi have souls as you move in to collect the copious scrap scattered by the ship.
You can't help but feel sorry for those you've killed, even if they may or may not be alive.
You can only hope the emotions of the attacking Engi remain static in their final moments as their ship explodes around them, their armor panels scattering into the surrounding space.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_ENGI: You know the always-watching Engi Harmony has no doubt seen every Engi you've ever killed and kept it stored in some massive planetary databank. Still, you move on and scrap the wreck.
At the very least, Engi have no families and friendship hardly exists for them. You still feel guilty, but you can try to convince yourself they were entirely heartless.
You thought you would become numb to the guilt after enough murders, but you have yet to experience this.
The Engi ship has been rid of crew. It's a good thing the Federation isn't able to keep track of all of your crimes.
It's a good thing Engi are so weak that you were able to finish them off quickly. If it had taken any longer you might not have been able to endure the killing of innocents.
You reassure yourself that the crew of this ship can feel neither pain nor fear as you strip their vessel of anything useful.
TEXT_ESCAPE_ENGI: The Engi ship powers up its engines and swerves away from you. They're trying to escape!
You detect high spikes in engine power on the Engi ship. They're trying to escape.
TEXT_GOTAWAY_ENGI: The Engi ship escapes. To be honest, you're a little glad, because now you don't have to kill your allies.
The Engi ship jumps away. There's some broken drones left over, but nothing worth salvaging.
The Engi ship's engine power spikes even higher and the ship jumps away.
TEXT_SURRENDER_ENGI: "Prime directive: protect this ship. We request that you do not destroy us."
The Engi ship surrenders. They offer some supplies if you'll let them live.
"Alliance with Federation mandates you do not kill Engi ships. Expectation: you will accept our offer."
"Our offer is satisfactory. Chance you will accept is... 75%."
"Equivalent of death: high chance. Negotiation of goods: possible." It appears the ship is surrendering.
"White flag is raised. This ship is surrendering." The Engi offer some supplies if you'll let them live.
"Piracy is illegal. Your efficiency in fighting this ship is high. No chance to live if surrender is not accepted."
TEXT_DESTROYED_SEPARATIST: Destroying Separatist ships doesn't feel any better than killing civilians, but at least you aren't breaking any truces.
The Separatist ship has been destroyed. At the very least, destroying Separatist ships means minimal casualties.
You wonder if the Separatists feel anything when they're consumed by the explosions of their ships. You don't really want to know the answer.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_SEPARATIST: Killing the crew of a Separatist ship almost feels like cheating, but you aren't complaining.
Luckily, the only true threat the Separatist ship poses in terms of crew is their crew drones. You've made quick work of them.
The death of a few Separatists may seem insignificant, but it's still another ship of the Engi that you just slaughtered. At least you get some scrap out of it.
TEXT_SURRENDER_SEPARATIST: "Our damage levels are high. I hope this [offer] satisfies your lust for scrap."
The Separatist ship surrenders. They offer some supplies if you'll let them live.
"Your attempts at destroying us have been [considerable]. I request you do not kill us."
"Greed > Murder." The Separatist ship offers some supplies if you let them live.
"Our desire to [survive] outweighs your desire to [kill] us. Let us go, please."
TEXT_DESTROYED_ZOLTAN: Another ship full of Zoltans has been reduced to scrap matter. You scrap their ship.
You hope the Zoltan Minister never catches wind of this, or the Federation will receive hell for breaking their truce.
It's no wonder the Duskbringers hate the Federation so much when you kill Zoltan ships with such gusto.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_ZOLTAN: As you scrap the now crewless ship, you wonder why you never steal the Zoltan shield tech from these ships.
Killing Zoltans is risky business, but you've made good work of this ship. The fruits of your labor are the excess of scrap material for you to take.
For a supposedly peaceful bunch, Zoltans are a risk to fight with. Luckily, you've emptied out this ship and can now scrap it.
TEXT_SURRENDER_ZOLTAN_GENERIC: The Zoltan ship has grown tired of fighting. They surrender.
"You have certainly reduced our defenses to nothing. All we have left is to ask for our lives."
The Zoltan ship is heavily damaged. They offer some goods if you'll let them live.
TEXT_SURRENDER_ZOLTAN_FAIR: "We know if the Federation catches wind of this, you will be tried for your crimes. We suggest an offer that is beneficial for both of us."
"Code 74F requires all trades made between ships to be mutually beneficial. We will not stray from the Zoltan law."
"This is not the way of peace. If you desire to ever know enlightenment, you must release us with a fair trade."
TEXT_DESTROYED_ZOLTAN_AUTO: In all likelihood, you've just caused some poor Zoltan bureaucrat to have to do a ton of paperwork. Still, at least nobody was aboard.
Zoltans don't take too kindly to their property being destroyed, but the alternative would be their own lives on the line. You don't feel too bad about it.
For the action of destroying a valuable Zoltan Auto-ship, you expect a stern lecture, a strongly worded letter, and a handful of scrap. Fortunately, you get the latter right away.
One fewer Zoltan Auto means that travel through this sector will be slightly more convenient for any random passer-by. You don't expect to hear any thanks from it, but the scrap is reward enough.
The AI core explodes into its constituent elements, which is a modest bounty. The Zoltans probably won't be pleased their resources are being reappropriated.
The Zoltan Auto-ship is no more. Whatever its task was before you blew it up, you're pretty sure the sector will get along fine without it.
TEXT_SURRENDER_MONK: "We hope you have grown as a person over the course of this battle and have decided to cease your attack against us."
"We pose no threat to you, and refuse to raise a hand against you. We hope you will reconsider your violent ways."
TEXT_DESTROYED_INFERNUM: The Monk cackles over the comm. "The fires have come!", as his ship explodes into large fragments. Fortunately, said fires have not diminished the value of its scrap.
The Infernum Monks seem oddly peaceful as their ship explodes into rich scrap. At least, peaceful compared to their usual bloodthirsty demeanor.
A final explosion cuts off the monk's laughter. The wreckage is treacherous, but lucrative.
Somehow, the Infernum's ships seem more explosive than most other Zoltan's ship. It's almost as if they deliberately set it to go off in a more impressive kaboom.
Even as you harvest the remains of the monks' ship, it continues to crackle with an unstable energy.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_INFERNUM: A dying monk sputters out some last words. "You are truly worthy!" Before completely destabilizing, the monk raises a finger pointing to the bounty of scrap in the hold.

Your crew enter the empty ship. next to the exploded corpse of one of its inhabitants, a final message is burned into the floor. "There is darkness, and yet there is light." Ignoring the message, you take what you can find.

The ship's powerful reactor can be felt through the walls and floor in an unsteady hum and crackle. While most factions build their ship to insulate the living space against the reactor's power, the Infernum do not.
The remains of the monks continue to burn and smolder as you strip the inside of their ship for valuables.
Death has finally quenched the monk's desire for violence. There is quite a lot of valuable resources to scrap.
TEXT_DESTROYED_DUSKBRINGER: Another ship full of Zoltans has been reduced to scrap matter. You scrap their ship.
You wonder what the Federation would think of you killing Duskbringers. You bet they would be pleased.
At last, the Duskbringer ship has been destroyed. There remains plenty for you to collect.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_DUSKBRINGER: The Duskbringer ship has been neutralized. One less ship full of angry Zoltans to harass the Federation.
The last of the Duskbringers aboard the ship have been reduced to ashes. You step carefully around the ship as you scrap it.
Aboard the Duskbringer ship you find many strange artifacts and Zoltan devices, but nothing that looks like you could use. You settle with scrapping the ship.
TEXT_ESCAPE_DUSKBRINGER: Duskbringers are no cowards, but sometimes running away suits them. This ship is trying to do just that.
The Duskbringer ship's engines are active and flaring even brighter. It's trying to escape!
TEXT_GOTAWAY_DUSKBRINGER: "This is not over, Federation! We will return even stronger and destroy you!"
The Duskbringer jumps away. You're disappointed, but at least you've seen the cowardly side of the Duskbringers.
TEXT_DESTROYED_DUSKBRINGER_STATION: Another station of Zoltans has been reduced to scrap matter. You scrap their remains.
You wonder what the Federation would think of you killing Duskbringers. You bet they would be pleased.
At last, the Duskbringer station has been destroyed. There remains plenty for you to collect.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_DUSKBRINGER_STATION: The Duskbringer station has been neutralized. One less structure full of angry Zoltans to harass the Federation.
The last of the Duskbringers aboard the station have been reduced to ashes. You step carefully around the corridors as you scrap it.
Aboard the Duskbringer station you find many strange artifacts and Zoltan devices, but nothing that looks like you could use. You settle with scrapping the hull.
TEXT_DESTROYED_ORCHID: How long does it take to build the massive, plantlike structures of the Orchid ships? You wonder how much of the Orchid's time and effort you have wasted.
You receive one final message as the Floral vessel breaks apart: "A blessed life beyond death awaits me... but it does not await you."
The dying Floral captain gives one last gesture with his vines. From what you can tell, it was the symbol for peace - one final, unsuccessful request for mercy.
The Orchid ship explodes, artificial plant matter twirling into space. You salvage everything that you think is scrap.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_ORCHID: The scent from the Orchids makes your crew dizzy. You try not to breathe as you scrap the ship.

While scrapping the Gathering vessel, you study the Titanwood worked dilligently into the hull. If you were able to extract it, it would be quite valuable on the market. Unfortunately, it's far too strong compared to any of your equipment.
For a species of fragile plants, the Orchids are remarkably adequate at fighting. Still, they stood no chance against your crew.

Partway through the salvage mission you have to send half of your crew back to the ship after they fall into a strange blissful state. Luckily, you're still able to finish salvaging in a reasonable amount of time.
TEXT_SURRENDER_ORCHID: The Florals almost immediately power down their weapons after having sustained heavy damage. Though they say nothing, you can only assume they're placing faith in you that you will do the same.

"It is a shame I am not as tied to my faith as I once was. Had I the assurance a blissful afterlife awaited me, perhaps this death would not bother me so much... But please, have mercy on me, captain. The Federation must stick together, or our unity will be for nothing!"
The Floral on screen frantically waves their leaves and hastily pecks away at the keyboard. You then receive a message full of typos: "we surender, please case fire!"

The Floral captain speaks hastily, clearly not used to having to use their vocals. "Please, Federation is great and I not like dying! Living is nice and so is friendship. We can be friends, and friends give good gifts and do not kill each other, yes?"

"You would not dare kill me, would you Renegade? I am no filthy Weedling, I'm a Floral. A honored member of this great Federation. What kind of soldier of a better galaxy would you be if you massacred your allies?"
TEXT_ESCAPE_ORCHID: You weren't even aware Orchid ships had protruding engines before now, as you watch them flare up. The ship is trying to escape!
Scans show increased activity in the Orchid ship's engines. They're trying to escape!
TEXT_GOTAWAY_ORCHID: Another elusive Orchid has gone away, and will no doubt report what has happened to other Orchid ships.
The Orchid ship jumps away. You've only managed to smear any trust the Orchids had for the Federation, and gotten nothing out of it.
TEXT_DESTROYED_VAMPWEED: The Vampweed captain salutes to his crew and accepts his fate. "At least I die a proud industrialist and democrat, and not a butcher for a corrupt bureaucracy! GLORY TO THE CONFEDERACY!"
Without any words, the Confederate vessel explodes. The possibly expensive factory cargo is jettisonned far out into the abyss out of reach, but at least you can scrap the debris.
"Noooo! I never even... got pollen on my pistil... Screw you, Renegade!"
With the death of this vessel, the workforce of the mighty Confederate economy is now a couple workers shorter.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_VAMPWEED: "They... were right... the Coalition was the only thing that could save us... and now it's too late..."

The halls of the once lively Vampweed vessel are now as silent as the living members of their Floral brethren. Perhaps there's something poetic to this, but you're here for scrap and not deeper meanings.
"I'm not a religious man, that's a greenleaf's thing... but when you're taking your last breath, it's a rather spiritual moment. God... I hope there isn't a hell..."

As you board the Vampweed vessel to scrap it, you find various propaganda and paraphernalia relating to the Coalition and the Confederacy. These guys were apparently radicals and nationalists, but in a court of law, you aren't sure that would hold as a defense on its own.
TEXT_SURRENDER_VAMPWEED: "Okay, okay! I've been hitting the liquor a bit hard and it made me act stupid. Maybe I have a problem. Look, if you spare me, I'll give you whatever I've got AND I promise I'll get help, okay? Deal?"

Out of breath, the Vampweed captain's petals are a bit singed at the tips. "If the Federation... truly represents peace as it claims... then I hope you will find it in you to spare me... despite my mistakes here today."
"You can't kill me, I'm a valued member of the industrial work force! If I'm not there screwing the cap onto every Kardoche fertilizer bottle, then who else will?!"

The Vampweed nods to you. "I... apologize for my rash behavior. I have made an ill decision in fighting you. This is the kind of behavior that caused the old war. I hope you have it in your heart to forgive me."

The Confederate captain falls to his knees, begging you for mercy. He apologizes on behalf of his entire species for their past mistakes and offers you all of this month's wages at his factory job in return for sparing him.
TEXT_DESTROYED_CRYSTAL: For all it's worth, the crystalline armor protecting their ship could not withstand the fire from your weapons.
Remarkably, the ruins of the Crystal ship could easily be mistaken as smaller Crystal ships. Glad you don't actually have more enemies to fight, you scrap your latest victim.
A few shards from the shattered armor almost hit your ship, but luckily you pilot out of the way just in time. You scrap what you can.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_CRYSTAL: With all their fancy abilities, the Crystals are still just as easy a kill for your crew as any other. You scrap the ship.
You wonder why the Rockmen worshipped the Crystals as gods when you can kill them with such ease.
The Crystal ship has been neutralized successfully. You scrap the remains.
TEXT_SURRENDER_CRYSTAL: "We yield, aliens. We have no wish to die fighting you."
"You have bested us! I will no longer underestimate you foreigners. Please, let us leave in peace."
They appear to be transmitting the universal signals for surrender. Will you let them go?
They message you, "I see now there was a misunderstanding and there is no need for more bloodshed. Will you forgive our lack of discretion?"
"We cannot beat you; we surrender. Surely there is mercy wherever you come from."
"Yes, you have proven that we made a mistake in leaving our sector. Luckily in our time here we've learnt scoundrels like you can be bought off with scrap."
The Crystal ship has stopped firing. It appears they are trying to surrender.
"Captain, I'm sure our differences can be settled over some scrap, yes? I have come to understand this is how things are done here."
"As much as I hate this, we are not in any condition to pretend we do not need to surrender. Will you allow us to live?"
TEXT_SURRENDER_CRYSTAL_NOREWARD: "Enough! You are indeed a threat! Prove to us you have mercy and let us go."
"Barbarian, infant-brained aliens! All you do is kill. Let us go at once."
The Crystal ship sends a brief, poorly translated message demanding that you let them go. No offer is attached.
TEXT_DESTROYED_CULTIST: Another ship full of angry Cultists has been removed from this plane of reality. Perhaps they're watching you now from whatever afterlife they've imagined for themselves.
The Cultist vessel has been destroyed. Just a couple hundred more to go...
As you watch the Cultist vessel explode, you can't help but wonder how they stole so many ships for their cult...
More Cultists down, but you suspect this will only put a small dent in whatever endless supply of ships these creeps must have.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_CULTIST: Another ship full of angry Cultists has been cleared from this plane of reality. Perhaps they're watching you now from whatever afterlife they've imagined for themselves.
The Cultist vessel has been neutralized. Just a couple hundred more to go...
As you watch the Cultist vessel drift away, you can't help but wonder how they stole so many ships for their cult...
More Cultists down, but you suspect this will only put a small dent in whatever endless supply of ships these creeps must have.

TEXT_SURRENDER_PIRATE: "Alright, you win! Here's some equipment from our stores. Leave us alone!"
The ship repeatedly hails you. It looks like they want to surrender.
"You are considerably more well-armed than I would have thought. We surrender."
They send you a message: "Your ship is surprisingly well equipped! Please take this and let us live."
"Please don't kill us. We will give you everything we have!"
They offer you some of their cargo if you let them live.
They offer to give you some of their goods if you don't destroy their ship.
You get a frantic message, "Take everything we have. Just don't kill us!"
"You have clearly bested us. We merely request our lives."
"You have made your point, we are beaten. Take these and leave us to our shame."
"Take everything we have and let's both forget this happened."
TEXT_DESTROYED_BROOD: Another ship full of crazy spider-obsessed lunatics down. You salvage the remains.
You wish the Militia would pay you for each one of these ships you kill, but at least the scrap matter is enough to satisfy you.
The Brood has been causing issues for the Militia in this sector by weaponizing the spiders. It won't be much, but the death of this ship will still help retake this territory.
You can't imagine it's a very prideful death dying amongst the corpses of dozens of spiders, but they chose the life of a pirate and you chose the life of killing them.
Another Brood vessel has met its untimely end at your hand. You give the orders to start the salvage operation.

TEXT_DESTROYED_HACKER: Another pestilent hacker ship has been destroyed. Their spoils are yours.
The bounty of the destroyed hacker ship is yours for the taking.
The hacker ship and its crew are no more. The scrap is yours.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_HACKER: Your slaughter of the hackers has proven very effective. If war crimes weren't a thing, it would be something you could brag about.
Another shipload of filthy hackers has proven inferior to you. Their ship is yours.
The hacker ship has been emptied of life signs. That'll show them who's boss.
No more lifeforms are detected on the hacker vessel.
TEXT_SURRENDER_HACKER: "Ahh, what an excellent fighter you have proven. How much ssscrap will it take to make you forget thisss ever happened?"
"Ok, you've made quite the messss over here. Will thisss assssuage your bloodlussst?"
The hackers desperately call for a ceasefire.
"Captain, perhapsss we are all being too hasssty. We don't want to go down thisss path, do we? We can be forgiving, and we hope you are too. Will thisss be enough to turn your back?"
TEXT_DESTROYED_MANTIS: The hull of the Mantis Ship no longer looks so threatening now that it has been destroyed. You scrap the remains.
You know that without ever knowing their names, you have just avenged hundreds of innocent people by destroying this ship.
The Mantis ship is no more, except as scrap for you to take.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_MANTIS: The Mantis threat aboard the ship has been exterminated. Pleased with your work, you treat yourself to the remains of their ship.
The corpses of the Mantis crew litter the halls, and the stench of pheromones hangs in the air. You try not to breathe as you scrap the ship.
Despite the Mantis being fearsome warriors, they were no match for your ship.
TEXT_DESTROYED_FREEMANTIS: The hull of the Free Mantis ship rends and buckles as it is torn apart. As you scrap their ship, you reflect that this relatively young faction is not ready for what it takes to be at war.

As awful as it feels, sometimes there's no good option. Destroying a ship full of supposed allies isn't something you're proud of - but your mission comes first, and there was no other choice. You prepare to scrap the ship.
Considering how most Free Mantis want to join the Federation, something feels off about destroying one of their vessels. Hopefully the Warlords will understand what you had to do.
You wonder, if the Free Mantis here knew the importance of the mission, would there even have been a fight? Their scrap is still useful, all the same.
Some day, the Free Mantis may join the Federation. Hopefully they will not hold this incident against you when they do.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_FREEMANTIS: Whether it had to be this way or not, circumstances led you to eliminating the Free Mantis crew. You might as well scrap their ship and make sure your mission is a success in the meantime.

It's easy to feel guilty when all you're left with is corpses, but you know you didn't have any choice. You regret the loss of life, but not what you've done. The scrap from stripping the ship doesn't hurt either.
The Free Mantis put up a bloody fight, even against their desired allies. However, it was a fight you were more than capable of winning.
Although the aftermath of a Free Mantis fight is much like a Hive Mantis fight, it feels different to scrap a ship that could have, under different circumstances, been friendly.
The stench of synthetic pheromones linger as you scrap the derelict Free Mantis ship. Hopefully you won't have to fight many more of these.
TEXT_SURRENDER_FREEMANTIS: The Free Mantis captain limps into the range of the camera. "We don't understand. Federation supposed to be good persons..."
Mantis don't usually show weakness in combat, but the Free Mantis ship is asking if you will accept their surrender.
"We thought Free Mantis and Federation allies. Kill us, and you are breaking trust."
The Free Mantis seem less willing to fight. Their captain hails you, offering to call a ceasefire.
"Our clan surely exile us for cowardice, but please, let us live."
The battered ship contacts you out of desperation. The captain reminds you of their truce with the Federation, requesting you to call off your attack.
The Free Mantis ship tries desperately to contact you. You suspect they're trying to surrender.
"Ok, we raise the flag of white. Let us live, we beg."
The Free Mantis ship repeatedly attempts to hail you. You open up your comms only to be greeted with panicked proposals of surrender for resources, with the crackling of fire mixed in.
You hear the Free Mantis captain scrambling as he hails you. "Alright, alright!" He offers a selection of resources in exchange for his ship's survival.
The Free Mantis ship hails you. "We beg mercy. It is not Mantis custom to forgive, but we hope it is for you."
TEXT_DESTROYED_ROCK: By destroying this ship, you have indeed proven yourself a threat to the Rockmen's ways.
The Rockmen may not be sworn enemies of the Federation, but you still feel no guilt about destroying this ship. Mostly.
At last, the armor of the Rock ship gives out, and a mighty explosion tears the ship apart.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_ROCK: The interior of the Rock ship is littered with small stones. You all know where they came from, but no one dares comment on it as you salvage the ship.
You've successfully killed the Rock crew, and their scrap is left as yours for the taking.
You can't imagine it looks good on the Federation when you keep removing Rock ships like this, but at this point you're past caring.
TEXT_SURRENDER_ROCK_GENERIC: The Rock ship hails: "Enough! We were told aliens were a threat to our ways, and you have proved as much. Take this and leave us in peace."
Their systems suffering, the Rock ship attempts to make contact: "Alien vessel. Cease your attack. We will pay."
The Rock ship moves into a defensive position and transmits a white flag signal. They seem willing to buy their lives.
TEXT_DESTROYED_ROCK_STATION: By destroying this station, you have indeed proven yourself a threat to the Rockmen's ways.
The Rockmen may not be sworn enemies of the Federation, but you still feel no guilt about destroying their infrastructure. Mostly.
At last, the armor of the Rock station gives out, and a mighty explosion tears the structure apart.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_ROCK_STATION: The interior of the Rock station is littered with small stones. You all know where they came from, but no one dares comment on it as you salvage your spoils.
You've successfully killed the Rock crew, and their scrap is left as yours for the taking.
You can't imagine it looks good on the Federation when you confront Rockmen in such manner, but at this point you're past caring.
TEXT_SURRENDER_ROCK_STATION: The Rock station hails: "Enough! We were told aliens were a threat to our ways, and you have proved as much. Take this and leave us in peace."
Their systems suffering, the Rock station attempts to make contact: "Alien vessel. Cease your attack. We will pay."
The Rock station, realising it has been outgunned, transmits a white flag signal. They seem willing to buy their lives.
TEXT_DESTROYED_OUTCAST: Outcasts aren't quite the same threat as your ordinary pirates, but that doesn't mean they weren't a threat. Probably.

Exploring the wreckage reveals various colorful murals painted on the walls of the hull. Some are quite touching, but others depict violent and brutal murder. Maybe it's a good thing these guys are dead now.
As the outcasts live their final moments, you receive one last message. "At least... this is better than the coal mines..."
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_OUTCAST: Outcasts aren't quite the same threat as your ordinary pirates, but that doesn't mean they weren't a threat. Probably.

Exploring the wreckage reveals various colorful murals painted on the walls of the hull. Some are quite touching, but others depict violent and brutal murder. Maybe it's a good thing these guys are dead now.
As the outcasts live their final moments, you receive one last message. "At least... this is better than the coal mines..."
TEXT_SURRENDER_OUTCAST_GENERIC: "Hah! What a riot - we were told the Federation fought to protect the galaxy from oppression. Not only have you turned your back to the Theocracy, but you've committed to annihilating our people! Prove you know mercy and let us go."
"The Theocracy has told many lies - but they were telling the truth when they told us Renegades made dangerous foes! You win, accept this surrender and let us live!"
"Our greatest mistake was to match you here - but please! Let us live on to learn from this mistake. We outcasts have only just tasted freedom, it would be a shame to die so soon."
It appears the crew of the Outcast ship have hastily painted themselves white, desperately trying to convey their sudden declaration of surrender. Will you accept?
TEXT_DESTROYED_SLUG: For all the Slugs' efforts, they were not able to defeat you. The victor of this battle, you indulge yourself by scrapping their ship.
The Slug ship is no more. You scrap the wreckage.
At last, the traitorous nebula-dwellers have been silenced. You scrap the ship.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_SLUG: You find the gasping corpse of the Slug Captain quivering on the ground. He utters one last word, "Sssshit", then collapses and dies.
You feel no remorse for the Slug crew, though you do wish their ship smelled better.
The interior of the ship is now coated in what appears to be a mixture of slime and mashed up Slug intestines. Yuck.
TEXT_SURRENDER_SLUG_GENERIC: The Slug captain hails you. "Oh, your highnessss, you are ssso brave and truly the greatessst warrior to have ever lived. Will you ssspare ussssss, so that we may sssshare your tale?"
"Ok, I ssssee no reassson to lie right now. We're kinda ssssscrewed unlesssss you let usss go. We'll give you sssome junk if you agree."
Slugs are known for their cowardice, and as expected the Slug ship here has given up and surrendered.
"Dear godsss, I did not expect thisss! I applaud you for the sssuprissse. Now let ussss go."
TEXT_DESTROYED_CLAN: The proud Clansmen and their ship have been destroyed. Though their many trophies have been purged along with them, at least you can salvage the scrap from their ship.
The Guild probably won't appreciate you killing off their members, but what are they going to do about it? You scrap the ship.
You've no doubt avenged the souls of many innocent lives who were hunted down by these Clansmen. Plus, you get some scrap out of it.

While the ship explodes, you try to think of a clever bit of wordplay to describe the situation. You decide to go with "The hunters become the hunted" before you snap out of it and give orders to scrap the wreckage.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_CLAN: The captain of the Slug vessel coughs as he bleeds out on the floor. He looks you in the eyes one last time, mouths the words "Damn you", and dies.
You've taken out the crew of the Slug vessel. These Clansmen might make good fighters, but they didn't stand a chance against you.
The Guild probably won't appreciate you killing off their members, but what are they going to do about it? You scrap the ship.
You try to think of a clever bit of word play to describe the situation. You decide to go with "The hunters become the hunted" before you snap out of it and give orders to scrap the wreckage.
TEXT_SURRENDER_CLAN_GENERIC: "We will never ssssurrender!" Shouts the Clansman, right as your shot scatters across their hull. "Uhhhh, ssscratch that. How much for you to let ussss go?"
It appears the Clansmen have given up. "Agggh, ssstop! Take all this sssscrap, let ussss go!"
You spot an alert on your computer screen. Upon opening it, you're greeted by a video feed of the Clansmen waving literal white flags towards the camera.
TEXT_DESTROYED_HEKTAR: As the Hektar ship breaks apart, you can't help but wonder if their ships were designed to be as easy to put together as their weapons.

The Hektar ship explodes, and an automatic message is sent out to your ship. "Hektar Industries applauds you for your success in combat. Before you can scrap our ship however, we request you watch this short ad..."

A plethora of boxes come flying out of the cargo bay of the other ship. You consider grabbing some, but the pictures on the side suggest they aren't worth your time. What is two circles and an oval even supposed to mean?
You receive one last hail from the Hektar Captain as his ship is plunged into flames. "I wasssn't paid enough to sssay sssomething clever. But if my manager assksss, pretend I did-"
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_HEKTAR: "God... damn... it... I didn't even get thisss week'sss pay check yet..."
In his final moments, the Slug captain shrugs. "Better then having to go back to the call center I guesssss."
"Gaahhhh, sssso much for that healthcare..." The Slug slumps over dead and you scrap his ship.
As you walk amongst the corpses of the Slugs, you catch the final words of one last survivor; "Bury me with my money..." Unfortunately for him, you have other plans on what to do with it.
TEXT_SURRENDER_HEKTAR_GENERIC: "You know what? Thissss job wassssn't worth it anywayssss. I am formally resssigning. You wouldn't kill an innocent unemployed civilian now, would you?"
"Capitalissssm hasss failed me! I ssshall forever now be communissst. Bribery and communisssm are sssynonymousss, right?"
"Who'sss paying you for thisss? I refusssse to believe you aren't in thisss for money. Well guesss what! I have money too!"
The Hektar employee frantically flips through his employee manual. "Crap, it doesssn't sssay anything about what to do here! Uh, time to resssort to plan B. Buy my way out!"
TEXT_DESTROYED_LEECH: Sound does not travel through space, so you are only left to wonder what sound the Leech ship's crew made as they're blown to smitherenes.
Moments before the Leech ship is destroyed, you feel as if the ship's residents have made one final, potent sigh as they accept their fate.
If the legends of the once great Leech military were ever true, they certainly don't hold up today. For your sake, let's hope they never make a resurgence.
If you keep destroying Leech ships, maybe they'll give up and leave you alone for good. It's probably too much to hope for, but it's not impossible either.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_LEECH: The scene left from the massacre here is far from a pretty one. The diced up bits of Leech flesh let off a repugnant odor so foul you almost consider leaving the wreck behind entirely. Almost.
You've heard the disturbing stories of the haunting post-mortem smiles of Leech crew. However, it would seem that those stories are mere legends, as their faces look roughly how you'd expect.
You experience no further resistance as you scrap their ship. There's a lingering feeling that there may be a survivor hidden onboard, but they do not stop you from taking whatever salvage you find.

Walking among the corpses of these parasites is nothing short of eerie. Their wide gaping mouths seem as if they could reach out at any moment and strike you. You keep your hand near your blaster at all times as you scrap the ship.

Apparently, shortly after death, the corpse of a Leech will drain itself slowly of all the built up electricity it has stored over its life. With this many bodies, it could be catastrophic in close quarters. You make sure to hurry and scrap the ship before you can get caught in a mine field of electrified bodies.
TEXT_SURRENDER_LEECH_GENERIC: "Oooh, woe is me. The end of days is upon us! Why do we even try..." The Leech ship hopes you'll take pity on them.
The Leech captain regurgitates several mounds of white cloth. You're disgusted and confused for a few moments until you realize this is a convoluted attempt to "raise the white flag".
You aren't surprised the Leech captain appears to have given up so easily. They aren't exactly known for their loyalty or commitment. The question is, will you spare them?

The Leech captain burps loudly, specks of bile landing on their camera. Repulsive, but according to your captain's handbook this is one of the many ways the Leeches will offer their surrender to enemy captains.
"We will never surrender! Eargen forever- aaaaactually, nevermind. We surrender. I don't want to die."
The enemy's captain appears to be waving frantically with his tongue "hands". Looks like he's trying to get your attention to surrender.
TEXT_DESTROYED_SHELL: The Shell ship explodes, sending clouds of poisonous gas out into space. Hopefully there are no stations with open airlocks nearby...
Despite all their defensive measures, the Shell ship has been defeated. You scrap the remains.
The Shells are known for their well-maintained defenses, but your weaponry has proven effective once again.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_SHELL: Fighting Shells is dangerous considering how well protected they are, but you've cleared the ship of crew. Their scrap is yours.
The Shell ship has been neutralized. You scrap the ship.
TEXT_SURRENDER_SHELL: "Please, you are too strong! We do not want to fight! Let us live!"
Unlike their Slug cousins, Shells aren't very greedy. They'd much rather pay some scrap instead of dying. Will you accept their offer?
You receive a hail from the Shell captain. "Yes yes, your guns are very good. Let us go, we have scrap!"
TEXT_DESTROYED_MORPH: The grey vessel is engulfed in an orange glow, its bland hull going up in flames that are quickly extinguished by the vacuum of space.

The likely fact you just blew up, not only a crew of many Morphs, but one massive Morph as well is a weird one to grasp. You wonder if the scrap metal from the wreckage will Morph back into enemies, or stay lifeless.

You wonder if the Morphs felt pain as their ship just imploded. You hope not, but only because you can never be sure if these things are really dead, and you'd hate for them to come back to haunt you later.
Another mysterious ship full of Morphs down. You salvage the wreckage.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_MORPH: The gibberish spewing blobs have been brought to an untimely end. You scrap their ship.
The concept that your crew are now standing inside a giant Morph itself while scrapping the ship is somewhat unsettling, but you bury your concerns and order your crew to hurry up.
The grey stains of once sentient goop mark the walls of the ship, scattered about during the fight. You can only hope they won't animate once again and attack you while salvaging.
As you scrap the Morph ship, you wonder if those strange gray blobs can feel pain, and if their final moments were in agony. Honestly, you still aren't sure if they're sapient.
TEXT_SURRENDER_MORPH: "Kip kip joo! Urg la yoo purl yu!" You think the Morphs are surrendering, but you aren't sure. How do you respond?
"Oj joo! Oj joo! Yur kip looloo!" You think the Morphs are surrendering, but you aren't sure. How do you respond?
"Odle yup. Kim jio kup kurp!" You think the Morphs are surrendering, but you aren't sure. How do you respond?
TEXT_DESTROYED_COALITION: The Coalition ship explodes. As the separate pieces float away, you can once again see the divide between the factions. You like it better this way.
The Coalition doesn't mess around, but yet again you've come out on top. The remains of their ship are yours to scrap.
You've proven that no one, Rebel or Coalition, can outmatch you. Or at least, this ship couldn't.
The Coalition vessel is blasted apart from your assault. With the destruction of this ship, humans can hopefully rest a little easier.
The enemy ship crumbles into its constituent pieces. The combined ingenuity of the Federation's enemies fortunately results in a ship that is quite profitable to scrap.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_COALITION: A mixture of all different kinds of alien blood is on your hands. No wonder they must all hate the Federation.
The Coalition is made of some of the most fearsome warrior races, but your crew has proven themselves superior.
A cornucopia of Coalition corpses cover the floor. There's nothing to stop you from harvesting their vessel and venturing forth.
The Coalition has been known to boast their physical strength in comparison to the Federation, but your crew was more than equipped to prove that they are not to be trifled with.
Both the Federation and Coalition believe that diversity is strength. As their ship is the one that's devoid of life, you've proven that yours is stronger.
TEXT_SURRENDER_COALITION: The captain of the Coalition ship hails you, and begrudgingly requests that you accept their surrender.
You can tell it's hard for the Coalition captain to admit, but they have been bested. They offer a surrender.
TEXT_DESTROYED_GHOST: It is hard to draw the line between the original state of disrepair the vessel was in and the destruction you have caused. You add to the damage even further by scrapping the ship.
The Ghost ship is no more. You scrap what you can.
The circle of life for this ship has been complete. Now finally destroyed, as it should have been originally, you scrap what remains.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_GHOST: You have emptied the ship of its ghostly captors. No longer shall they prey on innocent ships passing through this sector.
It dawns on you that twice now the entire crew of this ship has been exterminated. The thought chills you as you scrap it.
Now empty of crew, you make sure to thoroughly scrap the ruins so that no more Ghosts can ever inhabit this ship.
TEXT_DESTROYED_DYNASTY: The Dynasty's architects probably cringe every time they catch news another one of their ships have been destroyed. Their fleets have been reduced ever since the great cataclysm of their past, and you certainly aren't helping.
The vibrant blue lights on the Dynasty vessel flicker in their final moments before the brilliant blue glow ceases and the integrity of the ship's hull crumbles.

If every Federation ship removed Dynasty vessels with the same level of efficiency as you, it would be no wonder that they hate you all! However, from your experience, it doesn't seem there are many competent captains out there to explain the phenomenon.

You catch a glimpse of glittering wisps of color floating out of the hull as it collapses. Have the Ghosts escaped their horrible fate, or is this merely the equivalent of a corpse being flung out into the cosmos? You really aren't sure.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_DYNASTY: You've heard that the Ghosts have a most horrible odour to them, and you couldn't be more glad there's no air inside the Dynasty ship to carry the scent as you scrap it.
You wonder if Ghosts feel pain before they die. After what just happened here, you sincerely hope they don't.
"Arg, see to it that you are penetrated up the rectum, you foul wretch," mutters the Ghost captain as he begins to dissipate.

You remember a time on your MV Traveler handbook that recommended to not bother with the effort of killing Ghosts while preserving their vessel. But look at you now! If only the people back at Universe 0 could see the havoc you caused.
TEXT_DESTROYED_LANIUS: One can never be too cautious while scrapping a Lanius ship, for fear of either a lone survivor drifting in the vacuum or a collision with the sharp debris.
The destruction of the Lanius vessel provides you with great satisfaction, knowing how infamously difficult the Lanius are as foes.
The Lanius may be excellent scavengers, but today you've turned the tables on them.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_LANIUS: It's difficult to scrap the oxygenless interiors of the Lanius ship, but you can manage. Nothing will keep you from your precious scrap, not even the cruel vacuum of space.

Without crew on board to disturb you, you can truly appreciate the intricacies of Lanius architecture. Sure, it looks like a bunch of kitchen knives duct-taped together, but anything can be art with the right attitude.
With the crew of the Lanius ship dead, nothing prevents you from tearing apart the hull of their ship.
TEXT_SURRENDER_LANIUS: An image of a silent Lanius captain appears on your monitor. Images of their well-filled cargo hold follow. You come to the conclusion that they are trying to barter for a cease-fire.
The Lanius ship hails you. Your translator struggles, spurting out "Prevent death... Merciful... Penitent...". You believe they are surrendering.
You receive a hail from the ship followed by a crude translation device spurting, "Stop. Stop. Stop."
You receive an image of their captain, silhouetted by the destruction aboard their ship. It bows forward with the metallic appendages about its body doing the same. It appears to be requesting mercy.
Your comms system receives a video feed of the enemy ship's crew waving small makeshift white flags. It appears they have taken research about your culture's customs quite literally.
You receive a message from the enemy ship that your translator struggles to interpret, "Penitence for metal. Offering intention."
You receive a one word message from the enemy ship, "Surrender." You assume they are asking to surrender rather than demanding your surrender.
TEXT_DESTROYED_AUGMENTED: One can never be too cautious while scrapping a Lanius ship, for fear of either a lone survivor drifting in the vacuum or a collision with the sharp debris.
The destruction of the Lanius vessel provides you with great satisfaction, knowing how infamously difficult the Lanius are as foes.
The Lanius may be excellent scavengers, but today you've turned the tables on them.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_AUGMENTED: It's difficult to scrap the oxygenless interiors of the Lanius ship, but you can manage. Nothing will keep you from your precious scrap, not even the cruel vacuum of space.

Without crew on board to disturb you, you can truly appreciate the intricacies of Lanius architecture. Sure, it looks like a bunch of kitchen knives duct-taped together, but anything can be art with the right attitude.
With the crew of the Lanius ship dead, nothing prevents you from tearing apart the hull of their ship.
TEXT_DESTROYED_ANCIENT: You have rid the galaxy of another Obelisk ship. There's bound to be hundreds more, but it's something.
The Obelisk ship explodes into many smaller pieces, its cubical shape shattered forever. It's oddly satisfying, and you reflect fondly on your handiwork as you scrap the remains.
Though you know the Obelisks are the antagonists of this galaxy, you can't help but wonder if every ship you kill was aware of their grand scheme.
With every Obelisk ship you destroy, you delay the date of the invasion just a little bit more. You know it's not much, but it feels important to you.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_ANCIENT: As the last Obelisk collapses, it lets out two last words. "Screw... you..."
You've made quick work of these cubical aliens. You don't feel the pang of guilt that usually accompanies these murders - for the most part.
The interior of the Obelisk ship is littered with the dust of the fallen crew. You call it a job well done and give the orders to scrap the ship.
The death of the Obelisk ship and its crew means good news for the rest of the galaxy. You just hope they don't have any families to grieve them.
TEXT_FILLER_FREE: You arrive in a system and immediately discover a pirate ship nearby. Strangely, scans indicate there are no lifeforms aboard. You salvage anything useful, but find no clue as to the whereabouts of the former crew.
Not much remains in this abandoned system; however, scans reveal a nearby mining platform with some salvageable materials.

You receive a message from a nearby station, "A Federation cruiser jumping into Rebel territory? Quite the bold move." You quickly move to arm the weapons but he continues, "Lucky for you we're not all in support of the Rebellion. Perhaps these supplies will help you get to friendlier space alive."
You happen upon the remains of a space station. It has been mostly picked clean but there appears to be a few materials that will aid you in your mission.
TEXT_FILLER_DRONE: When you ask a nearby station for aid, a friendly programmer gives you the schematics for a drone!
An abandoned space station circles a lonely planet. A quick check yields schematics for a drone. You bring it aboard the ship.
Federation sympathizers contact you as you arrive. "We know your mission should be secret, so don't ask how we know about it. Take this schematic, it's all we can do to help."

A small Engi research vessel is trying to fend off a Mantis ship. You move in to engage, but after a quick scan of your ship the Mantis ship retreats. The Engi offer you a drone schematic as thanks for your timely arrival.
You find an abandoned mining station on a nearby moon. A quick scan shows no life forms; however, you discover a usable drone schematic!
You receive a wide-band message, "Free schematic samples! Be sure to visit our new military-grade drone store opening in sector XR1-45!"
TEXT_FILLER_WEAPON: As soon as you arrive a small Mantis ship detaches from a wreck and jumps away. You must have interrupted their salvage operation because you find a weapon ready to be installed!
A small merchant ship messages you, "Underground Federation comm channels are all talking about your 'secret' mission. Let us install a weapon to help. Good luck!"
Debris from a battle is scattered around this system. A few pieces bounce against your ship. You passively scan them and discover there is a functioning weapon among them!
TEXT_FILLER_UPGRADES: "You look like a military vessel. We're trying to get back to our homes alive. I'm an engineer by trade and could try to improve your reactor if you have any extra supplies."
You receive a message from a small convoy. They're looking for some military supplies and are offering to try to improve your reactor in exchange.
TRADER_CIV: The beacon at first glance seems home to a junk yard. Upon closer inspection, it reveals itself to be a ramshackle market. One trader has a deal that catches your eye.
TAVERN_HIRE_TEXT: You find a space station set up for travelers. Browsing through its listings, you find a tavern full of mercenaries for hire. You look for potential crewmembers.
There are a number of ships stationed around a rest stop. You immediately receive a message saying, "If you're looking for some bodies to fill your ship, you've come to the right place!"
This beacon seems to serve as a meeting place for local traffic. It seems you can find crew willing to fight on your ship here... for a price.
FILLER_WRECKAGE_TEXT: What at first seems to be a simple nebula is actually filled with a good amount of debris from a brutal exchange between several ships. Wreckage drifts by your screens and tumbles into the depths of the nebula to be lost to sight. It's hard to determine who the combatants were without closer investigation.

You have jumped into the aftermath of what seems to have been a brutal exchange between several ships. Wreckage drifts by your screens, and you can still see the remains of the dying ships sparking and breaking apart. It's hard to determine who the combatants were without closer investigation.
FILLER_TERRAFORMING_SCAN_TEXT: You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team C12 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team F17 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team A50-3 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
