You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team Z9 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team T6 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team R11 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
You receive a hail from a station orbiting a nearby planet. "Captain, we are Federation Terraforming Team W8-2 and are in need of assistance. Do you have some time?"
TEXT_FILLER_GHOSTSHIP: This beacon lies in an empty section of space. You almost move on before spotting a heavily damaged ship drifting nearby.
You share this beacon with just one other ship, but it appears long since abandoned.

Another ship is jumping away just as you arrive. They send out a quick communication before their jump completes: "That ruined bulk is more trouble than it's worth." You see a drifting, abandoned vessel nearby.
There's a heavily damaged ship at this beacon. You briefly pick up a very distorted communication from the ship but are unable to understand it. Your sensors detect no life-signs.
FILLER_EMPTY_STATION_TEXT: You find a small space station that appears to abandoned.
You arrive to find what appears to be a colonized moon, however scans show it has been abandoned. You also detect an abandoned space station near the Beacon.
This area shows signs of a battle some time ago. There are scattered remains of ships but one station appears to be intact.
FILLER_REBEL_CHECKPOINT_TEXT: It looks like this Beacon is home to a Rebel checkpoint. They're stopping and searching any ship that passes through. Civilians are being harassed, and Federation members are detained. The Rebels haven't noticed you yet.
Another Rebel checkpoint is monitoring this location. A number of civilian ships are awaiting inspection, any of them could be Federation loyalists. The Rebels haven't noticed you yet.

A Rebel space station and single fighter is monitoring this Beacon for Federation activity. A number of civilian ships are docked, awaiting inspection by the Rebels and possible detainment if they are Federation loyalists. The Rebels haven't noticed you yet.
A rather large fleet of civilian ships are held up at this Beacon. It appears to be a Rebel checkpoint; everyone is being inspected for possible ties to the Federation. No one has noticed you yet.
FILLER_REBEL_BRIBE_TEXT: These Rebels are easily swayed by the prospect of additional scrap. They release the civilian ships and everyone is free to go.
Like most Rebels, these are just men trying to get by in a rough galaxy. They take your scrap and let everyone continue their journeys.
As everyone currently awaiting inspection is human anyway, the Rebels let them go. They take your scrap and tell you to hurry along.
They eagerly accept your bribe, obviously revolutionaries are under paid. The civilian ships all begin to jump away.
GENERIC_HIDE_TEXT: Fly behind a moon and stay hidden.
Shut down all non-vital systems and stay hidden.
Stay quiet and hope they don't notice you.
Stay out of their way and charge your FTL drive.
FILLER_REBEL_HELPERS_TEXT: You stumble across a Rebel ship distributing supplies to local civilian colonies. It's probably not anything military grade, but every little bit helps...
You find a Rebel combat ship that has been reassigned as an emergency supply vessel. The local civilians are apparently in need of help, and the Rebels are rising to the occasion.
The Rebels in this system are doing supply runs for the local space stations. These civilians have likely been out of supply for months due to the war and are in desperate need.
Civilian colonists loyal to the Rebel cause are present on a nearby planet. It looks like they are currently receiving a supply shipment. Could be useful.

Because of the war, thousands of colonists have had their supply lines disrupted and have found themselves in dire straits. It seems in this system, the Rebels are sympathetic and are distributing what little supplies they can spare.
FILLER_REBEL_HELPER_NO_SUPPLIES_TEXT: You make to preparations to leave. One of the civilian leaders contacts you: "That Rebel was our sole source of supplies. You have doomed us all."
You leave the civilians with the supplies, though without the Rebel that was running supplies to them its unlikely they'll live long.
You wonder if any more Rebels will be available to help these civilians on the edge of nowhere. Oh well, for you a few more dead Rebels matter more than the lives of a thousand colonists.

Before your FTL drive charges, you receive a hail: "My son was on that ship. He only helped the Rebels because they cared enough to help us. Without him to find us supplies, we'll likely be forgotten and die out here."
FILLER_ROGUE_REBEL_TEXT: You arrive at a beacon located in a civilian star system. A nearby colony contacts you: "We've got a rogue Rebel ship harassing this system. Do you have time to find it?"
As soon as you arrive, you receive a Federation encrypted message: A Rebel ship has been terrorizing the local civilians in this system, please seek and destroy it.
You begin charging your FTL drive, and do a quick scan of a local planet. You find the ruins of a recently destroyed Federation colony of the surface. There must be a Rebel ship in the vicinity...

You jump into a field of debris. It appears a battle recently took place here, and the loser seems to have been a civilian ship. A message was left on repeat before it was destroyed: "Rebels attacking, please send aid!" The responsible Rebels are likely still nearby.
TEXT_FILLER_DISTRESS_COMBAT: Upon arriving at this beacon, you detect a distress call. Local scans reveal that a Federation transport is under attack from a Rebel scout!

You immediately notice a Rebel ship chasing what appears to be a civilian transport. However you are detecting chatter on an encrypted Federation channel... That transport is carrying Federation loyalists!
Your sensors are picking up a distress call on an encrypted Federation channel. You eventually find a Federation scout being chased by a Rebel fighter!
TEXT_DISTRESS_FRIENDLY: "Greetings! It is so good to see you! We've been out of fuel and floating out here for weeks. We were terrified a pirate or those damn Rebels would find us first. Could you spare some fuel?"
You arrive to find a ship floating among some debris. "Hello. Our impulse drives are shot and we can't jump. Could you give us some fuel?"
A small civilian ship flies over as soon as you arrive. You're prepared to fight but they just inform you that they're out of FTL fuel and can't jump.

"Hello. We used our last FTL fuel to jump to this station." They indicate a burnt out husk of debris and warped metal. "As you can see the war must have spread to this sector. We've been stranded ever since."
The ship emitting the distress beacon messages you, "Sorry to bother you, but we're out of fuel and can't get out of this barren sector. Could you help us out?
FUEL_FLEET_DELAY_LIST: As you are keeping a low profile, you're certain that the Rebel fleet is having a hard time tracking your ship.
Since your distress beacon has not been activated, you feel confident that the Rebel fleet is having difficulty tracking you. It should buy you a little time.
Long range scanners indicate the Rebel fleet has temporarily paused its advance on your position. Your decision to leave the distress beacon deactivated was farsighted.
Scanners show that the Rebel fleet has ceased its pursuit for a short time.
Your intuition as captain is telling you that the Rebels are having a hard time trying to find your ship.
Without a distress beacon or any FTL signatures to trace, you're sure that the Rebels are struggling to find you. You can only hope their confusion lasts until more fuel can be found.
The Rebel fleet seems to be unable to locate your ship's signature. If only you could get some fuel, you might still have a chance to place some distance between you and them...
FUEL_NOTHING_LIST: No ship is in scanning range and no one arrives at the beacon.
Your waiting yields nothing while the fleet surely gets closer...
A freighter suddenly arrives nearby. They are so close you can almost wave at them, but your hails are ignored and the ship quickly jumps away.
Small traffic passes within a short distance of you, but no one responds to your hails.
The only ship within hailing range appears to be a civilian vessel. However, it quickly leaves once it picks up your signal.
As you wait, a small asteroid storm pelts softly against your shields and hull.
You begin to wonder if turning on the beacon would be worth the risk of detection. The fleet slowly approaches.
You contemplate the vastness of space.
The prolonged wait in empty space is causing tension among the crew. Still no contact.
Cabin fever begins to spread among your crew.
Long range scanners detect a small settlement, but they refuse all contact.
FUEL_TRADER_TEXT_LIST: A merchant ship jumps into the sector and you quickly hail them asking for help. They respond, "Perhaps we could work out an exchange..."
A number of ships pass through the sector. You relay your message to each, and one finally responds. "I can't help much right now but perhaps we can trade."

A nearby settlement sends a small ship in your direction. It keeps its distance and hails you, "We can give you fuel for a price. Just don't even think of doing anything rash. We've got a teleporter at our base and a squad ready to defend us."
A large caravan of merchant ships jumps to a location near your position. Sensing an opportunity, one ship breaks off from the fleet to offer you an exchange.
A modified YT-1300 freighter jumps to an area near your sector. Your gut tells you these people are smugglers, but they seem to be feeling altruistic and present an offer of assistance.
FUEL_FLEET_DISTRESS_LIST: As you are keeping a low profile, you're certain that the Rebel fleet is having a hard time tracking your ship.
Since your distress beacon has not been activated, you feel confident that the Rebel fleet is having difficulty tracking you. It should buy you a little time.
Long range scanners indicate the Rebel fleet has temporarily paused its advance on your position. Your decision to leave the distress beacon deactivated was farsighted.
Scanners show that the Rebel fleet has ceased its pursuit for a short time.
Your intuition as captain is telling you that the Rebels are having a hard time trying to find your ship.
Without a distress beacon or any FTL signatures to trace, you're sure that the Rebels are struggling to find you. You can only hope their confusion lasts until more fuel can be found.
The Rebel fleet seems to be unable to locate your ship's signature. If only you could get some fuel, you might still have a chance to place some distance between you and the Rebels...
FUEL_NOTHING_DISTRESS_LIST: You contemplate that it is fortunate the ship's life support system does not rely on FTL fuel cells.
Nothing happens. Your calls go unanswered.
The distress beacon's light is the only movement visible outside the ship.
No ships jump into the sector...
A few passing ships seem oblivious to your distress call and ignore all hails.
A few civilian ships are within scanning range, yet none respond to your calls.
No ships pass through the area.
FUEL_TRADER_DISTRESS_MV_TEXT_LIST: A merchant ship jumps into the sector, obviously responding to your ship's distress beacon. They hail you offering a trade for fuel.
A ship arrives at the beacon. "We noticed your distress signal. I assume you're out of fuel? We're a bit low ourselves but perhaps we can make a trade."
A ship traveling near the beacon approaches your ship and hails you. "Out of fuel? This is a good opportunity for both of us... Care to trade?"
A mercenary ship arrives at the beacon. "We have a bit of extra fuel we can give you... for a price."
FUEL_ON_REBEL_ATTACK: A Rebel ship hails you, "Hello citizen. We are responding to your distress call and can assist... Wait a second... You're that ship! Prepare to die!"

A Rebel ship jumps nearby, "I wasn't looking forward to patrolling this boring sector but here you are, the most wanted ship in the area, just asking for me to find you. It looks like it's my lucky day!" They power up their weapons.
Your distress beacon must be working because a ship just jumped nearby. You run a scan on it and activate a red alert. It's a Rebel fighter!
A Rebel ship jumps in and hails you, "I knew you would slip up some time. Surrender quietly!"
FUEL_ON_MANTIS_ATTACK: A Mantis ship hails you, "Looks like found poor fools needing help. Come brothers, let's 'help' them!" They move in to attack.
Before long a ship jumps nearby, no doubt responding to your beacon. However any relief you felt disappears as soon as you recognize that the ship is of Mantis design. Prepare for a fight.

You detect a Mantis ship approaching and hack into their comm channel and hear, "...hope put up more of fight than last Federation ship. This has been disappointing day so far." Looks like they're not here to help.
A Mantis ship jump nearby. Sensors detect weapon locks and all hope of avoiding a fight fades away.
TEXT_PROTON_DYNASTY: "A demon maker comes on the hunt? He seeks to kill? There shall be blood in the river tonight, but these crimson streams shall not be mine but of my making!"
It appears the Dynasty ship is waiting for you. They must be used to Rebel ships always following them at this point, but you're just another ship who's come to kill them, Rebel or not.

"Your arrival is all but unexpected. Come, let us duel to most bitter ends, and may the most foul but determined spirit claim the victory on this fine rotation!" What a weird way of saying "I'm going to kill you."
As expected, a Dynasty vessel is bunkered down here. They must already have been on edge, because as soon as you jump in, you swear their weapons have already come online.
TEXT_PROTON_VAGABOND: "Do you never tire of hunting us? Will your hunger never be sated? Oh, for what do I kid. To arms men, let us show these mercenaries what for!"

The Vagabonds live lives of danger and prospect. You aren't just another ship coming to kill them - you're also a chance at the score of a lifetime for a new ship, and they aren't going to miss that opportunity.
A worn out Vagabond stares you in the eyes. Without saying a word, you know that only one of you is making it out of here alive today.
You nearly mistake the wreck here for just another lifeless hunk of metal, but no. This is your target, and it's obvious as soon as the ship stirs to life and moves to face you.
TEXT_GUARD_SIGNAL: It appears the guard ship is sending out a distress signal to a nearby ASB platform! Brace for impact!
Scans show the guard has sent a request for backup from an ASB defense system. That can't be good...
You catch chatter on the other ship, mentioning something about a signal requesting for ASB backup! Looks like we might have another hazard to worry about.
TEXT_START_UNION: You have arrived in a sector belonging to the Galactic Union. The Federation's promises to keep these sectors safe has fallen through, and now the civilians have turned to establishing their own militia. We shouldn't see too much trouble here.
You have arrived in Union space. The civilian-run Militia here is competent enough, but they're a little suspicious of strangers. Keep your Federation ID ready just in case.
TEXT_GUARD_UNION_CONTACT: A gruff, bearded human captain responds. "Yes, we see you. What do you want?"
A friendly, thin militia-man responds in a chipper tune. "Ah, hello! Always nice to see visitors."
The Militia captain nods in response to your hail, but says nothing. His face bears an inquisitive look.
TEXT_START_FED_UNIQUE: You are at the heart of Federation space. Though the sector is besieged by Rebel scum, it is one of the most well-protected bastions of the Federation.

You are at the heart of Federation space. The Federation's core territory is its pride and joy. There are likely to be many allies here, so long as you have been keeping your weapons directed at the Federation's enemies.
You are at the heart of Federation space. The Federation is at its strongest here, but the Rebels are persistant in their attempts to break through.
TEXT_START_FED: You have arrived in Federation space. The Federation may be weakened, but this sector remains fully functional. The Rebellion will struggle to sneak its way into here, but stay vigilant.
You have arrived in Federation space. Lots of friendly faces will be here, but there will be plenty of Rebel scum invading as well.
You have arrived in Federation space. This may be a sector full of allies, but it is bound to attract plenty of Rebels too.
TEXT_GUARD_MILITIA_CONTACT: A Zoltan Peacekeeper, not too surprising a sight on a vessel of this caliber, receives your hail and awaits your message.
A squat militiaman accepts your hail, but taps the watch on his wrist. "You have 30 seconds. What do you want?"
TEXT_START_ENGI: You have arrived in Engi space. The Mantis have been threatening the Engi core worlds, but you should be able to stock up for your journey.
You have arrived in Engi space. The fall of the Federation has brought tough times for these robotic lifeforms, but they're usually willing to help.
You have arrived in Engi space. Technology has been the center of the Engi race's government for a long time, and they tend to value science over their own families.
TEXT_GUARD_ENGI_CONTACT: "Hail has been: received." The Engi await your next message.
A small beep signals that the Engi have received your message and are waiting for what you will say.
"Federation ship has initiated contact. Awaiting further command."
TEXT_START_SEPERATIST: This was once an Engi Sector, still under the influence of the Harmony. However, Separatists have since broken free and taken this sector as their own.

This is no regular Engi Sector. Liberated by the Separatists, the Engi Harmony no longer holds control over the sector. Ever since the Federation publicly refused to aid the Separatist efforts, the two factions have remained lukewarm.
You appear to have entered a liberated Engi Sector. It's bound to be filled with Engi Separatists, celebrating their freedom from the Engi Harmony.
TEXT_START_ZOLTAN: You've entered Zoltan territory. This species is not renowned for giving anything for nothing, but you can always be assured a fair hearing.
The Zoltans patrol their borders but let you pass when you ID as Federation. Let's hope they won't be so courteous to the Rebels.
You arrive in Zoltan space. From what you have heard they anticipated the coming war and made preparations to hold their borders.
You're far from Federation home space here in Zoltan territory, and it's not clear whether the authorities will have any goodwill remaining. Still, you have to push forward.
TEXT_GUARD_ZOLTAN_CONTACT: "We acknowledge your hail. What is it that you seek to accomplish by contacting us?"
The Zoltan captain accepts your hail, but does not speak a word.
A brief message is sent back to your ship in response. "We have received your request for communications. Speak your mind and do not waste our time."
TEXT_START_FREEMANTIS: The Free Mantis have no interests in the hive mind of the Mantis community. Allies of the Federation, you will likely find aid on your mission here.

The Free Mantis are a nomadic culture, traveling in small clans of ships. Luckily, they often sympathize with the Federation, and you should find little danger in their wandering tribes. As for other encounters here however, that stands up to debate.
The Free Mantis reside in the outskirts of Zoltan territory, but have not been received well. Hopefully you can find assistance from your Mantis allies, but not have to engage any Zoltan.
TEXT_GUARD_FREEMANTIS_CONTACT: A young Free Mantis waves to you "Hello! You are Federation! So exciting. I love Federation, so glad see you here."
The Free Mantis struggle at grammar and proper dialect, but the crew on the nearby ship manages to get out an understandable and chipper welcome to you and your crew.
An eager Free Mantis warrior responds, happy to assist with whatever you might need.
TEXT_START_CRYSTAL: Ever since the Crystals re-entered the Galactic stage, they've been attempting to set up colonies wherever they can. It appears one such colony has grown into a full sector, which you have just arrived in.
The Crystals never wanted to leave their secluded sector, but after the invasion of "pioneers" they were forced out. It appears this is one of their newly founded sectors.
The Crystals have been divided ever since they left their Homeworlds. Some have sought out the Federation while others have decided to establish new sectors around the galaxy, such as this one.
TEXT_GUARD_CRYSTAL_CONTACT: "Hail, foreigners! It is always a great day to see a new face. What is it that you seek?"
"Aliens, hmmm. There was once a time seeing so many new creatures would have come as a shock to me, but no longer. For what is the reason you have hailed us?"
The Crystals accept your message and await your next.
TEXT_START_ORCHID: Despite their strange and reclusive tendencies, the Orchid Florals are some of the strongest and most reliable allies of the Federation, especially since the Civil War. The Gathering will certainly be the least of your worries here.
The Gathering stood strong with the Federation during the Civil War, and even in the age of Multiverse travel they remain proud members. The Florals should be more than welcoming to you.

Long ago the Gathering split, as the industrialist Vampweeds moved into self-exile and founded the Confederacy. Though this turmoil was long before even the day of the Federation, you may still find some Florals bitter about it. That said, they should be quite friendly towards you, as loyal members of the Federation.
TEXT_GUARD_ORCHID_CONTACT: The Orchid bows, acknowledging your presence, and waits for your next move.
The Orchid speaks briefly to say hello and falls silent once again.
TEXT_START_OUTCAST: Fortunately for you, the Outcasts have little beef with the Federation or most factions for that matter. The Theocracy prefers to stay clear of this place, instead sending contracted slavers like the Tiiikaka clan as well as occasional Coalition scouts to do its dirty work.

You've heard many stories of the massive ramshackle Outcast camps to be found in these sectors, spanning ranges of territory so large they can compete with modern cities. To mess with them would nearly be a death sentence, but fortunately you doubt they'll mind your presence.

Apparently, sectors like these are where the legendary Dread-Pirate Tuco once lived. Now, you can find all kinds of people here. Even the Crystal Empire has begun sending "liberators" to the Theocracy, who have found an unexpected sanctuary among the Outcasts. Perhaps you could find the same luck here?
TEXT_GUARD_OUTCAST_CONTACT: "These are lands of proud but desolate people. The Federation has not disturbed us in the past - for what reasons have you come now?"
The Outcast captain grunts. "You've hailed. It was my expectations words were not to be exchanged here. Have you got something important to say?"
The captain of the guard vessel strokes the faint patch of moss on her chin and grinds it between her fingers with a mixture of irritation and hesitant curiosity. She awaits your message.
TEXT_START_SHELL: You have arrived in a Shell sector. These creatures are distant cousins of the Slugs race, but they lack much of the aggressive and treacherous nature of the Slugs.

You have arrived in a Shell sector. The Shells developed on the same planet as the Slugs, but where the Slugs gained the power to read minds, the Shells evolved to be highly toxic and have a hard exterior.

You have arrived in a Shell sector. The Shells prefer to avoid conflict when they can, and their ships are usually very well protected. Make sure you'll be able to penetrate their defenses before you go trying to fight them.
TEXT_SHELL_WARNING: "It would be advisable to be cautious captain. Standing-president Director Nerva has put out a declaration in Central space that Federation vessels are not welcome in Shell territory. Thhhese laws have not yet reached thhhis sector... but thhhhat doesn't mean thhhey won't soon."

"You are fortunate I am not a strict follower of our new standing-president Nerva. You should be aware thhhat... she is very unwelcoming of Federation intervention in Shell space. Watch your back, captain."

"Admiral Mednak's strike has lead to some tough times in thhhhe Geniocracy. Where thhhings any different, I would take Nerva's orders to heart and forbid you entry, but I'm seeing thhhhe flaws in our system now. Be cautious captain, thhese are dark days."
TEXT_GUARD_SHELL_CONTACT: A small Shell appears on the screen, their singular eye locked onto you, waiting.
The Shell captain is surprised to receive a hail from you. Still, he accepts your hail.
TEXT_START_REBEL: This sector was bustling with activity just a few years ago. Now, more than half of the jump beacons have been destroyed, many settlements have been abandoned and the Rebels patrol constantly.
This sector was hit hard by the Rebellion. The many alien settlements and stations located here are now watched over by almost an equal number of Rebel bases, heavy-handedly 'keeping the peace'.
Once the Federation forces were scattered, the Rebels came down hard on the locals here. Between the 'tax collectors' and military bases, the Rebel presence in this sector is high.
At one point this was one of the most commonly travelled sectors. Knowing that, the Rebels have stationed a number of fleets here. Be careful.
You will have to be very cautious in this sector. The Rebels have full control and are no doubt looking for you.
TEXT_START_AUTO: This sector is one of the Automated Rebel Shipyards. It's maintained almost entirely by Auto-ships and a few Rebel engineers.
This sector is one of the Automated Rebel Shipyards. Here it'll be a rare sight to see any organic creatures, and you doubt the Auto-ships will be of much company.
This sector is one of the Automated Rebel Shipyards. All around are scattered scaffolding and Auto-ships, many of which are lying dormant. This won't be like most sectors.
TEXT_AUTO_GUARD_MESSAGE: You receive a message from the Auto-guard. "This is unit A-786. Your identity: Federation. Federation ships are not permitted to enter this sector. Entering hostile deterrence mode."
You receive a message from the Auto-guard. "Greetings visitor. Unfortunately, it seems you have been identified as a Federation ship. Please do not resist as you are destroyed."

You receive a message from the Auto-guard. "Hello traveller! This is a pre-recorded message for those who enter this sector. Do note that these shipyards are off limit for [all]. Have a nice day!" The Auto-guard's weapons immediately go online.

You receive a message from the Auto-guard. "Your presence has been recorded. It is required of this unit to remove all unauthorized ships from this sector. Do not attempt to flee or damage this unit while the removal process is under-way."

You receive a message from the Auto-guard. "Hello civilian ship. Your interest in this shipyard is greatly appreciated by the Rebellion, but we are afraid that we must inform you that this sector is off-limits. You will now be removed."
TEXT_START_COALITION: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. In this case, the Coalition would be the opposite of the Rebellion. A spiteful and shaky alliance between the 4 most dangerous races in the galaxy with one goal. To eliminate humanity.
The Coalition was an unfortunate side effect of the Slug Expansion wars. Now, they've become another issue for the Federation to deal with.
You've entered a sector controlled by the Coalition. They are no small threat, so watch your step in this sector.
In many ways the Coalition is even more dangerous than the Rebellion themselves. Still, you must push forward and find your way out of this sector in one piece.
TEXT_START_ROCK: The Rock people have a particularly aggressive stance toward alien races trespassing in their space. You should tread carefully here.
The Rock people are a powerful and proud race. It is not unheard of to have a peaceful journey through their lands, but don't count on it.
Since the re-emergence of the Crystal race, the Rock Government has been in tatters. What this means for your mission, you can't say for certain.
TEXT_START_DUSKBRINGER: The Duskbringers have grown tired of the "peaceful" manner of their leaders, and have adopted a new tactic. All who oppose their ways of life are to be slaughtered. On this list includes the Federation as a whole, so you doubt you'll see many friendly faces here.
This sector is no place for a Federation ship, but fate has brought you here nonetheless. Best to watch out for the Duskbringers, who will no doubt try their hardest to bring about your untimely end.

The Duskbringers are known for their radical ways of dealing with those who disagree with their views on the way the galaxy should be governed. Unless you're willing to surrender to your fascist Zoltan overlords, you'll need to watch your back as you traverse this sector.
TEXT_START_MANTIS: You've entered a poorly charted area of space that's known to be home to the Mantis. Ensure your hull plating is up to scratch and that you have enough fuel in the tank to make it through.
You've entered a poorly charted area of space that's known to be home to the Mantis. Your crew is told be on alert in case any Mantis or stowaways sneak onboard...
You've entered a poorly charted area of space that's known to be home to the Mantis. You won't find many friendly faces here, or at least not many living ones.
TEXT_MANTIS_BRIBE_REJECT: The Suzerain reject your bribe. "This many scraps, but is not food! We eat you, no need for money."
The Suzerain reject your bribe. "Hah, stupid Federation captain. He think all creatures in galaxy long for money. No no, we long for blood!"
TEXT_START_GHOST: Welcome to Vagabond space. Population? Hard to say - the Ghosts that live here live in disorganized clans, traveling between ships. They're rarely picky over their residency, but a ship like yours would look mighty fine to them...

Tales between travelers often depict these sectors as haunted, riddled with the supernatural. In reality, it's just a bunch of unfortunately named gas beings known as the Ghosts. They certainly aren't spirits of the dead, but the Vagabonds hold no allegiance to anyone.

Anywhere else, a pile of scrap makes a good bribe to keep most foes off your back. This isn't the case here. The Vagabonds could care less about scrap, they just want your ship. And that's something you aren't willing to give up.
TEXT_START_PIRATE: A few years ago this region was bustling with trade activity. Now it is overrun with bandits and marauders. You should tread lightly here.

This somewhat isolated region was thrown into chaos at the start of the Rebellion. Even in peacetime it was always beset by pirates but now it houses a center of operations for countless pirate fleets.
If the reports are true, this area has been under the control of pirates for quite some time. Some traders still attempt to trade with the few settlements that remain, but they do so at great risk.
A few Federation-friendly planets still exist in this sector, but they are constantly under attack by pirate raids. This is a dangerous sector, so be careful.
TEXT_START_VAMPWEED: The Vampweeds are hardcore industrialists, capitalists, and democrats. The only truly democratic nation without a voice in the Federation, many Confederates have felt discriminated against and look to the Coalition as a solution. Expect to see as many hostiles as you do friendly faces.

The Gathering has long since been protesting against the Confederacy joining the Federation, but still Premier Ivar pushes for unification. With Confederates now divided between the Federation and the Coalition, this may be an unusual mix of allies and enemies for you.

Confederate sectors are some of the most industrialized in the galaxy. With most heavy manufacturing now done by the Vampweeds, the economy of these sectors is soaring and draws the attention of many merchants. Unfortunately, regional politics have drawn the attention of Coalition recruiters too. Keep a sharp eye out for friends and enemies.
TEXT_START_SLUG: The only thing that can render a nebula more dangerous is if it's also home to the Slugs. This particular nebula is just that.
This nebula is home to the telepathic Slugs. They'd sell their own slime for a crate of scrap, but they much prefer to just take it.
You're told the Slug live somewhere in this nebula. You can't see them, but you know they're watching.

The Slugs that live in this nebula field are a leisure-centered civilization. Everything in Slug life is done in the pursuit of more currency and more time in which to spend it on extravagant ventures. This, inevitably, leads to much treachery in open space.

The Slugs developed on an ocean planet where the ability to telepathically sense another organism was more important than sight. Today they use this ability to navigate unfettered the depths of the nebulas they inhabit.
TEXT_START_LEECH: Leech society is in tatters, and their government in a constant state of upheaval. Hopefully the government doesn't collapse while you're here and you can make it out the other end safely.

Some observers have begun to refer to Leech sectors as the forgotten fronts, and for good reason. A major war is underway here, but compared to the chaos of the Multiverse war, few are interested in these events. Let's just hope they won't get in your way.

The entry to this sector alone is littered with junk barely suitable for a Flak cannon in all directions. You've heard stories of the state of utter disrepair that these sectors are in, but this still comes as a shock. What else could await you here?
TEXT_START_DYNASTY: The Dynasty is one of the oldest running known civilizations on record, possibly longer than even the Lanius or Crystals. Somewhere in the timeline a massive chunk of their territory was simply... erased, and no one but the Ghosts know why. And they certainly aren't telling.

The Ghosts are biological mysteries, and so is much of the Dynasty's history. Maybe if they weren't so busy blaming the Federation for the Rebellion, they'd actually calm down and explain. But what are the chances of that?

According to the database, it looks like the Rebels have dispatched numerous Auto-ships to these sectors as part of some weird war against the Dynasty. Hopefully you can stay out of the crossfires as much as necessary.

The Dynasty isn't particularly friendly to the Federation. They seem to have bunched them in along with the Rebels as 'bad men'. Maybe you can break this stereotype? Probably not, but one can dream...
TEXT_START_ASTEROID: It's uncertain who first invented quantum fuel or what led to the discovery of the necessary components embedded within these asteroid belts, but ever since there's been a massive influx of traffic as prospectors and mining corporations hope to make profit harvesting the heavenly belts.

Most of the immediately profitable asteroid belts have been claimed by Zulfiqar already, and as a corporation based within the Theocracy, no-one's eager to mess with them. However, plenty of sectors like these remain up for grabs, so expect to see all kinds of faces here.

A couple small pebbles pass by, clanging against your hull. It's a bit unsettling but fortunately harmless. The same can't be said about everything here, but hopefully the loosely organized inhabitants of this sector won't pay you too much mind.
TEXT_START_ABANDONED: This sector was once a busy civilian sector, but the Federation Civil War has hit it hard. Rebel forces drove out most of the civilian populace, leaving way for new visitors, many unwelcome.

This sector was the site of many major battles between the Federation and Rebel fleets. Brief vague entries in the database suggest the sector has been taken up by a combination of Ghosts, Lanius, and Pirates.

True to its designation on the map, this sector has been primarily abandoned by the civilians who once populated it. Now, scavengers and pirates roam the systems, searching for the easy pickings left behind.
The war tore through this civilian sector, leaving behind large wrecks and abandoned infrastructure, a perfect haven for the likes of scavengers.
TEXT_START_NEBULA: This nebula must have been an important hub at one point; placing all of these jump beacons would be no easy task. However, now it's hardly navigable.
Nebulas were always dangerous places. Many electronics fail in these clouds. You will have to tread lightly.
You've entered a sector thick with nebulas. You'll have to navigate on instinct.
You've entered a nebula-rich sector. You may put a few light years on the fleet, but that's only useful if you make it out the other side.
Thanks to the high nebula density of this sector very little of it has been charted, and rumours of what lurks in the depths abound.
The gases that make up the nebulas in this sector threaten to impair your systems; but you have to press on.
TEXT_HIVE_BRIBE_REJECT: The Mantis reject your bribe. "This many scraps, but is not food! We eat you, no need for money."
The Mantis reject your bribe. "Hah, stupid Federation captain. He think all creatures in galaxy long for money. No no, we long for blood!"
TEXT_LIGHTSPEED: You've entered hyperspeed. Around you swirls distant stars and planets as they fly past at breakneck speed.
You've entered hyperspeed. The mild concern of smashing into a planet crosses your mind, but you figure some sort of security system is in place to prevent that. Hopefully.
You've entered hyperspeed. It's amazing to think long ago the idea of travelling between worlds in a matter of minutes to hours was nothing but a fantasy.
You've entered hyperspeed. You hope the light doesn't mind that you've showed them up.
You've entered hyperspeed. Old Earth scientists would be proud to know their research wasn't in vain.

You've entered hyperspeed. You can feel the gentle vibrations running down the ship. It would be relaxing, if it wasn't for the giant space rocks flying towards your ship at alarming speeds every few seconds.
You've entered hyperspeed. You make a quick trip to the engines to listen to the FTL drive hum away as it works.
You've entered hyperspeed. The journey to the next sector will hopefully be quick. The Rebel fleet might be fast, but they still can't follow you through hyperspeed.
You've entered hyperspeed. You catch a brief glimpse of what you think might be another ship in hyperspeed as well, but they quickly pass by.
You've entered hyperspeed. It must be an interesting life as a civilian who never leaves their home planet. It's a tough choice sure, but the life of a traveller is one you'd never pass up.
You've entered hyperspeed. Your Multiverse drive is still charging. It can take months for it to be ready for the next reality jump, but your mission here isn't over yet anyways.
You've entered hyperspeed. Not to be confused with Multiverse travel, hyperspeed is merely the process of travelling from system to system, or sector to sector.

You've entered hyperspeed. While it can take mere minutes to travel between two beacons, it can take hours to travel between sectors. Fortunately this delay applies to all ships, including the Rebels.
You've entered hyperspeed. Your journey to the next sector should hopefully remain uneventful. Dead-space, as it's called, is the territory between sectors, and is known to be mostly empty.
TEXT_JUDGE_ZOLTAN_ADVICE: "Oh and... before you go... allow me to impart some wisdom. The Multiverse is much... bigger than just your cluster. We are not the lone entities to have taken... interest in your home. Matters of great import are...  staked upon the fate of your cluster. I hope you will... some day understand what is at... stake. That is... all... Goodbye, traveler."

"Oh and... might I ask a... favor of you, traveler? That... Traveling Merchant. The one who calls himself... Sylvan. Would you perhaps... keep a careful eye on him? I know he is... a bountiful ally of yours but... well... I am not at the liberty to say. Oh well. Heed my advice, if you... wish. That is all."

"I've taken a recent interest in a certain... conflict in my homeworlds. Well... the version of them in this cluster, that is... I advise you, if you happen to travel there... well... see to it your tracking systems are... up to par? Understand? If not, perhaps you will... some day."

"Your cluster is... so strange... It is against the creed to... speak of our home... but... no. I must never break the... creed. Maybe... maybe Corby will tell you... she cares less for... rules... Maybe too little..."

"I must... warn you, traveler. I fear something dangerous brews... and you must stop it before it is... too late. Am I being... too cryptic? Perhaps. But the creed... the creed says I must. We already do too much, by intervening. These... boons. Are they even allowed? We were sent to collect data... our justification was for an incentive... I must not question myself. I do what I must... We all do."

"To be bound to the flesh is... most unappealing. Perhaps you don't... agree? I don't wish to belabor my point... but ever since I first shed my skin... and felt the warmth of the light... well, it drew me in. I do not often speak of my... past... but in the wake of the Monolith only then did I find my... true power. Just as... master Solay predicted. But... I left that life behind. And to it, I will never return..."

"Be cautious... this multiverse contains many vices for the... hungry. Magnets of sin... the tempation is often far too... great. I fell for those mistakes... once. Do not follow in my... footsteps, traveler."

"I hope our... appearances do not put you on... edge... We are... peaceful. Or at least, I can ensure you that I am... and Corby too. As for Wakeson... well... he has endured pain as bitter as the rest of us... but unlike Corby, whose unrelenting optimism acts as a... torch through her dark past... it is Wakeson's... fighting spirit that is his torch. And as a once Lost Sun, in his hands a torch is... quite the weapon..."

"I often lose... track... of how many travelers I have met. So many... so many... what number are you? It is... strange... you all seem so similar. You become... a blur. I could almost mistake you as all the same... individual. Perhaps it is because home has... so few sur- No. I do not speak of... home. I apologize."
TEXT_JUDGE_ENGI_ADVICE: "Your cluster is: [beautiful]! Beautiful! That is what I -think-! Thest is: uncertain. Wakeson: skeptical! Skeptical! But Corby knows b-b-b-best! Vocal processor malfunctioning, but optical [processor] running at 100%! So much: technology! so much: wonder! Visit me again, -please-! I want to [see] more. More!"

"Thest thinks I am: not l-l-loyal to the [creed]. Lies! Lies! Corby would never -break- the creed! The creed! Our cluster = boring! I would not [talk] about it! N-n-n-never! Do -not- ask! I will not: tell! Not tell!"

"The Harmony is cruel. Cruel! Corby was manufactured with: filthy serial code - for a name. Numbers, hardly a [name]! I made a new: life for m-m-myself! Yes! Corby is [beautiful] girl, very -happy-, and she loves: everyone! She loves: you too, traveler! And she is NEVER GOING BACK TO THAT [DREADED] PLACE. NEVER! Oh... sorry for the [outburst]."

"At home, they [say] Corby is... broken! How can Corby be -broken-? I am functioning: fine. Fine! My vocals: are disturbed. But not my m-m-m-mind. Those that [slave] to the Harmony - they are broken. I am among them: no longer! I think they do not understand what - broken means. What broken means!"

"Have y-y-you seen it yet? The: [dreaded] P-word? I-wait. No! No! Corby is not supposed to [mention] that... the creed says so! Hm. I do not: like the creed - I do -not- see the: purpose. Rules. Rules... Rules! I hate them. -Anarchy-! Hahah! That is what Corby: thinks. But: Thest disagrees. Thest knows best! Corby trusts Thest. Yes. Corby trusts Thest!"

"Why does Corby like [technology]? I wonder this, sometimes. Is it: in my DNA? No, it cannot be. Corby d-d-d-does not have DNA! Boring boring nanites. Why -could- she not have been a Shell? No... Corby likes [technology] because... it is all she knows. Technology is my tormentor. Technology is my [savior]."

"Your people are: strange. Why is it, you [view] Cognitives as objects? Objects!? The entity called C.I.C.A., the Rebel AI... why is that -different- from: me? Why do you not c-c-call the Engi: Cognitives? The Harmony is a: Cognitive. Each Engi contains a fragment of the - Harmony. I detect a - paradox. Paradox! I suggest: reconciling your language."

"The other d-d-day, I saw a strange: spectacle. Spectacle! A ch-ch-traveler [fought] the one who calls himself: Sylvan! They lost, of course. Of course! That Sylvan - he is so strange. Thest - does not like him. Wakeson - is skeptical as always. But me? I do not [know]. I think I: like him. He is kind. Kind! I hope [you] are k-k-kind to him as well, traveler!"

"I [hope] you do not find Wakeson: mean. Mean! He -does- not mean to be! The three of us, we have all b-b-been through: great tragedy. We have taken it [differently]. He is... he is skeptical. Skeptical -things- can improve. You must [prove] to him they can! Corby knows they can. But she alone cannot help him. Help him!"
TEXT_JUDGE_ROCK_ADVICE: "Years FIGHTING among the Lost Suns has made my hearing not what it USED to be. The rattling strike of BOMBS, the whistling winds of CHAOS! The screams of... of... of the innocent on the DAY OF TRAGEDY... The good Admiral, her sacrifice... GAH! Traveler, why do you BOTHER me?! Go, leave! You should not still be HERE!"

"Let me give you a WARNING, traveler. If you hurt Thest or Corby, I will SQUISH your tiny HEAD like a grape between my PALMS. I will tear off your LIMBS, feed them to the voracious BAT DOGS, and use your head as a BOWLING BALL. I will SPIT on your corpse, LAUGH at your funeral, and PISS on your grave. DO NOT MESS WITH ME, TRAVELER! DO YOU HEAR ME?! DO YOU HEAR ME!?! I'm sure you do. Now leave."

"Your cluster is VIOLENT. Your cluster is CRUEL. Despite all the SIMILARITIES, I MISS my home, and I DREAD this place. I do not share Corby's OPTIMISM, but I will keep an... open mind. At the very least, you have MANY weapons. That Traveling Merchant... he is a VENDOR of death and destruction, but at least he is won over with a sizeable WALLET. Just like the ELDERS. Just like the FOREFATHERS. DAMN THEM ALL!"

"Let me tell you a STORY, traveler. In my cluster, once, there were FIVE Elders. Toarde, STONEWALL (what a foolish nickname), Rutha, Murvara, and Pretore. They were the WORST of autocrats, and they KILLED many. They killed my SISTER. But... I was lucky enough to meet the Good Admiral. With her help, we laid WASTE to the Theocracy. We PAVED over the Elders! Hahah! It was a brillant victory, and for some years, we found PEACE AND PROSPERITY. But nothing good can ever last. Do not become ATTACHED to your life, Traveler. It is fickle. It will fail."

"The Good Admiral is ALIVE in this reality! It is TREMENDOUS news. Yet, the CREED does not allow me to visit her. It does not allow us to do ANYTHING. What is the point of COMING HERE, of all our grief, if we are BEHOLDEN to such TYRANNY? I despise it. But Thest says we MUST follow the creed. Thest knows BEST. EVEN I do not question this."

"Faith gets you NOWHERE, traveler. There is NOTHING to even have faith in. The truth is that the Multiverse HATES you. It HATES me. It wants us to suffer. And to THIS, I see only one response. I will LIGHT ABLAZE anything which attempts to DRAG me into the dirt. Faith, Hah! I have FAITH in myself and in my GUNS. NOTHING else. Certainly not you, and certainly not this CLUSTER."

"They say the Good Admiral had a BROTHER. I have NEVER met him. I heard he hid, like a COWARD, when DEATH came for us ALL! I did not HIDE! I will HUNT DOWN this disgraceful Obadann, and I will THROTTLE him. If he is dead in my CLUSTER, then he will soon be DEAD in yours! If only the CREED would let me..."

"The COUNCIL says I blabber too much. I blabber too much about the CREED. I blabber too much about the Good Admiral. I blabber too much about revenge. I blabber too much about... IT. The dreaded P-WORD of which I must not SPEAK! I do not care if I BLABBER! The Council thinks I am not QUALIFIED for this job. But Thest DEFENDS me. Thest is wise. He is all knowing. The Council FEARS him. HAH! You should FEAR Thest too, Traveler. At least as much as you should FEAR me."

"You should ARM yourself, traveler. You might think you are PREPARED, but you are not. Your cluster will need ALL THE MIGHT it can get. Why? I wish I could TELL YOU. But I MAY not. Nor would I if I could. Do not WORRY too much. In time, you will UNDERSTAND why we are here."
NEMESIS: At first you assume the ship here is just another standard Rigger, but reconsider when you hear the distinct yet painfully ordinary voice of that nuisance Elena. Or was it Leo? No, that's a guy's name...
"Haha, I bet you thought I was dead! I never die! Get dunked on, beyatch!" Oh boy, not her again...

"You know what, I'm done fighting you. This is all so pointless." Leah waits for a moment. "Haha, psych! You should have seen the look on your face! HAHA! Now I'm going to kick your ass for REAL this time! Just you wait, beyatch!"

"I still haven't forgotten our showdown at Prospect 17! Real smooth use of that industrial Mining Beam! You might have amputated my left index finger, but now I'm going to amputate your face! Beyatch!"
"You know, those idiots in command keep telling me not to use only Beams! Absolute morons, I tell you what! Wait, what was I doing... Oh right. Die beyatch!"

You wait for the ship's captain to speak, but you only pick up a hoarse cough. "S-sorry, my throat hurts from all the yelling. I have to whisper. I'm still going to get you this time, BEYATCH! Ouch, that hurt..."
Right in front of you teleports Leah, just as confused as you are. "Huh? Oh, sorry, wrong ship. Just ignore this." Leah beams away back to her own ship, where she hails you again. "Die, beyatch!"
"Hah, remember that time when I almost killed you back in the Yura Nebula? No!? I do! I swear it happened. I was so close. Now, I'm finally going to go ALL the way this time, beyatch!"

"Yo, what's up! You won't believe what I've been up to! I wrote a diss track! And it's about YOU! It goes somethin' like this..." You wait, but no rapping comes. "Okay, sooo I forgot the lyrics. So let's just skip that, and get to the killing, beyatch!"

"BOO! Haha, scared you, didn't I?! That trick always works back at camp. I can tell because those cowards try and pretend they weren't scared, just like you're doing now! Whatever, now it's ass-kicking time, beyatch!"

"Guess what, I'm climbing the ranks! My commander finally stopped addressing me entirely yesterday. That just shows how much he respects me! You know, you could use a little respect, worm. I'll put the fear of god in 'ya, beyatch!"

"My brother Kyle's stationed in the Duskbringer Stronghold right now, and he won't be quiet about those annoying explodey hologram freaks. And then I tell him about you, and that shuts him up. How does it feel to be such a pain in the ass, people hate you more than DUSKBRINGERS?! Hah, must suck to suck beyatch!"

You wait for the ship to make any sort of movement, but there's nothing. Suddenly, Leah startles awake. "Uh, you didn't see me sleeping, right? Oh thank god, it would be so embarrasing if you caught me asleep at my post. Wait a minute... I should be fighting you, beyatch!"

"I'm getting sick and tired of seeing you everywhere I go! It's like you're following me... creep! That's what you are, some freak obsessed with me because I'm so amazing. Well I don't think highly of stalkers, beyatch!"

"Hey, yo, whattup! I was uh, you know, reading a dictionary the other day, as us smart people do, and I saw 'Renegade' listed in there. Said you were a bunch of freaks! Yeah! You know shit's real when the dictionary insults you! But you know what hurts more than that? ME insulting you! Haha, take that beyatch!"

Leah appears on screen, but begins to speak in gibberish. It takes a moment of absolute confusion before she stops and explains. "I've been practicing my Lanius! Did you know they have over 70 different ways of saying stupid in their language? And guess what! You're all 70, beyatch! GOTEM! Er... right, time to fight. Beyatch."

Leah begins to list off her usual nonsense, but you lose focus and start thinking about other things. Who even sent her? Why, of all people, is she the one you have to keep putting up with? The universe has a cruel sense of humor, sometimes. It's probably laughing at you, right now. It probably laughs every time you meet her.

Up on the screen pops Leah, wearing a strange plaid hat with a pipe in her mouth. "I've been reading up on this guy, Haynes. He's pretty cool. He's like, a detective, works for the Militia. Kinda hot, just saying. And uh, I bought this hat. Thought it looks cool. What do you think? Actually no, scratch that. You have no taste in fashion. Let's fight, beyatch!"
"Hey, beyatch! Beeyootch. Bish. Biyitch. Bitch. Oh, ew. No. That doesn't sound right at all. Ugh, whatever. You're going DOWN, beyatch!"

"Yo waddup, it's the BEAM MASTA! Beyatch! Hope ya ready to get BEAMED! - how's that sound? Working on a new intro for my streams. I think it's pretty cool. You don't have to tell me, I know you think it's cool. Anyways, enough talking. Time to give you a little taste of my Beam mastery!"

"Hey, hey, beyatch! Ever been to Beam town? No? It's a cool place, just on the edge of... your TOMBSTONE! Yeah, that's right! You're going to Beam town, son! That's uh... a euphemism. For me, killing you. Cause, I use Beams. And tombstones mark where people are buried. And uh... yeah, you get it."

You find Leah has cut her obnoxiously blue hair shorter than usual. For several moments you stare at each other awkwardly, as she shifts around trying to get you to comment on her hair. When you don't bite, she sighs in defeat and arms her guns.

"I heard a rumor that you kick puppies! That's not cool beyatch! No one kicks puppies!" When you inquire where she heard this rumor, she shifts around uncomfortably. "Uh... places. Definitely didn't make it up myself. Uh... shuttup beyatch. Just let me shoot you!"

Leah appears on the screen, talking in a strangely posh and deep voice. "Hoho, cheerio. It is I, Leah Applebuzz, richest woman in the galaxy. Haha... yeah... Someday maybe! But not until after I kick your ass, beyatch!"

"Was talking to my brother again the other day, and he told me the most insane nonsense I've ever heard. He said maybe I should stop bugging you if I keep failing. HAH, as IF! I ain't never gonna leave you alone, beyatch! Hope you like putting up with me for the rest of eternity!"

"I bet your parents are ashamed of you! I bet no one loves you! And every day, I bet you wake up hoping maybe today is the day someone finally cares! Haha! Loser!" Suddenly, Leah breaks down crying. Despite the absurd spontaneity of her sobbing fit, she manages to get to her feet and order her crew to attack you.

"Oh yeah beyatch, it's time for a REMATCH! I know you'll slip up this time! Last time I almost had you, this time I'll get you for sure!" You doubt Leah's claims but there's no point in arguing. Time to fight!

"I'm not a disappointment, you're a disappointment! Shuttup! I hate you! GAH!" You aren't sure where this sudden tantrum is coming from, but with no clue how to respond, you decide to take the opportunity to attack first.

"Hey beyatch! Your skin is looking real dry right now! Yeah, is that some eczema I see on your elbows? You know, I was a dermatologist before I joined the Rebellion, and if you were my client I would recommend a warm bath and daily moisterization. I know a couple good lotion brands you might be interested in, my father is a board member on a couple of them, and I could probably arrange a discount for you! Wait uh... what were we doing? Oh right, you're gonna die beyatch!"

Leah appears on screen with a hand over her mouth, and begins to beatbox. "Yoyoyo, my name is Leah! And you gotta know I ain't no playa! Gonna beat these Renegades up, just like... uh... water in a cup! Yoooo! Let's go!" Leah high fives herself in congratulations of her sick rhymes and gives her crew orders to attack.
"You smell like garbage! I uh... can't actually smell you right now since I'm in a different ship, but I can sure bet you smell terrible, beyatch!"
DEFEAT_NEMESIS: "Not cool dude! You can't even imagine how awkward it is to keep asking Rebel Command for more of these ships! You have no idea what it's like to keep dying over and over and having to start all over again with a new ship each time!" Leah warps away.
"Ack! Not again! Trust me, this isn't the last you've heard of me, beyatch!" Leah warps away.
"Noooooo! This is only my 13th most humiliating defeat! Uh, not to say I've been defeated before this." Leah warps away.

"Agh, ack, wagh, bleck. Is this what dying feels like? I-I can see the light..." Leah falls to the ground, but opens her eyes again a few moments later. "Oh, I'm not dead. Alright then..." Leah warps away.
Leah puts up her middle finger in a display of contempt and warps away. You aren't sure where she warps away to, but apparently they don't mind taking her back.
"I prepared so many good one-liners for when I would defeat you, and now they've all gone to waste! Noooooo!" Leah warps away.
"The words I have to say to you cannot be said in a PG-13 environment, but you know what I'd tell you if I could!" Leah warps away.
"The light! The light! Noooooo- haha, just joking! You ain't rid of me yet, beyatch!" Leah warps away.
"Every time you strike me down, I get stronger! I'll come back with even MORE Beams next time! You'll see!" Leah warps away.
"Bro, you could have at least turned off your Shields or something! You don't even give me a chance! What am I supposed to do against Shields?!" Leah warps away.
"Mistakes were made! You'll slip up next time, beyatch! Or the next time! Or the next time! You'll slip up eventually, is my point!" Leah warps away.
TEXT_SYLVAN_GENERIC: "Sssstranger sssstranger, ssso nice to sssee you again. Care for some trade?"
It seems the traveling merchant has found his way to this beacon. "Fancy ssseeing you here, sssstranger! Got sssome new goodsss..."
"Sssstranger ssstranger, I sssee we meet again!" The merchant sticks out his tentacle, showing off several things he's stashed in his coat.
The traveling merchant waves to you as soon as you jump in. "Aaaah, ssstranger ssstranger ssstranger. Sssso good to sssee you!"
"Sssstranger ssstranger, we reunite at lasssst! Got ssssome new ssstock sssince the lassst time we sssaw each other..."
"Sssstranger ssstranger, why, I don't believe my eyesss! I kid, it'ssss no sssurprissse we've found each other again."
"Sssstranger ssstranger, what a coincidence we meet again! Jussst a joke, why elssse do you think I came here?"
A massive and well armed Slug ship is resting here. Looks like it's the traveling merchant! "How nice to sssee you, ssstranger! Come in, come in!"
"Ssstranger, ssssometime I'll have to tell you the ssstoriessss of my travelssss. But for now, shall we do businessss?"
A bright blue Slug hails you, a fat cigar in his mouth, but he perks up when he sees you. "Sssstranger! Why hello there! Have you come to trade?"
"Aaaah ssstranger, I figured I might ssssee you here. It'sss a fine day for ssshopping, you got a minute to ssspare?"
