TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MV_REBEL: It appears you aren't alone! A fellow multiverse traveler, this time a Rebel, has already found their way to this beacon, and is moving in on your location.
You were aware the Rebels had been finding their way into this sector, but you didn't expect to see a Multiverse-drive equipped vessel defending this beacon!
It appears you aren't the only ship at this beacon, nor the only ship with a Multiverse-Drive here either! A hostile Multiverse Rebel ship has spotted you and is moving in to attack.

"Haha! At last we have found you. It only took 768 different realities full of chocolate pudding or shape-shifting god aliens to find you here!" A beat up Multiverse Rebel ship moves in, weapons armed and ready.
A confident Rebel captain of the nearby Multiverse ship boasts about his abilities at tracking you down, and swiftly gives his crew orders to attack. You figure you should do the same.

The Rebel ship at this beacon looks like it has been through a lot... and for good reason! It's a ship from across the Multiverse, and it seems they've tracked you down to this beacon and are looking for a fight.
The Rebels are a common sight all around the galaxy, but the ship here is no ordinary Rebel. They appear to be a Multiverse-Drive equipped vessel, and they've decided to engage you in combat!
"You're that Universe 0 bloke! Haha, we've got you now. You're one hard fellow to track down, but in the end, the Rebellion will always win!"

A Rebel Multiverse ship approaches. "You son of a buzzard, do you know how many realities we had to suffer through until we found you? This is like, the 9th version of myself to pilot the 16th version of this ship! So quit running and just die!"
You're amazed at the amounts of effort these Rebels go to tracking you down. A Rebel ship in poor condition bears down on you, determined not to let you past.
A mute Rebel officer fumbles, performing lazy sign language your translator slowly converts to verbal communication. "A Free Mantis ripped out my tongue. I blame you. Now I'm going to kill you."

You receive a hail from an overweight Rebel. "I was an MFK Ace you know, but then I took a Bio-Beam to the knee. But if I can kill you... maybe Vance will give me another chance!" You suspect he's lying, but you don't have time to refute his claim.
The pastel blue hull of a Rebel MV vessel glides past. As soon as they spot you, they power up their weapons and engage!
A Rebel ship comes screaming into the system... literally. The captain is shouting at the top of his lungs. Some of these Rebels are complete nuts; it looks like you'll have to crack another one.

"Straight out of Universe 1, and the first thing I find is a Federation Renegade? My luck is never this good! Promotion, here I come..." Seems you'll have to prove this isn't quite the lucky encounter he's looking forward to.

A Rebel captain appears on the vidscreen, chewing on a squirming bowl of young Orchids. "While tracking you down, we ran out of food. Now I'm stuck eating these gross baby things. Please, just let me kill you, so I can go find some food that doesn't cry when I bite it."

A nearby Multiverse travelling Rebel ship broadcasts an automated message; "Glory to the Rebellion!" You remember the time when the Rebels cared enough to actually say it themselves. At least, you get to blow them up all the same.

Most of the Rebel forces sent from Universe 1 are ships like these. Strangely, you don't encounter many of them outside of random chance like this; you suppose the Rebellion keeps its Warp-Bays somewhere else. Regardless, a challenger is beckoning, and you aren't going to disappoint!

You've heard Admiral Vance has some kind of personal grudge against Renegades, and so the Rebellion relies on its signature blue-clad MV Rebels to carry the burden of the invasion. You wonder how it feels to jump out of U1 just to face down a ship like yours. You're sure glad you don't.

"I used to be a Fed during the Civil War in U1. But after the U0 invasion began... well... you either became a Rebel or you accepted your death or enslavement. If things had turned out differently... well... I hope you understand none of this is personal."
TEXT_DESTROYED_REBEL_MULTIVERSE: "It's okay... I saw this... coming..." The Rebel captain collapses as their ship breaks apart around them. If they saw this coming, they should have thought twice about messing with you. Good riddance.
"I guess I'm not getting that promotion after all. Darn." The last look of disappointment in themselves is erased as the Rebel's body is thrown out into the abyss as their ship is destroyed.

Another Rebel turned to dust. Whether it's the signature orange of mainstay Rebels or the blue of these specialized invaders, a dead Rebel is the only good Rebel. With a couple exceptions, of course. You'd fancy a Rebel who gave you free scrap; that'd be a good Rebel for sure.
From amidst the explosions you receive one last hail; "Is it too late to be sorry? It is? Damn..."
It's a very small dent you've made in the Rebellion's MV fleet, but you weren't paid to do this either. Let's just hope the Flagship falls as easily as these ships do by the time you get there.
TEXT_DEAD_CREW_REBEL_MULTIVERSE: "It's okay... I saw this... coming..." The Rebel captain collapses. If they saw this coming, they should have thought twice about messing with you. Good riddance.
"I guess I'm not getting that promotion after all. Darn." The last look of disappointment in themselves is erased as the Rebel captain falls over dead.

Another Rebel turned to dust. Whether it's the signature orange of mainstay Rebels or the blue of these specialized invaders, a dead Rebel is the only good Rebel. With a couple exceptions, of course. You'd fancy a Rebel who gave you free scrap; that'd be a good Rebel for sure.
Though the last life signs aboard the Rebel ship are quickly fading, you receive one last hail; "Is it too late to be sorry? It is? Damn..."
It's a very small dent you've made in the Rebellion's MV fleet, but you weren't paid to do this either. Let's just hope the Flagship falls as easily as these ships do by the time you get there.
TEXT_DEFEAT_MULTIVERSE_TRAVELER: "At least... when I'm dead... I won't have to look at your stupid face anymore..."
The Multiverse ship has ceased to function, sending out a mist of blue vapor from what was their drive. You scrap their ship.
"Ah shit, guess I'm dead now." The Renegade's vessel promptly shuts down.
You've sent another crew of Renegades to the great multiverse in the sky. You hope this doesn't end up being you someday down the line instead.
The Renegade has met their untimely end. That'll teach the galaxy not to mess with the likes of you.
In the end, this ship wasn't much different from you. All the same, they're the dead ones, and you aren't.
The defeat of this vessel marks another victory for you and your crew. You hold a celebratory toast in hopes to more successful battles after salvaging the wreck.
"Aaaaaaghghghghghgh," moans the enemy captain. He gasps for air, then falls over dead. The enemy is no more.
Some day, you might earn enough of a name for yourself that these ships stop trying to mess with you. But for now, you can cross another set of pillagers off the list.
You can't imagine what your kill count will be by the end of your mission, and frankly you aren't sure you want to find out. Still, there's nothing stopping you from salvaging these latest remains.
TEXT_SURRENDER_MULTIVERSE_TRAVELER: "Ahhh crap crap crap! We surrender, stop firing for the love of Newton's Third Law!"
The ship sends several images of a white flag to you. You figure that's a good sign that they wish to surrender.
"Ok, we messed up. But if you kill us, well that's just not very cool, man."
"Look, this was a bit of a mistake. Let us go, and we promise we'll never make this mistake again. Probably."
"I'm a fellow Renegade like you! Surely you understand we only wanted scrap! It was a mistake messing with you, take this and let us live!"
The ship hails you, their captain soliciting a... favor for your 'pleasure' in turn for letting them live. When you express your disinterest, they offer something of more monetary value instead.
The enemy hails you, speaking a mess of untranslated garble. "Apologies, I forgot to turn my translator on again." The captain pauses. "AAAAAAAAAAAAAH DON'T KILL US DON'T KILL US!"
"Do you know who I am? If you kill me, my 37 wives will be absolutely devastated! Please spare me, for their sake! But also mostly mine!"

"I have traveled thousands of realities and no ship has ever fared so well against me as you. You have earned the right to not be killed by me. Please stop." The enemy captain sounds triumphant, but you can see the fear in his eyes.
"God, this is worse than the time we had to fight off an infestation of parasitic bat-worms! I can't believe I'm saying this, but we surrender!"
"We will not surrender! Okay that's a lie, we surrender. I really don't want to die."
"Ugh, I can't believe I've been brought to my knees by such an ugly bastard like you. Will you take our surrender, so my legend doesn't have to end in such a disappointing manner?"
"I'm too pretty to die! Wait, maybe I can buy this stupid idiot off with some junk... wait, is my mic on?" The ship goes silent, followed by an offer of surrender.
"Great, another scar for my face. I'd like to live past today, even if it means I'm going to be the mutilated amputee that you've left me as. Can I buy your mercy, perhaps?"
TEXT_FIGHT_MULTIVERSE_TRAVELER: "Federation, you are the next of many kills that I foresee in my future! Let us duel!"
"What a disgusting ship you have there! I shall be doing the Multiverse a favor by ridding it from existence."
"A fellow Renegade? A true pleasure to meet you here, new friend! Now die."
"Crap, this isn't the solid gold reality. Oh, there's a ship here. Men, get ready for battle!"

"Where the hell are we? This is what we get for not using a warp-bay... wait, Federation? God damn it, we're in another one of those civil war realities. Looks like we're fighting our way out of this one!"
A Multiverse ship jumps in a few seconds later, ready to pillage. There's no other option but to fight!
"Bow down to me, foolish ship! This reality now belongs to us!" You doubt any ship could conquer an entire reality on their own, but regardless it's time for a fight!
"Apologies stranger, it's really nothing personal that we have to kill you. Scrap's a hard commodity to come by! Well not really, but you can never have enough."
"Don't even bother trying to run, Federation! Your ship is forfeit to me now! Hahahah!"
From out of the tunnel comes a foreboding, yet strangely colored Renegade ship. It looks like talking it out isn't an option, because their guns are already firing!

It's a common philosophy among Renegades that all scrap they can get their hands on belongs to them. You're guilty of this quite often as well, but now another Renegade has arrived and sees you as their next target!
"Hello there, friend! I have a gift for you, would you like to see it?" You reluctantly ask what it is, only to be met by them charging forward in an offensive attack!
"Haha, I am but 4 parallel universes ahead of you! But I will not have won until I've defeated you in EVERY universe! Yahoo!" The ship moves in to attack.

"You have to help me. No matter where I go, people keep calling me a Renegade. HOW DO THEY KNOW?! My name is Dan, I work in real estate, I just bought this ship to give it a test spin, and now everyone wants to kill me. And... and I want to kill everyone! Something's terribly wro-AGH! GIVE ME YOUR MONEY OR DIE!"

"One Renegade to another, my luck's kinda gone to shit. I heard a rumor, a myth really... that when a Renegade dies, supposedly you wake up in another body and start all over again. Frankly, I'm kind of hoping you kill me. Who knows, maybe some day I'll wake up as you! Hahah! Heh..."

"You'll never believe what I just came back from! I swear to god, there was this like, big place at the center of everything. There was a talking can of beans, and god himself, except he was a Slug with a big ring... and there was a guy with a collection of hats, and a guy with a card that smelled weird, and... and they were ALL SLUGS. I'M GOING INSANE!" The deranged Renegade raises his weapons, turning to violence in his madness.

It's strange, seeing so many Renegades around nowadays. A long time ago, there only used to be a few; it certainly wasn't a popular title. But something about the adventure has drawn more people in. As the newcomer approaches you however, it seems one of your adventures is about to end.

"Father, is that you?! Have you come back to me? You old coot, I hate you! Get out of my LIFE!" You have no idea what the Renegade on the other end is talking about, but whether they're your child or not, they're about to see the business end of your guns.
TEXT_DEMANDS_MULTIVERSE_TRAVELER: A Renegade approaches, demanding you give them tribute. Will you give in to their demands, or fight your way through?
"Ah, what a welcome surprise to see a fellow Renegade! Unfortunately, I think you have something we want..."
"Stop right there, Federation vessel! We claim this beacon for our own, and you're in our territory! You'll have to give us tribute if you want to pass."
A Multiverse ship threatens you nearby, and it seems you might find yourself in a fight soon unless you can satisfy them with a tribute.

"Ah, I see you've already found your way to this reality. I'm sure you've found your collection of riches, and have plenty to share with us, right?" You suspect this is more than just a friendly request when their weapons swivel to face you!
TEXT_OUTPOST_FEDERATION: You receive a hail from the nearby Federation refueling station. "Hello!-" The other end is cut off briefly by a loud bang. "SHIT! OW! OH MY GOD! AGH!" The Federation captain returns on screen a moment later. "Ugh... ignore that. We recruited a couple rookies and one of them just dropped a box of fuel on my foot. Sorry about that. Despite my throbbing foot, it's good to see a friendly face! If you need anything, don't hesitate to ask!"

The Federation anthem blasts through your stereo, temporarily deafening you. An automatic message loops as you rush to turn down the volume. "FEDERATION!!! YEAH!!! FED! ER! A! TION!!!" Despite the overwhelming patriotism from the nearby station, all other business seems to be going as normal. You should be able to get free supplies here.

A Federation commander aboard the nearby station hails you. "Renegades! Some day I hope to visit Universe 0 myself, but in the meantime it's wonderful to have visitors from the core of the Federation itself. Whatever you need is yours. Go get those Rebel bastards!"
TEXT_OUTPOST_UNION: A friendly Union outpost hails you. "It's a good day for the Federation! We've heard the Rebels have had some setbacks getting to Node 17 because of insurrection within their own ranks! Haha, now ain't that poetry! In celebration, any friends of the Federation get our service on the house!"

"Normally, I wouldn't be inclined to do free handouts, but you Renegades are carrying the weight of the whole damn Multiverse on your back! I don't know how much I can stand behind all of Universe 0's decisions, but I can respect your mission! Whatever you need, I'm willing to provide."

A Union commander waves you over. "I made a mistake, siding with the Rebels in the Civil War. Anyone with a sensory organ can see now the Rebels almost tore this galaxy apart! I know it's not much, but if I can help you in any way it'll make me feel even a little bit better about my past."
TEXT_OUTPOST_ENGI: "Scanning for Federation Identification..." The Engi pauses as a few drones swarm over your ship, scanning it thoroughly. "Identification: retrieved. Goodwill protocols indicate Renegade beneficiaries must receive apt compensation for services."

A busy Harmony outpost is in the middle of receiving dozens of incoming and outgoing shipments at once, and yet it still manages to hail you. "Core processors overloaded - traffic has overwhelmed official capacity by 356%. However, capacity may be surpassed even further if Renegade captain deems necessary. You are permitted to: raise overcapacity levels by no more than 30%. Be quick."

A joint Harmony and Ministry outpost has been constructed nearby. While most of the Engi ignore you, a Zoltan officer hails you. "Greetings. In the eyes of the Federation we are all equals, and so I see it only honorable we extend you a warm welcome. Do you need any assistance?"
TEXT_OUTPOST_ZOLTAN: A Zoltan outpost, functioning also partly as a temple, hails you. "It is in the nature of Illesctrianism that we open our minds and accept all others." The Zoltan pokes a look at you. "You are... hard to accept. But I will consider it a test of my faith and accept you regardless. The services of this temple are at your disposal."

"The Ministry welcomes you, Renegade captain. These are dangerous, partisan days. I'm sure there are many things we disagree on, but let us put them past us today. What is it that ails you? If you could divulge such information, perhaps we could provide treatment."

"Ugh... Renegades..." The Zoltan captain makes a rude gesture with his hands before realizing he's on camera and is quickly embarrassed. "I mean... uhm... hello there! May the Great Eye bless you on this fine day! Whatever you need, I'm sure we can offer!"
TEXT_OUTPOST_ORCHID: A Floral monk hails you, speaking in sign language. "The Gathering welcomes all peaceful folk to these lands. Whether you have tasted the nectar of the sweet fruit of Cyrtal'y Mncolo or are but a simple traveler seeking refuge, we are grateful to offer it. What might we do for you today, captain?"

The nearby outpost seems to be a retrofitted terraforming platform that now acts as an emergency supply outpost. "The Federation has brought much prosperity to the Gathering. It is only right that we repay our debts." The Floral gestures towards the docking bay where a team awaits your ship.

"Our wealth is yours! There is no nobler system of economics than to ensure all receive an equal share to what they contribute to society. And you, you are the hopeful savior of our reality! It should seem only right that we owe you anything, anything at all!"
TEXT_OUTPOST_FREEMANTIS: "Oh yes yes it is Renegade that is approaching! Can barely containing excitement!" The Free Mantis commander of the nearby outpost takes a giant sniff from a bottle of pheromones. "YEAH!!!!!! I AM EXCITING! I GIVE YOU ANYTHING! I GIVE YOU FIRSTBORN, I GIVE YOU-" The Mantis promptly collapses, twitching slightly from the raw energy pumping through their veins. Nevertheless, a more able team awaits you in the docking bay.

You receive a hail from the nearby outpost, where a sobbing Free Mantis awaits you. "You are... so beautiful. So majestic, I deserving not of seeing you! Go, taking the free things and leave before I cry last of every tear!"

A hail comes in from a human Federation officer working aboard the nearby Free Mantis station. "I must say, these Free Mantis are... very interesting to work with. When I first was rescued from Rebel captivity by one, they kissed me and started praying at my feet. We're married now!" The Federation captain pauses before remembering what he was talking about. "Er... sorry, when you live among the Free Mantis too long you start to ramble about nothing. Is there any assistance you're in need of? I'm sure the rest of the crew here would be honored to help you."
TEXT_OUTPOST_CRYSTAL: "Aliens, how curious. Ycathine knowns what kind of mysterious tales you could tell!" The Crystal yawns. "Or that's what I used to think. Unfortunately, you all seem quite boring. That said, boring or not, I've pledged my duties to the Federation and I intend to uphold them. What do you need?"

The Crystalline station nearby locks all of its weapons onto you, threatening to open fire. "STOP RIGHT THERE! THIS IS IMPERIAL SPACE! GET LOST OR- oh crypt, you're a Renegade! Wow! My apologies. Feel free to dock, and I'll see to it my crew can provide whatever resources you're in need of."

The Empire has made remarkable progress in colonizing the space they've only just recently moved into. An outpost waving both the Imperial and Federation flags hails you, offering various free services.
TEXT_OUTPOST_OUTCAST: In the strange territory the outcasts call their home, it's not unusual to find all sorts of odd things. Still, the Federation outpost here comes as a surprise! A welcome one to be sure however, and as soon as you approach they open their hangar doors to allow you inside.

An outcast aboard the nearby Federation refueling station hails you. "I emigrated to the Gathering in what feels like forever ago. But being a part of the Federation is one of the greatest honors I could ever have dreamed to serve. Allow me to provide anything I can to assist you, Captain."

It's a bit surprising, although not entirely shocking, to find a Federation outpost here in Outcast territory. A crew of all sorts of species works aboard, and the commanding officer offers you free services in return for your commitment to saving reality.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE: As you jump into the system a pirate advances on your position. They are refusing all hails. Prepare for a fight.
Soon after arriving in the system you are hailed by a small cruiser. "What good fortune that we happen to run into each other. Nothing personal, but you have some information we need!"
The only other ship at this beacon messages you: "Finally, after months of waiting, someone has fallen into our trap!"
You barely have time to register jump completion before your ship warns you of an incoming ship with weapons hot.
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_MERCENARY: You spot a small black market at this beacon, but as you approach it a mercenary ship swings around and attacks. "Hah! What luck of ours. Our clients came here to hire us to scout you out, and here you are in the very same sector!"
"Wouldn't you know it, it's the captain of the hour! I assure you, it's nothing personal. Just, we've been given quite a sum in return for your head. You're a Renegade, so I'm sure you understand."
Seems someone's put a price on your head, because a mercenary is trailing you, weapons online! No surprise, but seems you'll have to take care of this first.

Strangely, Renegades and Mercenaries rarely get along. To the mercs, Renegades lack the honor and distinction the Syndicate brings them. The nearby ship seems to have taken that difference personally and lunges towards you!
TEXT_ENCOUNTER_SMUGGLER: "I spy with my little eye a ship with some fine gear I'm sure will sell for a pretty penny on the market! Surrender yourselves or suffer the wrath of my cannons!"

Smugglers rarely show aggression for fear of losing their precious cargo. Yet - when their stock is dry, sometimes the odd captain will try their luck and seize the cargo of a passing ship. Seems a bit risky to pick on a ship like yours, but that's their mistake.

"How quaint. I just sold off all my stock and here I was thinking I'd have to make my trek back to Argeonn when you showed up! Thank you kindly for the generous donation, stranger!" You aren't sure what the smugglers are referring to until weapons pop out of their hull!
A smuggler approaches, clearly intending to steal rather than to sell. Prepare for combat!
TEXT_SLAVER_FRIENDLY: You recognize the nearby ship as a well-known Tiiikaka slave trader. He hails you and offers you "laborers" for cheap.
A shifty looking slaver approaches, hailing with offers of promising and willing workers for a reasonable price.
"My friend, my friend, I empathize with what surely must be a great labor shortage aboard your vessel. Renegades don't have a long life expectancy, after all. Perhaps I can offer a solution?"
"Feeling frisky, friend? I can offer you something to help keep you warm at night, heheh... Not your thing? Well, I'm sure my 'wares' might have other uses aboard your vessel."
An unwashed slaver appears on your screen, promoting the fact his workers will do anything you tell them, satisfaction guaranteed or your money back.
It's sometimes appalling how freely slavers move about peddling their cargo. As a rather risky move, a slaver seems to have picked you out as a potential client.
TEXT_SLAVER_CHOICE: An especially aggressive slaver ship approaches you. "Hand over one of your crew-members and the rest of you can go free unharmed. We promise not to hurt them too much."
TEXT_MERCENARY_FRIENDLY: The Syndicate has no shortage of guns for hire who'll do just about anything for the right price. The vessel here is no exception.

A ship hails you: "Greetings! It seems you're having some difficulty with the Rebellion. I'd love to help, but I can't afford the upkeep required on this hunk of junk I'm flying... maybe we can come to an arrangement?"
"Got scrap? Need something done? Well, I'm the man for you!" The mercenary at this beacon flashes a toothy grin to reassure you.

Thanks to Vael and the Syndicate, mercenaries are swarming the galaxy. Their less-than-legal services are in high demand, and one is waiting nearby for ships like you that might find some use in their services.
A ship with Syndicate markings orbits a nearby backwater station. You receive a shady message: "Anything is possible, for the right price."
"I've caught word... a Renegade? You must be busy. Busy busy, indeed! I understand your mission is quite important. Maybe, for a litle payment, I can make life easier for you?"
TEXT_MERCENARY_CHOICE: Upon completing your jump, you receive a message from a nearby mercenary. "Greetings and welcome to our beacon! For a small fee, we'll let you continue on your way."

"Well well well, if it isn't just the ship of the hour! I just had a client come by and pay me a handsome sum to kill you. Though... I'll make you a unique deal. Pay me the same rate, and I'll let you go."
"Ah, hello my friends! It is most unfortunate, for you, that we meet here in such a way! My clients just left, and they've given me quite the sum of money. Perhaps you could... match their pricing?"

"Today is a wonderful day, Captain! I have been paid a bountiful amount of scrap with the task of killing you! I'm afraid I will have to follow through with this... unless you could... give us some more scrap?"
TEXT_SMUGGLER_FRIENDLY: An Argeonn smuggler spins you a tale of the dangers of the open galaxy before pushing his wares. You doubt any of his contraband is exactly legal, but maybe it's worth a look?
You've heard stories, both good and bad, of Argeonn and their solicitations. A cocky and haphazardly shaven smuggler extends an offer to sell you some 'premium gear' for what he claims is dirt cheap.
"What great fortune it is that we've met each other on this occasion. You have scrap, and I have equipment. Perhaps we can arrange a deal?"
"There's no limit to the treasures my cargo carries, captain. And they can all be yours too! Just, for a price..."
The Federation is fairly lax on Argeonn and its smugglers, as their inter-dimensional services make for cheap transportation. With little to fear, a smuggler nearby peddles you some gear.

"I almost joined the Renegade business once... but it just wasn't the life for me. I much prefer Argeonn, I get the adrenaline rush with far less of the risk. You wouldn't happen to need any gear, would you?"
TEXT_SMUGGLER_CHOICE: A smuggler approaches, brandishing their weapons but not their contraband. "Sorry we meet on unfavorable terms, but we're starved for fuel and I'm afraid you're our only shot to get out of here before the patrols catch us. No hard feelings, it's just business."
TEXT_RUINS: Before you lies ruins unlike anything you've ever seen. Entirely black and cubical, the skeletons of a few massive warships remain at this beacon. Maybe you can salvage something here?

A humongous cubical mega-structure lies in your wake, transmitting a short but undecipherable message. Surely if this thing still has enough power to send a message, maybe it has something worth taking?

You appear to be witnessing the aftermath of a terribly damaged and brutally torn apart mega-class carrier ship, larger than your cruiser or even the Federation's largest fleet ships. Even stranger, the wreck is entirely black and cubical. Maybe it contains something worth salvaging?

The remains of a couple strange looking Auto-ships, certainly not of Rebel design though similar in tech according to scans, are scattered around the remains of a massive cubical cruiser. Maybe there's more tech aboard the ship?

The wreck of a dated and foreign vessel is being pelted by a small and thinly dispersed asteroid field. Though the asteroids have clearly caused some damage, the storm has mostly passed by, and won't be an issue for much longer. Maybe something of value is left behind?
TEXT_RUINS_TRANSLATE: "The nebulas are our next goal. Supplies are thin, but there are tales that the phantoms hoard unspeakable treasures in the clouds. They are mighty, prolific in population size, and a very proud people. But not even the proudest of beings shan't yield to our weapons. Hear me, the Dynasty will have met no match as relentless as ourselves. The days of peace between our kinds are over. The war demands of it."

"We do not know where they came from. Queen Y told us that we were divine. That we were the masters of reality. Yet, the newcomers... they claim they come from beyond, through a tunnel. They call it the [word unknown]. The engineers made no mention of such a place. They speak such strange words. Dreams of gods? A living universe? I see a great threat in them, but the Royals say they will not hurt us. Some kind of pact, a gift of the outskirts in return for peace. I do not foresee good in this, but it is not my decision to be made."

"I encountered one of the metalloids the other day. In broken dialect it asked me if I could spare it ammunition. To arm himself against my crew, I thought? Nay, he merely scrambled it down his throat, gave a garbled thanks, and drifted away. I sometimes question the origins of them. I would study them, see what makes them tick, but I can never get close enough to capture one before they slip away. It is infuriating. I have never known such failure."

"The crystalline, the attendant whom I was given by the Royal appointment, tells me strange stories of life in his world. What a simple creature. Why do the Royals painstake us to endure with these mortal beings? They birth, they age, they die. We do not. Even the Commonwealth does not toil in such fashion as them. Perhaps they are glad to have been spared? The phantoms knew no such luck. I hope to dispose of him soon. Perhaps the appointment will grant me a servant who speaks less next time."

"Nine months I have served aboard this vessel for Ambassador L. It is insufferable. Life in the slums of the Commonwealth, as grueling as it were, was more pleasant than this. I am treated like... like a crystalline! A mortal! The Royals have forgotten that we too are [word unknown]. I will not stand for this. Tomorrow, I will overthrow the Ambassador. I will leave this place! The Commonwealth will rise, it will prosper! I just know it!"

"They say the war is going well. I am not so certain. There are rumors, very concerning rumors, of a genocidal plot by the Royals. They talk so often of the Commonwealth, the gears of war. I am afraid they may be the next target. Yes, it will be the enemy. But... the enemy is us. If they are truly parallel to ourselves, should we not expect equal retaliation? I fear the worst."

"I heard a strange story the other day. They say that the crystalline emperor, Ycathine, had a feud with Queen Y. Stranger yet, he left the palace. Alive. Unheard of... no mortal has ever challenged the Royals and lived! What are we coming to? Have we lost our dignity, to allow ourselves to be spit upon by repugnant beings? In my outrage I slaughtered the last of my servants. It is a small demonstration, but it is a fitting one."

"War with the Dynasty was a mistake. Not that I fear we will lose. Nay. It is just that... they are so numerous. We were aware of this fact, but not of the severity of it. Our victory is certain, but when will it be? We are running out of time. The Royals continue to lie, they say the war is going spectacularly. But if we keep distracting ourselves with petty squabbles, soon even their tone may shift. They say the Reaper never yields. I did not believe it when I heard it. But, there is too much evidence now for it not to be true."

"While exploring the other day I came across a remarkable system. A beautiful world populated by strange creatures. With almost no landmasses, the oceans stretched so far I feel as though they could engulf all of [word unknown]. The primitive species here will not bother us. They may even provide great entertainment. I think I shall build a resort here. The Royals are always looking for new ways to spend their leisure."

"The Monolith looks well. It is a marvelous work of art, and to think inside sits [word unknown]! There are few habitable systems around it, but those that are, I wonder if some day they will birth life capable of appreciating the Monolith's beauty. Should the war go south, should there be left no other trace of us, at least the Monolith shall stand proud as an eternal grace of our perfection!"
