TEXT_SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_GENERIC_2_CHOICE: Why do you keep saying that?
I'm getting worried. Why are you repeating that?
Stop repeating that, it's getting annoying.
Are you just going to keep repeating that?
Why do you keep repeating that same thing?
Is there a reason you're repeating yourself?
I know, you've said that before already.
Do you always repeat things like this?
Is this some kind of joke? Why are you repeating yourself?
You keep saying that, over and over.
Are you even listening? Why are you repeating yourself?
TEXT_STORE_REBEL_HOSTILE: The source of the distress beacon appears to be a small market under attack from a Rebel!
A merchant ship here is under attack from Rebels. They're helpless against them, and you may be their only chance at survival.
A Rebel ship is assaulting a small black market. Perhaps if you can rescue them, they'll sell to you.
TEXT_STORE_AUTO_HOSTILE: An automated Rebel vessel has opened fire on a small marketplace, presumably because they were dealing to Feds!
You receive a distress call from a small trading outpost. "Help! Our automated ship has gone haywire and is attacking us!"
You notice a black market under fire from an Auto-ship nearby. Looks like even the Rebels aren't pleased with pirates.
TEXT_STORE_PIRATE_HOSTILE: The distress beacon appears to be originating from a small, civilian-run market under attack from pirates!

Pirates don't always get along well with each other, and the scene at this beacon is evident. A hostile pirate ship is firing on another pirate station. The station's fate looks bleak unless you step in.
You notice a Federation merchant vessel being blockaded by pirates. This must be the source of the distress beacon.
TEXT_STORE_MANTIS_HOSTILE: A Mantis appears to have decided to prey on a nearby unarmed merchant vessel. While you don't find it particularly intelligent to travel into Mantis space without weapons, they're still civilians and they won't last long.
It appears a Mantis and a smuggler are duelling it out at this beacon, arguing over prices.
A Mantis is firing at a small Engi merchant trying to get out of the sector. It's not likely the Engi will last long.
TEXT_STORE_MORPH_HOSTILE: You didn't think you'd be seeing Morph ships acting quite aggressive as this... it appears a Morph is attacking a small Shell merchant ship!
You receive a hail from a distant Federation supply vessel. "Help, I think I accidentally angered the blob things! I don't know what they're saying but they're really scaring me man!"
"OOG! URP UPR TAGLE SPACK!" A ship full of Morphs begin to chant as they circle around a merchant ship. Looks like they could use some help.
TEXT_TONYS: An advertisement appears on your screen as you approach, depicting a slim and well-kept Leech. "Hey there, I'm Mr. Senior. Tony Senior, that is! Owner of Tony's! I'd like to announce our brand new partnership with Hektar Industries! Come on and stop by!" You swear you've seen this ad before long ago. This definitely isn't "brand new", and "Tony's" is a massive retail chain. For some reason they're looping this same ancient ad, but that hardly matters.

Looks like the nearby station is a "Tony's", one of the only Leech-owned as well as the largest retail chain in the Multiverse. Besides the usual commodities, these stores are infamous for selling military goods suspiciously labeled as "gardening appliances".

Seems an advertisement from the local Tony's is playing over your intercom. Strange to find such a large retail chain offering military weapons, but considering they also sell second-hand organs and prostitutes, it's not that out of place.

"Hey there folks! Come on in and stop by your local Tony's! We've got uh... um... come on and stop by!" Despite the unconvincing pitch, you've heard of these places. Owned by a mysterious and elusive Leech tycoon, "Tony's" serves as the Multiverse's largest retail chain, and for good reason.

A Slug ship flies past but stops when they see you. Their captain half-heartedly hands you a flier advertising "great deals!" on Hektar-brand modular weaponry(tm) being sold at the nearby Tony's. The ship jumps away, but you figure the reputation of the Leech retail chain outcompetes the rudeness of the Slugs.
A passive-aggressive jingle plays on the stereo, broadcasting from the nearby retail store. "Come on to Tony's! Come on to Tony's! YOU. WILL. SHOP."

The bright colors and simple yet recognizeable logo of the nearby store brings back memories. The infamous brand of "Tony's" is known for a lot of things, some good, some bad, and some bizarre. A lot of strange myths are centered around its founder Tony Sr., from his involvement in the mafia to a dark past with Zulfiqar. You have no idea if any of these are true, but their stores are known for quality merchandise, and you figure it's worth a look.
TEXT_TONY_NOTHING: Despite the colorful isles and fascinating trinkets, there isn't much here to excite a mercenary captain like yourself. Though, if you ever need a battery powered tongue trimmer or a complete set of action figures from the hit Leech soap opera "Orfaces of Rilla", you suppose you know where to look.

There isn't much in the store that interests you, disappointing considering all the tales you've heard of these places. A rather flirtatious Vampweed cashier attempts to get your number, but the bloodstains on her uniform warn you not to give her your time.

Several alien species roam the stores alongside you, but no one makes any attempts to speak to one another. Not that you could if you wanted to, because the music playing over the intercom is so loud the items on the shelves are vibrating. It's better if you don't stick around in case you lose your hearing.

A few ancient posters from a long-past Eargen election are still hung up outside. Considering no president has been democratically elected in the Republic for years, it's quite ironic, but a quick chat with the surprisingly friendly staff reveal that it's just become a joke among them. Besides that interaction, there isn't much reason to stick around.

You stop by the station but don't find anything of interest on sale besides the military supplies. You take a quick detour to the store's bathroom, but the uncomfortable sloshing noises from inside convince you to stay away and just wait until you're back on the ship.
TEXT_HEKTAR_STORE: Looks like a Hektar representative is orbiting a nearby marketplace, painted a gash shade of neon yellow which stands out from miles away. Hopefully whatever goods are inside aren't as obnoxiously vibrant.
An overenthusiastic employee of Hektar greets you. "HEY! HI! HELLO! HOWDY! HOW DO YOU DO? PLEASSSE BUY THINGSSS! I CAN'T SSSSEE MY FAMILY AGAIN UNTIL I MEET MY QUOTA!"

You arrive at the store, but the ship meant to greet you is deathly silent. After several subsequent hails the captain is startled awake. "Ah god damn it, you woke me up! Yeah yeah whatever, come sssshop or sssome ssshit."
A loud advertisement blasts over your stereo, with an obese Slug waving his arms in the air and begging you to come and shop. Seems like unfortunate placement considering you're already here.
These Hektar stores sure are plentiful. It's almost concerning how much of this sector is just stores, but you suppose it's better than deadly Rebels.
A sleezy clerk with grease stains on his chest eyes your ship. "Eh, a Federation ssship? You musssst have money! Gimme gimme!"
STORES_HACKED: A hacker ship is preaching deals to nearby ships. "Federation, aye? No matter, sssso long asss you got ssome ssscrap, you're welcome here."

A civilian is running a small shop here. "The hackers have allowed me to run my store under their control, so long as 90% of the proceeds go to them. So please, buy as much as you can so I can afford food tonight."
EMPTY: Your scans reveal a mining base on a nearby planet long since abandoned. No life signs detected.
This beacon has been built for a nearby civilian space-station. No one hails your ship.
TEXT_EMPTY_START: This sector is still under heavy construction to make way for supply depots and Multiverse warp-bays. This beacon has not yet undergone industrialization, and is empty as far as you can see.
NEBULA_NOTHING_LIST: You can't see anything through the thick gases surrounding your ship. Without knowing what is out there, all you can do is wait for your FTL to charge.
Without active sensors you have no other option but to look out of the view-ports in apprehension. It's eerily quiet.
As you wait for the FTL drive to charge, you half expect to be ambushed at any moment. However, no attack comes...
You feel naked without functioning sensors. You half expect a Rebel ship to appear from behind a cloud at any moment, but none come.
Your crew are constantly looking out of the windows, checking for hostiles. They jump at every creak and moan of the ship. The tension is almost palpable...
You nervously glance out the windows but the only thing to greet you is more clouds and silence.
You cycle through wide-band comm channels as soon as you arrive. Nothing but static.
With the sensors down, you spend a good deal of time staring out the window. It is, you must admit, rather beautiful here.
There's nothing here, save for vast swirls of gas reflecting rays from a distant sun.
EMPTY_COREWORLDS: A small Civilian settlement is nearby, well protected by Militia patrols. You don't bother trying to contact the settlement.
Despite all the civilian infrastructure in this sector, this beacon appears to be mostly empty.
No pirates, politicians, or people of any kind populate this place.
This beacon offers a break from the busy happenings of the civilians in this sector.
For once, a beacon where you aren't having to save a civilian from a pirate ship. You relax and do something on the ship.
A heavily protected Militia caravan is passing through this beacon. They won't respond to your hails, and attacking them would be practically suicide. You lay low and do something on the ship.
EMPTY_MILITIA: A small training exercise is going on nearby between several Militia ships. You feel it's best not to get involved.
You attempt to hail a small outpost nearby, but they decline your attempts at communication. You aren't too bothered by it, but you wish they hadn't been so rude.

A pirate vessel flies past, but before you can react they are promptly followed by a Militia ship. The Militia ship is much faster though and swiftly catches the pirates and starts to make arrests. You try not to get involved and slip away.
EMPTY_FED_NORMAL: The wreckage of a single Federation ship drifts nearby. There's not much there left to salvage, and you feel dirty even considering scraping it.
This beacon is rather unremarkable. It must simply serve as a connection for passing ships.
The Federation has been hurt greatly in this reality, and this system is filled with many abandoned Federation structures. There doesn't appear to be anything worth scrapping.
A few Federation and Civilian ships are passing through this system, but none respond to your hails.
EMPTY_ENGI: The complex arrangements of ship hulls and FTL drive capacitors floating abandoned in space suggest the Engi were here not too long ago; but no longer.
You arrive at a green planet with great plains and rolling waterfalls. It would be of little interest to the Engi nearby.

You have arrived near an Engi construction yard. Most Engi maintain their bi-pedal appearance out of habit but here you see a number of Engi hives working together to create massive organic machines adept at building ships. Truly a sight to behold.

Even though each "individual" Engi is made up of trillions of nano-machines, their culture still revolves around traditional social interactions. A nearby station seems to be constructed for entertainment of passing Engi travellers.

You see a number of Engi space stations and fleets nearby. Despite looking like piles of junk loosely tied together they are actually a model of efficiency. They just lack a certain aesthetic emphasis in their constructions.
This system appears quite peaceful. You're not sure how long it'll last between the combined threats of the Rebels and Mantis.
There are a number of merchant ships passing through the area despite the threat of Mantis invasion. No doubt interested in buying the efficient technology of the Engi.
You see a small Rebel carrier in the distance. You lay low and try to blend in with the other traffic. However it's surprising to see a Rebel military ship alone deep in Engi space.
The Engi seem to have avoided this particular node, along with every other life-form. You keep your eyes peeled for reasons why, but spin up the FTL without event.
A cluster of Engi satellites in orbit of a nearby planet are the only clue the mechanical species was ever here. You have other places to be.
EMPTY_HARMONY: The complex arrangements of ship hulls and FTL drive capacitors floating abandoned in space suggest the Engi were here not too long ago; but no longer.
You arrive at a green planet with great plains and rolling waterfalls. It would be of little interest to the Engi nearby.

You have arrived near an Engi construction yard. Most Engi maintain their bi-pedal appearance out of habit but here you see a number of Engi hives working together to create massive organic machines adept at building ships. Truly a sight to behold.

Even though each "individual" Engi is made up of trillions of nano-machines, their culture still revolves around traditional social interactions. A nearby station seems to be constructed for entertainment of passing Engi travellers.

You see a number of Engi space stations and fleets nearby. Despite looking like piles of junk loosely tied together they are actually a model of efficiency. They just lack a certain aesthetic emphasis in their constructions.
This system appears quite peaceful. You're not sure how long it'll last between the combined threats of the Rebels and Mantis.
There are a number of merchant ships passing through the area despite the threat of Mantis invasion. No doubt interested in buying the efficient technology of the Engi.
You see a small Rebel carrier in the distance. You lay low and try to blend in with the other traffic. However it's surprising to see a Rebel military ship alone deep in Engi space.
The Engi seem to have avoided this particular node, along with every other life-form. You keep your eyes peeled for reasons why, but spin up the FTL without event.
A cluster of Engi satellites in orbit of a nearby planet are the only clue the mechanical species was ever here. You have other places to be.
EMPTY_SEPARATIST: A cluster of nanobots floats nearby, but ignores your ship. It dissipates quickly, leaving you to your own devices.
Separatists Engi like to keep to themselves, and will usually avoid other ships. The Separatist nearby jumps away as soon as you approach.
You believe this beacon to be empty, though it's impossible to tell with all of the microscopic nanobots floating around in empty space.
Some space junk left over from what was presumably two Engi ships... merging. Unfortunately, none of it is worthy of salvaging.
Not an Engi ship in sight. You figure it's safe to do something on the ship.
EMPTY_ZOLTAN: There are some mineral-rich asteroids here that the Zoltan have left idle, but you've none of the necessary equipment to mine them.
You have to admit - Zoltan space is a beautiful and peaceful place indeed. However, re-engaging the FTL and finishing your mission is your priority, not sight-seeing.
A light asteroid field is entering the atmosphere of a nearby planet - a fireworks show on a galactic scale. There's little for it but to take in the ambience and program the next jump.
You stumble upon some Zoltan military vessels engaging in combat training. Their Energy Shields are impressive, but you note how quickly beam and ion weaponry take them down.
You don't have time to hail the Zoltan ship that was waiting at this beacon before it jumps away. They are a careful race.
A Zoltan shipyard is stationed at this beacon. You admire the display of hundreds of glowing Zoltans performing delicate exterior work on a massive transport ship.
A message broadcast from a nearby planet announces the presence of an ancient Zoltan monastery available for visiting. Likely just a tourist trap, but still too bad you don't have the time to visit.
EMPTY_CAPITAL: A group of Ministry ships are docked with a small station nearby. The chatter on the comms seems entirely political talk, and you decide not to intervene.
This beacon is bland and boring, similar to the typical political discussions between the citizens of this sector.
A vaguely interesting looking temple selling low priced souvenirs directs an advertisement towards your ship, but you quickly decline.
A Zoltan Peace Brigade is busy harassing a nearby star system for tax evasion. You decide not to get involved.
A Zoltan colony rests nearby, their Zoltan Shield online and weapons at maximum power. They clearly aren't interested in visitors.
A few pirate ships jump away as soon as you approach, leaving you to wonder what they were doing.
EMPTY_MONK: The ship computer informs you this beacon is considered sacred ground. You aren't sure why, because the beacon seems rather empty to you.
This beacon appears empty, other than the swirling nebulous gases. You wonder why the Zoltan Monks hide in these nebulas, and what they're hiding from.
Unlike other nebula sectors, you feel relatively safe in the thick gasses of these nebulas.
No ships can be found at this beacon. You can use this as a resting place.
This beacon is even more peaceful than the rest of the sector, with not a single ship to be found.
EMPTY_DUSKBRINGER: This beacon is too quiet. You're wary of a trick, but no ships appear. You relax, and focus on doing something on the ship.
The ruins of several ships are still here, but their bones have already been picked clean. You bet the Duskbringers had something to do with this.
A Zoltan brigade protects this beacon, a rare display of anti-Dusk measures being taken by the Zoltan government. They refuse to open communications with you.
The cold war between the Zoltans and the Federation is responsible for the evolution of the Duskbringers. Luckily, none of their ships are present at this beacon.
EMPTY_ORCHID: Orchid space is famous for being calm and peaceful. This beacon exemplifies that, with no ships in sight.
EMPTY_CRYSTAL: As soon as you arrive, all of the ships docked at a nearby station scatter and jump while the station itself uses some form of cloak technology to disappear. They mustn't like outsiders here...

No ships are in range, so you take the time to scan the area. It seems like every planet you've seen so far shows signs of highly developed habitation without overpopulation. They must have a very structured and well regulated society.
There appears to be no one living near this node, a rare sight in this highly developed sector.

You arrive near a civilian settlement. It looks like their homes, ships and stations all rely heavily on an intriguing crystalline material. You wonder how they are able to create so much of this substance, and what benefits it will provide to the other races of the galaxy.
A few merchant ships pass nearby but they are either ignoring your hails or their computer hasn't yet been adjusted to work through the same frequencies...
EMPTY_PIRATE: As soon as you arrive, a small ship de-cloaks behind yours. You immediately power up the shields and weapons, but they continue on their trajectory unimpressed. You try to calm your nerves.
A small pirate ship messages you, "That sure is a shiny ship you got there." You fire a warning shot across their bow and they respond, "Hey! No need for violence! It was just a comment..."
The only thing within scanning range is an old abandoned mining structure and a resupply station. They appear to have been picked clean by marauders.

You arrive to have a small fleet of Engi ships target you with a message, "Piracy results in negative societal impact. Not permitted." You assure them of your honest intentions and they allow you to pass.
EMPTY_BLACKMARKET: This beacon is noticeable only because of how empty it is, a rarity in this busy sector.
Not one speck of purple or white paint in sight. You relax and consider this a much needed break.
A few ships here are trading, but none respond to your hails. Probably an illegal sale, you figure.
An abandoned trading port is here, probably due to little business. Upon further inspection, they were selling antique snow globes. Nothing worth taking.
EMPTY_HACKED: In this dangerous sector you can never be certain of anything, including the apparent emptiness of this beacon. After a few minutes pass and nothing bad happen, you begin to feel safe again.
This beacon is empty, something unexpected in a sector like this.
Deactivated civilian infrastructure drifts nearby. You're too wary of a potential trap to approach it, so you use this beacon as a welcome break instead.
A few civilian ships scatter as you approach. You're left alone at the beacon.
An empty beacon in a sector full of tricks such as this is suspicious, but nothing seems wrong about the nearby system.
EMPTY_REBEL: You enter a system bustling with Rebel activity. Supply freighters and re-supply stations are dwarfed by a few heavy warships. Luckily, no one seems to be paying attention to small cruisers. No ships are scanning or messaging you.

You arrive near a small Rebel refueling depot. Your ship is being scanned multiple times so they must recognize you, but there appears to be no combat-ready ships in the vicinity. The only message you receive is a denial to your request to dock at the depot.
There is not much of interest nearby. A small sun in the distance with a few orbiting planets in nearby space provide little of interest.
EMPTY_JERRY: A stray balloon floats past, drifting aimlessly into the nothingness. How and why, you aren't sure, but this is why you should always hold on carefully.
In this surprisingly friendly sector, you've finally come across a beacon with nothing but silence.
There are no ships to be seen here, which is particularly unusual in Rebel space. Where's all the murderous soldiers out to get your head?
EMPTY_REBELHOLD: You enter a system bustling with Rebel activity. Supply freighters and re-supply stations are dwarfed by a few heavy warships. Luckily, no one seems to be paying attention to small cruisers. No ships are scanning or messaging you.

You arrive near a small Rebel refuelling depot. Your ship is being scanned multiple times so they must recognize you, but there appears to be no combat-ready ships in the vicinity. The only message you receive is a denial to your request to dock at the depot.
There is not much of interest nearby. A small sun in the distance with a few orbiting planets in nearby space provide little of interest.
EMPTY_AUTO: An abandoned shipyard lays far in the distance. It doesn't appear to be worth salvaging.
The empty husk of what was once an Auto-ship drifts nearby, scrapped well beyond the point of return by pirates.
This beacon is suprisingly empty, one of the few beacons the Rebels have not yet ravaged with their Auto-tech.
It appears the automated expanse of the shipyard has not yet reached this beacon.
Other than some distant scaffolding at this beacon, it's void of anything of interest.
EMPTY_MANTIS: At this point you almost expect a fight with the Mantis, but this beacon appears to be entirely devoid of other ships. You take the time to catch your breath and double check the ship's systems.
The only thing this beacon offers is a view of deep space and a brief respite from battles. For some this must be a welcome refuge.

A nearby Mantis mining operation is clearly using heavy Engi slave labor. You briefly consider the possibility of emancipating the slaves, but the Mantis presence is too formidable. You decide to lay low.
There aren't so many parts of Mantis space that aren't dotted by the wrecks of battles past, but this is one of them. You take a deep breath and prepare to move on.
There's nothing here but space debris and some uninhabitable planetoids.
You fancy you see something moving in the shadow of the beacon, but all remains still.
EMPTY_FREEMANTIS: A Free Mantis clan lays inactive nearby. You approach, but they hail you with a warning to stay away. You figure it's best to abide their wishes.
There is no sign of any permanent habitation near this beacon, only a lone Free Mantis ship that jumps away before you have the chance to hail.
The occasional space junk flies by, but nothing worth for even firing from a Flak cannon.
There are no ships in sight, not even of the Free Mantis. We have some time to spend to ourselves.
EMPTY_ROCK: You receive a message meant to degrade you as aliens. You half expect an attack but it seems to have come from a small civilian shuttle.
No one bothers your ship as you float among numerous space stations and mining platforms. The Rock certainly run efficient operations.

You arrive and detect signs of battle. A few ships are taking passes at each other near a small station. You don't know if it's a territory issue, a contest or a rite of passage but you decide it's best to stay out of it.
There's not much at this beacon. Just a few abandoned depots, stripped clean.
A few freighters pass by but they refuse all communications. Must not want to sully their reputation by talking with foreigners.
You see a small trading post and ask about refuelling but they respond, "Go away! We don't serve your kind here."
You see a Zoltan merchant and ask about his wares. He responds, "Sorry, but it took years to gain their trust. I can't be seen communicating with you. I hope you understand." He cuts communications.
EMPTY_ROCKHOME: The Rock Elders keep a very strict eye on all of their systems. It seems their authoritarian ways have had a very negative effect on the nearby system, because there isn't a single ship roaming about.
Despite your very presence in this sector being a crime, no Rock ships stop you. A few civilians linger before jumping away, but you are undisturbed.
It's a miracle to find an empty beacon here, one free from the brutal enforcers who patrol this sector and the ever hostile citizens.

You can't remember many tales of the Rock Inquisition from Universe 0, but you're sure just a horribly violent war had terrible casualties on the Rock population. This beacon is unnervingly empty of all life, and you can only wonder if it is a consequence of the warmongering of the Elders' pre-Federation years.
A Rock patrol orbits around the beacon, but luckily they seem rather laid back. They hail you, "We won't tell if you don't either."
EMPTY_LOSTSUN: A few Lost Sun fortifications are scattered about, but none contact you. You take this time to rest.
You are greeted by nothing more than an unusual break in the usual busy wartime activities of this sector.
A nearby Lost Sun station cloaks as soon as you jump in. You take the message and fly away until you're alone.
EMPTY_SLUG: You arrive at the beacon and are relieved at the sight of open space. Nebulas are terribly claustrophobic.
This beacon marks a 'small' gap in the nebula. No colonies or ships in scanning distance.
You are relieved to see your sensors blink back on after the jump. No ships detected.
The Slugs rely heavily on their telepathic powers and are reluctant to give up that advantage by extending beyond nebulas. It's unlikely you'll encounter any this far from the clouds.
You arrive in an area clear of nebula and quickly check to see if the sensors are working. Everything is fine and no ships are detected in the vicinity.
NEBULA_EMPTY_SLUG: When it comes to Slugs, no news is not necessarily good news. However, if they are watching, they don't seem to want to confront you.
It's not unusual to feel paranoia in a Slug controlled nebula, but for once, it is unfounded.
Either this part of Slug space is deserted, or it's too dense for even Slugs to detect your presence. Time to move.
This area of the nebula seems entirely empty until a small Slug transport and its escorts emerges suddenly from through the clouds, only to disappear again in a matter of seconds.

You explore around the beacon and are shocked when a rock the size of a small moon suddenly looms ahead of you. Scans reveal the solid-looking rock is just a husk, almost entirely mined out of useful minerals.

There are a number of small stations for travellers in the area, lit up by guiding lights and advertisements. Only Slug ships are docked so you decide it's better to avoid a confrontation and steer clear.
EMPTY_SHELL: You arrive at the beacon and are relieved at the sight of open space. Nebulas are terribly claustrophobic.
This beacon marks a 'small' gap in the nebula. No colonies or ships in scanning distance.
You are relieved to see your sensors blink back on after the jump. No ships detected.
You arrive in an area clear of nebula and quickly check to see if the sensors are working. Everything is fine and no ships are detected in the vicinity.
NEBULA_EMPTY_SHELL: Shell space isn't quite as calm as you expected, but it's always nice to see a break from the other ships here.
You catch a brief glimpse of a Shell ship before it disappears into the nebula, but you doubt you'd be able to catch up with them. The beacon is otherwise empty.
No ships, not even of Shell origin, inhabit this beacon.
Shell space isn't too developed compared to many other regions, so it's not too unsurprising to find empty beacons such as this.
Much of Shell space has been closed off to be used for scientific purposes. You aren't sure what those purposes are, but your computer won't give any more information. Still, no one bothers you here.
EMPTY_COALITION: The wrecks of a few Federation ships float nearby, but nothing appears salvageable. It appears a battle just happened here, but whatever happened to the other ships involved you don't know.
The only thing this beacon offers is a view of deep space and a brief respite from battles. For some this must be a welcome refuge.

You jump out of your seat when you see there is another Coalition ship nearby. However, rather than raising their weapons, they slip away. It appears they want to avoid you as much as you want to avoid them.
You find the area around the beacon to be rather empty. This might be a good place to take a break and relax.
TEXT_NEBULA_EMPTY_COALITION: No ships can be found in this nebula, a surprisingly unexpected outcome in this dangerous sector.
This nebula beacon is void of any ships, thankfully including Coalition ones.
The empty nebula here is far more concerning than relieving, but no ships approach from the clouds.
EMPTY_SPIDER: A Militia squadron is clearing out several civilian vessels from the beacon. They attempt to do the same to you, but when you show your ID they leave you alone.
An abandoned station has been left behind at this beacon. You briefly consider scrapping it until you realize their automated defense system is still online. Best to ignore it...
The spider infestation has done a good number on this sector. Most of the civilians have already evacuated, leaving much of the sector empty, such as this beacon.
A refugee ship flies past. You're cautious, wondering if they might be infested, but the ship makes no attempt to contact you and jumps away.
EMPTY_LANIUS: You pass a civilian ship that warns of the nearby Lanius. "One of them attacked a civilian transport and started to melt their hull. But then the weirdest thing happened... another metal ship actually fired on its companion until it backed off." Apparently there are disagreements among the Lanius about what should be salvaged.
A few Lanius military ships are settled nearby, but they refuse all hails. Not wanting to mess with so many deadly ships at once, you leave them alone.
The ruins of an ancient Lanius settlement drift nearby, but you don't risk scrapping it for fear of angering any potential Lanius witnesses.

The raiding of this sector during the Lanius hibernation made this sector a massive site of traffic, but after the Lanius awoke and began attack civilians with reckless abandon, the number of visitors plummeted and the sector returned to its original state of relative obscurity.
EMPTY_AUG: Despite the usual clusters of ruins or Lanius you expect to find here, this beacon holds nothing more than a break from combat.
A few wrecks float nearby, but they've been picked completely dry. These ancient beings must have been prolific builders to have left so much behind...
EMPTY_ABANDONED: The charts indicate this was the location of a small skirmish over a military facility on a nearby moon. Oddly, scans pick up no signs of debris from either the battle or the station. Yet another area sucked dry by scavengers.
Scans show no signs of any ships or settlements nearby. You have no way of knowing if the area was always uninhabited or if it was simply erased by scavengers.

You question a local settlement and they describe a fleet of metal ships wordlessly collecting all of the abandoned metal and debris in the area. When they approached important satellites, the settlements fired a few ASB warning shots. The Lanius moved on despite clearly having the firepower to overwhelm the settlements.

A few refugee ships are preparing for the long journey to another sector. They explain how a number of Lanius military ships surrounded them and began to hack their FTL drives. Fortunately the Lanius moved on after briefly scanning the civilian ships, leaving them more than a little shaken up.

You pass a civilian ship that warns of the nearby Lanius. "One of them attacked a civilian transport and started to melt their fracking hull. But then the weirdest thing happened... another metal ship actually fired on its companion until it backed off." Apparently there are disagreements among the Lanius about what should be salvaged.

You come across a human civilian ship preparing to leave the sector. They message you, "We're getting out of here! There was some cult rambling about the spreading of the disease, Humanitis. They forcefully boarded our ship and tried to open all of our airlocks, shouting, "Be purged!" Is nowhere safe anymore?"
This beacon is void of Lanius, Ghosts, pirates, or any other ship for that matter.
The charred remains of a civilian settlement suggests either recent pirate activity or a long ago battle with presumably Rebel forces. Either way, the beacon is now empty.
EMPTY_ORIGINS: Around you are the remains of a long-abandoned Crystalline society. You wish you could have seen what this sector was like before the Cultist invasion...
No ships are in view. You suppose this is how the Crystalline people would have preferred their sector stayed...
This beacon has not yet been touched by the swarms of invasive cultists. It should serve as a well earned break.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_VORTIGON: As you approach Vortigon, he begins to laugh menacingly. Uncertain, you back slowly out of the room and close the door behind you.
Vortigon is busy contemplating if he should change the color of his robes.
Vortigon brags about how cool his name is, and insults your 'pathetic' name. According to him, the name's length is what matters most.
Vortigon hopes that the crew of other Federation ships have more style and class than yours.
Vortigon appears to be under-way with some sort of strange ritual. As long as he isn't summoning any demons, you're ok with it.
Vortigon wonders what other lifeforms he might be able to convert into his cult now that he has left the Crystalline Homeworlds.
Vortigon makes it clear time and time again that he finds you disgusting. Why did we let this guy onto the ship?
Vortigon is busy cooking some sort of strange stew made with the blood of virgins.
Vortigon briefly mentions something about a rival cult, whose name sounds something similar to 'Mar', whose been stealing their recruits for some time. He doesn't sound very happy about it.
Vortigon never wants to see another damn teal ship ever again. Something about some 'Elder Cult', but he won't say anything more.
Vortigon hates being slow. He also hates tripping over his cloak. Come to think of it, he seems to hate a lot of things.
Vortigon wants to meet the Zoltan Minister some day. He thinks the Zoltan race would make an excellent addition to his cult.
Vortigon is busy writing another chapter for the Ember Holy Texts.
Vortigon requests that you make it mandatory for all crew members to memorize his scripture. You refuse.
Vortigon randomly quotes a verse from his holy texts, and then tries to explain the significance behind it.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_RUWEN: You question Ruwen about his seemingly routine early morning stretches. "Well, it's no secret that cryosleep does anything but wonders to your body! Spend a couple decades in a chamber and, well... well I don't quite remember how you foreigners say it. Rigid as a wooden plank?"
You find Ruwen redoing the coat of golden paint over his body. You aren't actually sure what color of crystal Ruwen is underneath, but you're also uncertain if it's rude to ask.

Ruwen runs you through various common phrases in his language, but most are lost on you. It's almost like someone just stuck a bunch of syllables together with no rhyme or reason and called it an alien language!

You're impressed to find Ruwen tinkering with a couple devices on the ship, trying to improve their efficiency or repair damage from combat, though you'll have to get used to his foreign expletives whenever something goes wrong.
Ruwen's surprised how little Crystalline culture has evolved since he was freed from cryosleep. He supposes a century or two of complete isolation would do that to a society though.
You find Ruwen's room decorated by a number of oddities, personal reminders of his homeland. Several of them seem to be effigies of Dianesh, the empress. You don't ask him about it.

Ruwen plucks a golden shard from his arm and hands it to you. "In our tradition, this is symbolic for a wish of good health and protection. Should danger approach, you may plunge this into the throat of your enemies."

Ruwen still has so many places he wishes to visit someday. The Dynasty, for both its art and its military prowess, the Shells to witness the extent of their scientific advancement, and the Free Mantis because they talk funny.

Ruwen struggles with addressing different species properly. He once got himself into a life threatening situation after he took a Slug's advice and called a Mantis Suzerain a '5-eyed corpse humper'. "I see now why everyone warns me never to trust a Slug."

You find Ruwen carrying a box marked 'fragile' from the cargo bay into his quarters - something he brought aboard when he first joined your crew. "This, my friend, is Ryapel. It's the chemical stimulant we Crystals use to accelerate geode growth. Be very careful around it, it can cause some... unpleasant side effects to non-crystal biology."

Ruwen admires the colorful culture of the Mantis. "It's truly a shame that these insectoids are so hostile. My people do not practice any forms of dancing, and I would have loved to learn from them were it not that they would certainly harvest my organs at the first opportunity."

Ruwen shares with the crew an ancient Crystal legend of a sacred vault built within the caverns of the perilous world of Alcyrea. Though travel to Alcyrea was forbidden by the Empire, with their secret homeworlds now abandoned Ruwen wonders if someday someone might finally put the myth to the test.

It seems Ruwen is still troubled by that one time he called you an 'alien'. "I am truly, so terribly sorry. It's so unlike me, I... it just tears me up inside!" You tell him not to worry about it, but it doesn't seem to soothe him much.

Ruwen's always been one for adventure. Before his job as the ambassador he was eager to sign up to join the crew of a new settlement on the rim of the Rock-Crystal Empire. Then, you know, cryosleep happened and he woke up several centuries later.

Ruwen remarks on the incredible dramatic timing at which Renegades always seem to arrive just in time whenever something important is happening. The same thing happened to him, when his station was near destruction and the Federation Hero saved him just in time.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_DIANESH: Out of curiosity, you inquire just how the Elders scrubbed all traces of the Crystals so efficiently. Dianesh laughs. "It's a common misconception among foreigners that the Crystals and Rockmen lived closely throughout all of the Rock-Crystal Empire. Our two civilizations were spread apart by the length of several systems, and we Crystals have always been isolationists. The Elders didn't have to try very hard to chase us away because we were barely here to begin with."

Dianesh, at your request, explains why the Empire is... well, an Empire. "The adoption of the imperial title stems all the way back to the Rock-Crystal Empire. Even after the isolation of our people, we maintained and regulated a number of colonies and outer territories in what you usually refer to as dead space. It's a miracle it took you foreigners so long to find us."

"You'd be surprised to find much of the history of our people is as mysterious and lost to us as it is to you. It seems there was some kind of extinction level event in the past, something that wiped the entire origins of our people and split up our species. I can only wonder what..."

You begin to ask Dianesh another question about Crystalline history, but she stops you. "Please. Try asking me about something that isn't history related. I have other things to say besides spouting exposition."
TEXT_CREW_TALK_SALT: Obyn misses the days when he could just freely go about melting Clansmen. Being a Federation hero has its perks, but it also means you can't just go committing warcrimes. Probably.
Obyn reflects on the missed opportunity to call his 2nd mate "pepper".
Obyn wonders if his prized Salt launchers would be considered illegal by the Federation if they find out about them. He begs you never to tell anyone.
"Ever notice how the Clansmen change their accent with nearly every bit of dialogue? It's kinda creepy..."

Obyn might be big, rough, and violent, but he has a soft spot for poetry. His latest work is simply titled "I'd rip the eyes out of a hatchling's head and eat them with chopsticks for you." How romantic?
Obyn isn't sure if he hates Rebels or Slugs more. His character arc hasn't included Rebels until this point, but it just seems like everyone hates Rebels instinctually except the Rebels themselves.
Obyn is ashamed of both the Rock and Crystalline societies. He doesn't want to get into the specifics though, because politics and such.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_SYLVAN: You inquire why Sylvan persistently calls you stranger instead of your real name. Sylvan explains he's trying to avoid what he refers to as an 'immersion break'.
You ask Sylvan if he sells to anyone - even Rebels. Sylvan says yes, but a sly smirk suggests his other clients might not get the same preferential treatment as you.
Sylvan won't elaborate on his encounters with other Renegades, nor even the possibilities with encounters with himself. Strange, considering he normally has so many stories to tell.

You can't find Sylvan anywhere on the ship, but you suspect he might be in his quarters. Unfortunately, you wouldn't dare step foot in that room even with his permission. Some things you simply aren't meant to see.

For a brief moment you catch Sylvan leaving his quarters and spot a strangely shaped obloid object on the floor. Sylvan eyes you, and merely says "Don't assssk quesstions you don't want the anssswer to, sssstranger."

Sylvan frequently amuses the other crew with fantastical stories of mythical beasts, hidden sectors, and elusive mercenaries. You ask him about the authenticity of these stories, and he admits most of them are made up. "Ssssometimesss, ssstranger, a made up ssstory isss easier to grassssp than the truth."
You find Sylvan smoking on the bridge, away from the rest of the crew. It's strange to see him doing so, but at least he has the courtesy to do it in private.
Though you wouldn't dare enter, you can hear Sylvan speaking inside the ship restroom. Sounds like he's reciting different ways of saying "sssstranger."
"Sssstranger, have you ever heard the tale of Darth Plagueis the Wisssse? No? Ahhh too bad. What'ssss wrong, expecting ssssomething elssse?"

"Jussst ssso you know Ssstranger, you're my favorite ssstranger of all the ssstrangers I've ever had the pleasure or displeasure of meeting!" You think that's a compliment, but you aren't entirely sure.
You notice Sylvan walking around the ship without his signature outfit on. It seems so out of place, but considering most Slugs don't wear clothes at all, you suppose this would be normal to most.
You notice Sylvan's been stealing salt packets from the cafeteria. You feel like you should confront him or at least ask him what he's doing with all of them, but you know better.
Sylvan pulls you aside and hands you a small revolver with a pack of bullets crafted from fine silver. He warns: "Ussse thisss only in casssse of emergency, ssstranger."
You question Sylvan why he dress the way he does. He claims he stole it from another fellow, a human, during his era as a pirate. It's also where he adopted his signature "ssstranger" tik.
You find it strange Sylvan paints his ship like a pirate yet doesn't fly a pirate flag. According to him, he once did, but he's since scrubbed it away as well as all the memories attached to it.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_REAPER: Dessius reads you a few lines from a poem he wrote. Halfway through he starts crying, and it's clear its a very emotional piece to him. It's just a shame you'll never know why, because you forgot to bring your translator and have no idea what the poem says.

You ask Dessius why the Ghosts all speak so... fancy. "Ah, the answer is most simple. Have you ever heard a Mantis, those violent insectoids, and their choppy barbaric language? Well to themselves it must sound brilliant and smooth! But to us, it sounds imbecilic. Well, much a same effect occurs on your translators with our static."
You finally work up the courage to ask Dessius how Ghost anatomy works, but he just breaks out laughing. "AHAHAHAHAHHAHAHAHAHAHAHAH, my friend don't be silly!" and floats away.
Dessius sometimes wonders what he must look like to people who haven't a clue what the Ghosts are. A floating set of armor surrounded by some pink gas isn't a very usual sight.
Dessius wonders what a 'samurai' is, and why he keeps seeing people compare him to one.

Dessius humors the silly names that explorers and translators have given the Ghosts and their various titles. A better translation of 'Prime Reaper' would be Eldane Prodalccius. But where's the fun in that?

Dessius comes from a long line of long-named Ghosts. The Dynasty has only had 16 Prime Reapers in its time, and Dessius's bloodline has been in charge since the 7th Reaper. A Ghost will usually divide 10 to 12 times before they finally dissipate, which can make choosing an heir difficult.

Dessius has little worries about the seemingly problematic overpopulation issues that the Dynasty experiences. "Every year thousands of the most devoted zealots line up for their ceremonious plunging into the heart of the nebula to become one with the cosmos. It's wide scale population control without my own fingers ever once needing lifting."

Dessius confesses that his full name is actually "Anglicus Dessius Probission-Taledemy." For the longest time he assumed he had the longest name around, until he heard word of some Rockman cult leader who rivaled even him.

Dessius worries greatly about CICA's Auto invasion and the sphere of influence that the troublesome AI is slowly growing. You try to explain CICA isn't actually sentient, just controlled by Vance, but Dessius won't listen.
"Have you ever laid sight upon a ship such as the Dreadnaught from earlier? Nay, neither have I. Mine conscience struggles to comprehend what horrors might lie in the devilish mind of Vance."

"Stay at my side, friend, and the swift strike of my sword shall prove the setting sun that none before us shall last lest they fall to their knees and cry the holy words of mercy which appease us!" You aren't even sure if you know what that means, but it sounds endearing.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_ANOINTED: The Anointed promises they are not a cult leader. They advise you not to ask about it any further.
The Anointed informs you that "The Anointed" is their real name that they were given at birth. It's only pure coincidence that they ended up where they are now.
The Anointed advises you avoid making any racist allusions about the Lanius or Ancient hierarchies.
The Anointed repeatedly reminds you to always capitalize the "The" at the start of their name.
The Anointed is very picky about what scrap they'll eat. You can't understand caring when you're already eating space trash, but to each his own.
The Anointed swallows a massive chunk of scrap metal right in front of you, then walks away. You aren't sure if you just walked in at a bad time or if they were trying to make a point.
The Anointed appreciates you saving them, and offers you a small trinket made out of its own body matter. You warily accept it, and put it in the farthest corner of your room that you can.
The Anointed shares a story of when they ate an entire Dynasty warship before they became the leader of the Augmented. You're glad to have her on your side.
The Anointed calls dibs on everything in the cargo bay, should the mission be abandoned.
The Anointed is enjoying a nice glass of liquid magma in their quarters. You decide not to intrude on them.
The Anointed is busy sharpening their blades. They discourage you come any closer until the process is finished.
You find yourself warning the Anointed about eating the fuel cells for the 30th time since they joined your crew after you catch them in the act yet again.
The Anointed is thinking of new synonyms to describe itself, and finds the thesaurus to be largely unhelpful.
The Anointed isn't sure how to remove the lights stuck along its body, or how they got there in the first place.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_EATER: The Beacon Eater once met the leader of a second swarm somewhere long long ago. Someday they'll meet again, and probably kill each other.
The Beacon Eater has gone by many nicknames, but his all time favorite is "baconator."

The Beacon Eater has trapped himself accidentally at many a beacon before. Fortunately, the Lanius move around so much, it's not too long until they find him again. The longest he's ever been stranded was a year, no big deal.
The Beacon Eater's diet is insatiable. It's a high price, but a worthy one when it means he gets to look so damn cool.
The Beacon Eater explains the process of designing his own form. The stage it struggled the most over was the eyes. There was over 20 options at one point!
The Beacon Eater does not exclusively eat beacons, contrary to what his name suggests. Sometimes he eats a ship or two instead.
TEXT_CREW_TALK_WITHER: Wither is frustrated that half of the lines mentioning him say "Wither" and the other half say "Aenwithe".
Wither promises you that if his name was to be an easter egg, the guy it refers to is very cool. You have no idea what that means.
Wither asks you what version number we're on. You're confused, but he seems to realize something and apologizes, then leaves the room.
"Wouldn't it be funny," begins Wither, "If there was a super secret ending where Slugs take over the galaxy? Hah, not like that exists..."
Wither misses Larry. When you ask who Larry is, he mumbles something about Slug popcorn, Mantis Bishops trying to breathe, and the Great Eye.
Wither will never forgive the Augmented for what they did to his fleet. At least, not until you start a new run and do the quest all over again.
Wither complains about the rendering time for 1080p videos to render. The things that this guy says will forever be a mystery to you...
"I wonder what Wither thinks when he reads these. Assuming he reads them, of course." You aren't sure how to respond, considering you thought HE was Wither.
Wither complains about the intricacies of time travel and the danger of paradoxes. He's already destroyed a couple realities because he accidentally said hello to himself.
Wither thinks he'll become a youtuber in some alternate timeline. You nod your head, though you have no idea what youtube is.
Wither encourages using his ability to race him against the other crew. Not that it's practical, but it is fun for a couple seconds.
Wither wonders why the corpses disappear when crew die. If they're being taken, then for what purpose...?

Wither encourages you to join the Discord. You don't know what a Discord is, but if you did, the invite link would probably be on the Subset forums, under the Mod category, on the Multiverse page. Not that you would know.
Wither claims he once dared utter the phrase "MLG Pro." Even you hate the sound of that, and you don't even know what it means.
Wither apologizes if all of his dialogue goes over your head. You just aren't cultured enough to understand it.
Wither wants you to promise never to press the Panic Button, ever, under any circumstances. If you don't know what this means yet, you will eventually.

TIPS_LIST: Tip: You can press the "toggle button" on the top left side of your screen to change the mode of your toggle or amp equipment at any point - even in battle! It'll cost a drone-part to redeploy drones however.
Tip: The on-board lab can be accessed in the storage menu and can upgrade individual species or even subtypes when upgraded. You can install the lab for free with an upgraded Medbay!
Tip: You don't need items equipped for them to trigger blue options! If you think something might be useful, hang on to it for the future!
Tip: Hostile Autos, Hazards, or Zoltan Shielded enemies will never spawn in sector 1. However, make sure you can handle taking down a harder elite ship by the time you reach the exit!
Tip: Sector 6 and 7 will always be a unique sector. If you're hunting for unlocks for unique crew, make sure you can make it all the way there!

Tip: You may encounter more important Quests or locations with a [!] marker on your journeys. Sectors that contain this label in their name are unique, and Quests that have [!] cannot be overtaken by the Rebel fleet as long as they are active on the beacon!

Tip: Hostile stores might not always be immediately willing to trade with you. See what kind of store it is and try to bring crew for blue options if you can! Also remember, attacking stores won't make them want to sell to you!

Tip: Nearly all stores will always spawn with a section labeled "Essential Systems", where systems like Shields, Weapons, Oxygen, etc will be sold separately from regular systems. If you don't have Shields or Oxygen installed, they will always be available!
Tip: On the bottom right side of the enemy box some enemies will have special icons you can hover over to find out about special characterstics of that fight.
Tip: Later sectors will have a higher and higher chance to spawn random boss enemies called Renegade Cruisers. They will sometimes drop special loot unique to them if you manage to defeat them!
Tip: Read the event text! There are many new events and interactions in Multiverse different from Vanilla, and important details in events can be the secret to winning!

Tip: The Traveling Merchant will appear randomly but always spawns in sectors 1 and 8. Unless you choose to make him mad, he'll always present an opportunity to trade or sell resources. Sometimes he'll even tell you a story!

Tip: Keep an eye out for enemies with a "high threat level" indicator. This means they're a boss enemy! Across all runs their systems, crew, and weapons will remain consistent except for their Shields, which will still scale with sector.

Tip: Unique sectors will often have a loot transport encounter which will try to run if you choose to fight it. If you can crew kill, the ship will drop a special loot item that's an upgraded version of a regular weapon.

Tip: Unique sectors will often have a Trapper or Minelayer encounter. These enemies are optional and can be deadly, but will drop a Mine Launcher when defeated. Mine Launchers can be used as weapons or to delay the fleet!

Tip: Not all storage interactions can be performed using the storage button. Sometimes they will require a storage check in an event. Visiting stores, ignoring events, or revisiting old beacons will usually provide these opportunities!

Tip: You may sometimes stumble across special ruin beacons, which will appear unmarked on the map on most runs. Interacting with these ruins will sometimes provide you with special "Aether Tech", strong equipment that also provides new internal upgrade opportunities.

Tip: Some ships start with augments marked with [X], meaning they're external versions of existing internal upgrades. You can use these to install the internal upgrade for free, or keep them external - either to bypass any mutually exclusive upgrades they might have, or to stack effects further than normal.
Tip: Make sure you read the stats of the weapons and drones you find in stores carefully! Many weapons are different than their Vanilla counterparts and may not be what you expect.
Tip: Not every ship is made equal. Some are very strong, while others very weak. There's a large variety of playstyles and different starting advantages to try out as you unlock more and more ships!

Tip: Before every sector you will get an Atlas menu that provides additional information. If you find it overwhelming, don't worry about it for now. However, the information here can be very useful to finding potential unlocks if there are any!

Tip: Not all that glitters is gold. And in that same vein, not all that's blue is good. Make sure you read blue options carefully and understand the context - they aren't always beneficial, and some can even be dastardly!

Tip: Most sectors are protected by guard ships. Friendly guards usually won't bother you, but hostile guards might not be so benevolent. Blue options or bribes are good ways to get past them, but crew killing guards will always provide an item drop. Just be careful about reinforcements!

Tip: Remember that not all differences in crew of the same species are cosmetic! Most species of crew have a number of subtypes with different stats and abilities. You can always assume a subtype inherits the stats of its normal version unless its description explicitly says otherwise.

Did You Know? Orchids replenish oxygen fast enough to replace an Oxygen system if you open your doors! However, they will provide less oxygen on depressurized ships (those without Life Support installed).
Did You Know? The Travelling Merchant can sometimes offer very special and powerful trades outside of sector 1, including loot that is normally exclusive to special boss fights or events.
Did You Know? There's more than one ending you can get in Multiverse! The game doesn't just end with defeating the Flagship, there's plenty more secrets to explore.
Did You Know? Kernel, Crystal, and Spore weapons have special elite variants of their regular versions. These are harder to get but also much stronger!
Did You Know? You can unlock all of the Vanilla ships, as faithful as possible to their original versions, as well as the new versions. You can find them all on page 15!

Did You Know? After your first run that gets to sector 8, you'll unlock the option to change your challenge level each run. These have many effects that can customize your run's difficulty beyond the standard hangar difficulties.

Did You Know? In the equipment grab at the start, the resources and crew items will always give the same thing. However, the weapon option will give you a choice between a basic Ion, Laser, and Missile!

TIP (Crew): Humans - Humans can perform any task acceptably, whether it be repairs, combat, or manning systems. They're great for when you need crew to manage many different tasks, or when you need some cannon fodder.
TIP (Crew): Engi - Engi are excellent repairmen, but they're terrible at fighting. Make sure you have a good fighting team to protect your Engi repairmen.
TIP (Crew): Separatist Engi - Separatists are more versatile than Harmony Engi, being a little better in combat than regular Engi but still less than most crew.
TIP (Crew): Zoltan - Zoltans are a niche race: they can extend your reactor power past the usual maximum and provide ion immunity to the system they're in. You can also make them go boom if you want.
TIP (Crew): Mantis - Mantis are some of the best fighters in the galaxy, but they can't do much in terms of repairs. Make sure you have a staff of good repairmen as backup.

TIP (Crew): Rockmen - Rockmen are great for deterring fires or boarding teams. Their large amounts of health means they can tank a lot of damage, but try not to move them around too much because of their slow movement speed.
TIP (Crew): Lost Sun Commandos - The Lost Sun have embraced the ways of fire. These well trained Rockmen excel at putting out fires but move just as slow as regular Rockmen.
TIP (Crew): Crystals - The Crystals are a very powerful, though reclusive, race. They need less oxygen and have more health, and can even generate a thick wall of crystals to trap crew.
TIP (Crew): Slugs - Slugs are tricky and deceptive. They make excellent pilots as they are completely immune to mind control.

TIP (Crew): Orchids - Orchids are very interesting aliens, capable of refilling the oxygen in their current room. The ship must have a life support system, but as long as it does, a single Orchid is able to outperform it!

TIP (Crew): Ghosts - Ghosts make great repairmen in dangerous situations, apart from Vagabond variants that are more hazardous. They are completely immune to suffocation and fires, and they can pass through doors, even if they're hacked or upgraded.
TIP (Crew): Lanius - Lanius are great for boarding or deterring boarders, as they drain oxygen from their current room. Just be careful about keeping them with your other aerobic crew.
TIP (Crew): Skills - Remember that every crew can learn certain skills. The more you have them do a certain task, the better they get at it.

TIP (Crew): Elite Crew - Most races have an elite variant. They're not easy to get but they have heavily buffed stats and sometimes even unique abilities! The easiest way to get them is to head to their Homeworld sector and look out for certain events.

TIP (Faction): Civilians - Civilians aren't the best armed, and sometimes their ships don't even have weapons! You can always kill them of course, for low yielding rewards, but usually it's better to just help them out. Plus, you'll feel better about it too.
TIP (Faction): The Militiamen - The Militia is a Civilian managed military that protects Civilian sectors when the Federation cannot. They're serious folks, but they'll usually be happy to see you.

TIP (Faction): The Federation - The Federation may be in disrepair because of the Rebellion, but it's far from gone. You're bound to encounter plenty of helpful Federation ships. Just make sure they are who they say they are.

TIP (Faction): The Rebellion - The main threat to the Federation. It's highly unlikely you haven't heard of the Rebels. Every Rebel you kill makes the Galaxy a better place, but don't abandon your morals in the process.
TIP (Faction): Pirates - Pirates use stolen ships from other factions, but with crew which varies. Make sure you can deal with the different kinds of ships they may throw at you!

TIP (Faction): Slavers - Slavers are specialized pirates who, as you could guess, deal in the Galactic slave trade. You can often times purchase crew from these ships, but not every encounter with them will be friendly.
TIP (Faction): Mercenaries - Mercenaries work many different odd jobs, and hold no allegiances. Anyone can be a client, as long as you have the scrap required.
TIP (Faction): Smugglers - To Smugglers, everything and everyone is a chance for a profit. So long as you can offer something of value to Smugglers, they will be of little threat to you.

TIP (Faction): Rebel Auto-Ships - Rebel Auto-Ships are just as deadly as their manned ships. They're very weak early on but as you travel through the sectors they will get stronger and stronger. It's impossible to crew kill them, so make sure you have enough weapons to get through their defenses.

TIP (Faction): Federation Auto-Ships - The Federation has employed the use of basic Auto-ships for providing support. They're far less advanced than the Rebel AI, but they can still provide aid when necessary.
TIP (Faction): Zoltan Auto-Ships - The Zoltan Automated Fleet patrols their sectors to keep the peace. Make sure you're following their laws whenever one is nearby and there shouldn't be any issues.

TIP (Faction): Coalition - The Coalition is an alliance between the Slugs, Mantises, Rockmen, and Leeches. Their ships mix the technologies and tactics of all four races. Make sure you're prepared for handling this threat before entering their sectors.
TIP (Faction): Engi Harmony - The Engi are controlled by a single entity known as the Harmony. As long as you stay on its good side, the Engi will greet you as a friend.
TIP (Faction): Engi Separatists - The Separatists are Engi who managed to break free of the Harmony's control. They like to travel solo and their ships will usually have very few crew on-board.
TIP (Faction): Zoltan Republic - Zoltan ships are protected by powerful Zoltan Shields, which will protect them from most of your usual defense penetrating tactics.

TIP (Faction): The Duskbringers - The Duskbringers are a radical group of Zoltan who seek out the Federation's downfall. They're on generally neutral terms with the Rebellion and are protected by powerful Zoltan shields.

TIP (Faction): Zoltan Monks - The Zoltan Monks are dedicated to non-violence, refusing to harm others. Their ships usually don't have weapons, but when they do, it's only ion. You'll find them most often in their refuge in the nebula.

TIP (Faction): Mantis Hive - The Mantis Hive is no ally of yours. Before entering Mantis sectors, always make sure you can protect yourself from boarders, and maybe consider investing in a boarding team of your own.

TIP (Faction): Mantis Suzerains - The Mantis Suzerains are the leaders of the Mantis Hive. Their ships use advanced (stolen) drone tech and boarding equipment, and are piloted by Suzerain crew, very deadly warriors.

TIP (Faction): Free Mantis - The Free Mantis are allies of the Federation. They're not very intelligent and are very extreme about their devotion to you, so just be careful that you're always friendly to them, or they'll think you're a Rebel spy and cut off your head.

TIP (Faction): The Rock Theocracy - The Rockmen are devoutly religious folks. The Rockmen Elders will tolerate your presence in their territory so long as you don't challenge their leadership or their laws.

TIP (Faction): The Lost Suns - The Federation has been backing the Lost Suns for some time now, in hopes that they will bring about the downfall of the Coalition. They're obsessed with the holy fires and will stop at nothing to destroy the Rock Elders. Just stay on their good side, and everything will be fine.

TIP (Faction): Slug Kleptocracy - It takes a species of thieves to find pride in being officially deemed a Kleptocracy. If there was ever such a race, it would be the Slugs. Trust no Slug you meet unless you have the scrap to back it, and don't be suprised when that scrap is stolen too.

TIP (Faction): The Lanius Swarm - It's sometimes surprising that the Lanius are sentient. Having just awaken from a century long hibernation, the Lanius have assimilated once again into the Galactic scene.

TIP (Faction): The Crystals - After the discovery of the Multiverse drive, it didn't take long for the Crystal Homeworlds in nearly every reality to be swarmed by pioneers. The Crystals were forced to rejoin the Galactic scene and construct new sectors.

TIP (Faction): The Ghosts - No, the ghosts are not actual paranormal spirits. The striking resemblance to the undead that this gaseous race bears is from where their nickname originates. They populate stolen ships from other factions, with slight modifications.

TIP (Ship Class): Trappers/Minelayers - These specialized ships wield only Mine Launchers. You won't encounter them as often as other ships, but if you can defeat them, you may be able to steal their weapons.
TIP (Ship Class): Strike Fighters - Strike Fighters are specialized stealth ships. They will never have shields, but usually have very strong cloaking systems and high evasion.

TIP (Ship Class): Guards - Guard ships are usually encountered at the entrance beacon to faction controlled sectors. Depending on the faction's friendliness with the Federation determines whether or not you can pass through without a fight.

TIP (Ship Class): Stations - Stations never have any evasion, meaning your shots will never miss. However, they are typically protected by advanced defensive systems and can wield impressive arsenals.

TIP (Ship Class): Transports - The Homeworlds or Coreworlds of any faction will always have a special Transport ship moving around. Capture it without damaging the cargo and you'll find specialized equipment!
TIP (Ship Class): Dropships - These ships are centralized around boarding. They will always have a teleporter and usually high level medical systems.
TIP (Ship Class): Battleships - Battleships are incredibly strong ships that can wield up to 6 different weapons at a time! You won't see them until much further into your journey.
TIP (Ship Class): Motherships - Motherships are very strong ships centred on drone tech. Their weapons are usually weaker but their onslaught of drones is nothing to laugh at.
TIP (Ship Class): Riggers - Riggers are a common class of ship that wield drone systems. They're roughly as strong as a fighter but serve more niche purposes.
TIP (Ship Class): Outriders - Outriders are roughly as strong as Scouts, but will always have upgraded piloting.
TIP (Ship Class): Shuttles - Shuttle ships are extremely small and weak, and sometimes don't even come equipped with weapons. They won't put up much of a fight.

TIP (Ship Class): Pickets - Pickets are massive ships, usually the strongest among any fleet. They're extremely well armed and protected, but luckily can't be found until you reach the final few sectors.

TIP (Ship Class): Jailers - Jailers are special ships built for the construction of prisoners. Taking these ships hostage may present you with the opportunity to rescue their prisoners for your own benefit.
TIP (Ship Class): Protectors - Protector ships have extremely advanced defenses, but mediocre weapon set-ups.
TIP (Ship Class): Skirmishers - Skirmishers are tiny versions of fighters, usually wielding similar yet weaker equipment.
TIP (Ship Class): Bombards - Bombards are tiny versions of bombers, usually wielding similar yet weaker equipment.

TIP (Ship Class): Elites - Many different factions have additional fleets of Elite class ships. They are much stronger and can pack a serious punch, but usually lead to even greater rewards when defeated.

TIP (Ship Class): MFK Aces - No regular ship can compare to the power of an MFK Ace. These are the strongest ships the Rebel fleet has to offer besides the Flagship itself. Very rarely you'll find them in the Rebel fleet, and you'll get extra rewards for killing them, which can extend to delaying the Rebel Fleet!
TIP (Ship Class): Auto-Ships - The Rebellion aren't the only faction with Automated vessels. The Federation and Zoltan fleets also consist of AI ships!
TIP (Technology): Cealaforming - Cealaforming is technology used by the Slugms and the Coalition. It involves the transportation of nebula gasses to new locations to create artificial nebula beacons.

TIP (Technology): Combat Augments - Combat Augments can be used before any fight, including the Flagship, for different effects, usually to limit enemy systems. They're guaranteed to work as long as the enemy has the system in question, but will use some reactor power of your own.
TIP (Technology): Anti-Virus - The Anti-Virus augment can come in handy when dealing with hackers or slugs who try to shut down your systems. It doesn't cost any power, either!

TIP (Technology): Magnetic Arm - The Magnetic arm isn't nearly as efficient as regular scrap recovery arms, but they work much faster. Fast enough that you might even be able to salvage additional supplies when stuck in the Rebel Fleet!
TIP (Technology): Emergency Manual - The Emergency Manual augment provides you with additional pre-fight options like crafting fuel, salvaging scrap, or detonating a massive amount of explosives!

TIP (Technology): Zoltan Deleter - It's officially considered a war crime to use this devastating beam against any race other than the Zoltans. It's perfectly fine to kill the green energy dudes though.

TIP (Technology): Conservative Weapons - Conservative weapons require no power on their own, but rather feed off of power leaks in the weapon system. This has two downsides, at least one other weapon must be powered, and they have a much longer cooldown.

TIP (Technology): Recycler Weapons - Only regular ammunition consuming weapons come in recycler form. They synthesize ammunition from worthless junk, meaning they use no missiles to fire. However, they take much longer to charge.
TIP (Weapons): Lasers - Lasers are a staple weapon of practically any ship. They're excellent for damage and penetrating defenses, and very reliable.
TIP (Weapons): Missiles - Missile weapons consume ammunition but pierce all shield layers. They're very niche weapons that can do a lot of damage, but every shot comes at a price.
TIP (Weapons): Beams - Beams never miss their target, and can hit multiple systems as well. They're extremely powerful, but struggle at taking down shields.
TIP (Weapons): Ions - Ions do no physical damage but can temporarily shut down systems.

TIP (Weapons): Bombs - Bombs pierce all shields, use ammunition, and do only system or crew damage. They're useful utilities that provide a unique strategic advantage against some ships, but cant kill most ships on their own.
TIP (Weapons): Energy Cannons - Energy cannons are a mix between ion and hull damage. This makes them extremely good at taking down shields, especially Zoltan shields.

TIP (Weapons): Pinpoint Weapons - Pinpoints are tiny Beam weapons that can only hit one room at a time. However, they can never miss and do more damage than usual Beam weapons do, as well as have a high breach chance.

TIP (Weapons): Mine Launchers - Mines can't be found in stores due to a shared hatred of them by most people. However, some specialized ships called Trappers can be found, and when defeated, will drop Mine Launcher tech that you can use. Or more likely, sell.
TIP (Weapons): Flak Cannons - Flak cannons shoot large chunks of worthless junk at the enemy ship, and are an effective way of taking down shields quickly.
TIP (Weapons): Crystal Guns - The Crystal race's specialized Crystal weapons shoot special projectiles that can pierce 1 shield each, and require no ammunition to use.
TIP (Weapons): Kernel Launchers - Kernels are the Orchid race's weapon of choice. They require missiles to use, but pierce all shields and have a chance to not consumme ammo.

TIP (Weapons): Scanner - The Scanner does no damage of any kind, but can temporarily reveal rooms. It's ineffective on most ships, but it can be useful if you have no sensors or are stuck in a nebula.
TIP (General): Surrenders - Sometimes, a special surrender event will pop up. Every faction has its own list of unique surrenders that can sometimes occur.
TIP (General): Leftover Salvage - Occasionally when a ship escapes, wreckage from the fight will be left behind that you can salvage. It won't be much, but it's better than nothing.
TIP (General): Socializing - At empty beacons you can talk with your crew! Often times it'll just be useless chit-chat, but it is a free action.
TIP (General): Reinforcements - After killing guard ships, you might find yourself being hunted by additional reinforcements later on in the sector. Be sure to watch your back!
TIP (General): Jobs - As captain of this vessel, it's your task to make sure your crew are being productive. At empty beacons you are able to assign your crew to certain tasks.

TIP (General): Minibosses - Every Homeworld or Coreworld sector has a special miniboss event. It's always optional, and sometimes requires special blue option equipment. If you can defeat the powerful ship, you'll get insane rewards and sometimes even unique equipment. Minibosses will always be the same on any run, so you can master a strategy against them.

TIP (General): Pre-fight Preparations - Before every fight you will have a few options to make repairs or create supplies. It's not efficient scrap wise, but it can be life saving in some circumstances.
TIP (General): Special Augments - Some events give special augments that have no functional purpose other than to be sold or transported to a different location.

TIP (General): Loot - Some special transport encounters drop specialized weapons or drones. They're similar to regularly occurring equipment, but with a special modifier. They can do all kinds of things, like additional lockdown or piercing Zoltan shields!

TIP (General): Federation Outposts - Most peaceful sectors can sometimes host a Federation outpost. You'll be able to see these beacons from anywhere on the map, and they will provide free supplies or repairs.

TIP (General): Homeworlds, Coreworlds, and Strongholds - Many factions have their own "unique" sector that will only ever occur once. These sectors are generally more dangerous, even the peaceful ones, but have special loot transports, elite encounters, and minibosses with massive rewards.

TIP (Last Stand): The Judges - At the Last Stand, one of three judges will always spawn. They will either evaluate your systems, crew, or weapons. Depending on what you have, you can get unique and powerful rewards that are impossible to get elsewhere.
TIP (Last Stand): The Base - If you arrive at the Federation Base before the Flagship does, you'll get a few more repairs and a small sampling of supplies.
TIP (Last Stand): Tully - Admiral Tully is a respectable man, and a well trained soldier. If you can win over his trust, maybe you can even convince him to help you personally.

TIP (Last Stand): Flagship - Just as in Universe 0, the Flagship is split into 3 stages, with an array of powerful artillery weapons. It's no less of a threat however, so make sure you're as prepared as you can be.
TIP (Last Stand): Flagship Crew - The Flagship specializes in many different humans of different professions. They'll be staffed by MFK Aces elites, soldiers, engineers, and medics!
